<a id="nc-2-affine-composition"></a>

#### 2.14. Composition in affine word coordinates

*Theorem* `NC.2/affine-composition`

Proposed module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/UnipotentFundamentalGroup`, namespace `TauCetiRoadmap.AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty.NC2`.

The affine trivialization s_0(b,x):W\_≤n→M_n(b,x) induced by the universal connection satisfies comp(s_0(x_2,x_3)(f_2),s_0(x_1,x_2)(f_1))=s_0(x_1,x_3)(f_2 f_1). Multiplication is truncated concatenation in the displayed order. For equal endpoints it is an algebra isomorphism. The associated action of a source algebra element is right multiplication in these coordinates.

**Hypotheses.**

- One affine curve, one chosen cohomology basis, and endpoints in Y(k).

**Proof.**

1. Right multiplication by f_1 defines a horizontal endomorphism of the universal connection.
2. Evaluate at its pointer and apply the unique pointed-map property. The resulting natural transformation realizes f_1 in finite-path-module.
3. Compose the natural transformations and evaluate; right multiplication gives f_2 f_1, fixing the convention without commuting the words.

**Checks.**

- With two generators and n=2, composing coordinate T_1 then T_2 gives T_2T_1, distinct from T_1T_2.
- The empty word is the identity endomorphism.

<a id="nc-2-proper-maximal-quotient"></a>

#### 2.15. Proper extendable quotient

*Theorem* `NC.2/proper-maximal-quotient`

Proposed module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/UnipotentFundamentalGroup`, namespace `TauCetiRoadmap.AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty.NC2`.

Let X be a smooth proper geometrically connected characteristic-zero curve and j:Y↪X a nonempty affine open containing b. Restriction C_dR(X)→C_dR(Y) is fully faithful. The canonical pointed map 𝒜_n(Y)→j\*𝒜_n(X) is surjective, and its target is the maximal length-n pointed quotient extending to an integrable connection on all of X with no logarithmic poles. Every horizontal map from 𝒜_n(Y) to a restricted length-n connection from X factors uniquely through it. The proper length graded pieces are quotients of V_X^⊗i, not free tensor powers in general.

**Hypotheses.**

- Smooth proper X, rational basepoint in nonempty affine Y, characteristic zero.

**Proof.**

1. Prove restriction full faithfulness in characteristic zero on the horizontal Hom connection: a rational horizontal section with a pole of maximal order r&gt;0 has derivative of order r+1, while a regular connection matrix contributes at most order r. The leading pole coefficient cannot cancel, so the section extends across each removed smooth point. Apply this to Hom of two regular connections.
2. Before using the image, extend any subconnection of a restricted regular connection: across a removed smooth point, saturate its generic subspace inside the regular bundle over the local DVR. The intersection is stable under the connection because both the generic subspace and the ambient regular bundle are stable; saturation makes the submodule and quotient locally free on a curve. It is unipotent by subquotient closure. The image of the universal map thus extends to X and contains the pointer. Universal pointed evaluation on X supplies its retraction from 𝒜_n(X); uniqueness makes the composite the identity, forcing surjectivity.
3. For each extendable target, universal pointed evaluation on X gives the unique factorization. Extendable quotients are exactly the ones with zero residues in their canonical logarithmic extension.

**Checks.**

- For X=P¹, 𝒜_n(X) is the unit for all n, even though puncturing creates nontrivial universal word generators.
- For a positive-genus proper curve the degree-two cup-product relation prevents the proper algebra from being the free tensor algebra.

**Needs.**

- [`NC.2/affine-universality`](#nc-2-affine-universality) Kim’s affine universal property
- [`NC.2/universal-object-existence`](#nc-2-universal-object-existence) Existence of universal length objects
- `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`

**Used by.** [`NC.2/hadian-filtration`](#nc-2-hadian-filtration); [`NC.2/word-path-bridge`](#nc-2-word-path-bridge); [`NC.4/iterated-coordinates`](#nc-4-iterated-coordinates); [`NC.4/residue-disc-density`](#nc-4-residue-disc-density).

**Sources.**

- [Kim09](#src-kim09), Section 1, p. 111: Uses full faithfulness of restriction for unipotent connections.

<a id="nc-2-filtered-path"></a>

#### 2.16. Hodge filtered path fibres

*Definition* `NC.2/filtered-path`

Proposed module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/UnipotentFundamentalGroup`, namespace `TauCetiRoadmap.AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty.NC2`.

A filtered unipotent connection is an integrable connection E with a finite, exhaustive, separated descending filtration F^iE by subbundles, satisfying ∇F^iE⊆F^(i−1)E⊗Ω¹ (or Ω¹(log D) on the canonical extension of an open curve). For 𝒜_n(b), filter its constant kernel I^n/I^(n+1) by the quotient filtration from V_dR^⊗n, where V_dR=H^1_dR∨ has the dual Hodge filtration. The Hodge filtered path fibre at x is x\*𝒜_n(b) with the resulting filtration. On the dual coordinate ring this induces the multiplicative filtration and F^0 path subtorsor. The existence and uniqueness of the geometric filtration are the theorem hadian-filtration, not fields assumed in this definition.

**Hypotheses.**

- Smooth proper curve or the canonical logarithmic extension to its smooth proper compactification.
- Dual filtration convention: F^i(V∨) annihilates F^(1−i)V.
- General filtered modules and Hodge filtrations are imported from p-adic Hodge theory.

**Construction.**

1. Specify the filtration and transversality on the imported connection; the subbundle condition makes fibre restriction exact.
2. Use the augmentation length grades and the quotient of the tensor Hodge filtration for the universal kernels.
3. Restrict the actual filtered bundles at endpoints; dualize to filtered coordinate objects and check tensor/coalgebra compatibility using the universal construction.

**API.**

- `FilteredPathFiber.filtration` (projection): For each integer i the subspace F^i in the endpoint fibre.
- `FilteredPathFiber.graded` (data): The associated length grade has the quotient tensor Hodge filtration.
- `FilteredPathFiber.unit` (simp): The universal pointer at b lies in F^0.
- `FilteredPathFiber.dual` (compatibility): Dualization uses annihilators of F^(1−i), and comparison maps are strict filtered maps.
- `FilteredPathFiber.truncate` (functoriality): Length transition maps preserve the Hodge filtration.

- `filtered_unit` (degenerate): The filtered unit is k for i≤0 and zero for i&gt;0.

- `filtered_augmentation_quotient` (characterisation): A filtered quotient of a finite path fibre carries the image filtration, rather than an arbitrary splitting filtration.

**Checks.**

- At length zero the unit filtration is k in degrees i≤0 and zero for i&gt;0.
- Frobenius is not required to preserve the Hodge filtration.

<a id="nc-2-filtered-extension"></a>

#### 2.17. Filtered extension classification

*Theorem* `NC.2/filtered-extension`

Proposed module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/UnipotentFundamentalGroup`, namespace `TauCetiRoadmap.AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty.NC2`.

For filtered integrable connections E,F on a smooth proper curve X, with logarithmic poles along a reduced divisor D when present, extensions that are strict on filtered bundles are classified by H¹ of the two-term complex F^0 Hom(E,F)→F^(−1) Hom(E,F)⊗Ω¹_X(log D). The differential is the induced Hom connection. Forgetting the filtration is induced by inclusion into the full logarithmic de Rham complex. This is a classification of extension classes; uniqueness of a class does not by itself imply equality of filtrations on a fixed underlying bundle.

**Hypotheses.**

- Finite exhaustive separated subbundle filtrations and Griffiths transversality.
- Proper X and logarithmic canonical extensions if D is nonempty.

**Proof.**

1. Choose local filtered splittings, which exist for strict extensions of vector bundles. Their differences form a Čech 1-cochain in F^0 Hom; connection off-diagonal terms form a 0-cochain in Ω¹(log D)⊗F^(−1) Hom.
2. The cocycle and horizontality equations are precisely the total degree-one hypercohomology cocycle condition. Changes of filtered splitting give coboundaries.
3. Reconstruct the extension from such a cocycle and check the inverse construction; the forgetful map is the inclusion of complexes.

**Checks.**

- For D empty and E=F=unit with trivial filtration, the displayed filtered complex has O_X→Ω¹_X, the usual de Rham extension complex.
- Changing a filtered splitting changes the cocycle by a coboundary.

**Needs.**

- [`NC.2/filtered-path`](#nc-2-filtered-path) Hodge filtered path fibres
- `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2`

**Used by.** [`NC.2/hadian-filtration`](#nc-2-hadian-filtration).

**Sources.**

- [Had10](#src-had10), Thesis §2.2, Proposition 2.2.3 and proof, p. 29; Lemma 2.2.1, p. 27: Classifies strict filtered extensions by the first hypercohomology of the two-term filtered Hom complex, using local filtered splittings. Lemma 2.2.1 supplies the unfiltered de Rham complex calculation.
- [BD2m](#src-bd2m), Proposition 6.1, p. 30; Remark 5, p. 31 of the author manuscript: States the extension classification and distinguishes class uniqueness from a rigidified filtration.

<a id="nc-2-hadian-filtration"></a>

#### 2.18. Hadian’s universal Hodge filtration

*Theorem* `NC.2/hadian-filtration`

Proposed module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/UnipotentFundamentalGroup`, namespace `TauCetiRoadmap.AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty.NC2`.

For a pointed smooth proper curve X/k in characteristic zero, the universal connection 𝒜_n(b) has a unique Hodge filtration by subbundles, rigidified at b, such that Griffiths transversality holds, the sequence V_dR^⊗n⊗O_X→𝒜_n(b)→𝒜\_(n−1)(b)→0 induces the specified quotient tensor filtration on the kernel and the inductively specified filtration on the quotient, and 1_b∈F^0. Start with the unit filtration at n=0. Equivalently construct the canonical logarithmic universal connection on a nonempty affine Y⊂X, rigidify it by the pointer, and pass to the maximal no-pole quotient. Filtered quotients inherit the image filtration. The affine bundle without its compactification does not satisfy a uniqueness theorem.

**Hypotheses.**

- Smooth proper X, characteristic zero, rational b; n≥1.
- On an auxiliary affine open use its canonical logarithmic extension to X, including nilpotent residues; impose the basepoint pointer normalization.

**Proof.**

1. Use filtered-extension to lift the underlying universal extension class with the prescribed graded filtration. Hadian’s filtered Ext calculation gives the lift and uniqueness of its class on the proper compactification.
2. Rigidify the filtered universal extension at the pointed fibre. A pointed connection automorphism is identity by universal-pointed, turning the isomorphism-class result into uniqueness for the normalized universal object.
3. For proper X use proper-maximal-quotient and the filtered quotient construction. The kernel is a quotient of the tensor grade; it is not assumed to be the entire tensor power.

**Checks.**

- For n=0, the pointer 1 lies in the usual F^0 of the unit.
- At n=1 for genus g proper X, the V_dR part has filtration F^0=ann H^0(X,Ω¹), of dimension g.
- The same uniqueness assertion on an affine bundle alone is excluded.

**Needs.**

- [`NC.2/filtered-path`](#nc-2-filtered-path) Hodge filtered path fibres

- [`NC.2/universal-pointed`](#nc-2-universal-pointed) Universal pointed object
- [`NC.2/proper-maximal-quotient`](#nc-2-proper-maximal-quotient) Proper extendable quotient

### Frobenius, horizontal continuation and the crystalline comparison

<a id="nc-2-rigid-fibre"></a>

#### 2.19. Residue-disc fibre

*Construction* `NC.2/rigid-fibre`

Proposed module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/UnipotentFundamentalGroup`, namespace `TauCetiRoadmap.AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty.NC2`.

For a unipotent overconvergent isocrystal E and a rational special-fibre point z, define ω_z(E) as the horizontal sections of E on the residue disc \]z\[. For any lift x∈\]z\[(K_0), evaluation is a canonical tensor-natural isomorphism ω_z(E)≅E_x. For x,y in the same disc, define T\_(x→y)=ev_y∘ev_x^−1. It composes, is horizontal, respects tensor products and the unit, and is independent of any chosen coordinate on the disc. These are local fibre identifications; they do not identify different discs until canonical-frobenius-path is proved.

**Hypotheses.**

- Smooth good-reduction curve and unipotent overconvergent connection.
- Endpoints rational over K_0; otherwise extend the unramified coefficient field first.

**Construction.**

1. Import the isocrystal evaluation at a point from RD.3 and represent it on the residue disc by horizontal sections.
2. Use the unipotent filtration and recursively solve the connection using local primitives on the disc; uniqueness with a prescribed value proves evaluation is an isomorphism.
3. Tensor naturality and composition follow from uniqueness, not from a choice of basis.

**API.**

- `RigidHorizontalFiber.horizontal` (data): The kernel of the connection on disc sections, as a coefficient-field vector space.
- `RigidHorizontalFiber.eval` (equivalence): Evaluation at a lift is a tensor-natural linear isomorphism.
- `RigidHorizontalFiber.transport` (constructor): Transport from x to y is evaluation at y after inverse evaluation at x.
- `RigidHorizontalFiber.transport_comp` (simp): T\_(y→z)∘T\_(x→y)=T\_(x→z).
- `RigidHorizontalFiber.tensor` (compatibility): Evaluation and transport commute with the tensor structure and send the unit to one.

**Unit tests.**

- `rigid_unit` (degenerate): Horizontal sections of the trivial rank-one connection are the coefficient constants.
- `rigid_same_endpoint` (computation): Transport from x to itself is identity.
- `rigid_nilpotent_transport` (computation): For a constant nilpotent matrix N with N²=0 in d−Ndt, transport is 1+(y−x)N and therefore has the positive sign.

**Checks.**

- For the trivial connection the horizontal sections are the constants and every evaluation is identity.
- For d−Ndt on a disc with N²=0, transport x→y is 1+(y−x)N.

**Uses.**

- BDMTV Theorem 5.3: Matches rigid and de Rham endpoint fibres.
- BDMTV equation (42): Conjugates Frobenius from fixed lifts to arbitrary endpoints.

<a id="nc-2-rigid-frobenius-equivalence"></a>

#### 2.20. Frobenius pullback equivalence

*Theorem* `NC.2/rigid-frobenius-equivalence`

Proposed module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/UnipotentFundamentalGroup`, namespace `TauCetiRoadmap.AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty.NC2`.

On the unipotent isocrystal category of a smooth curve over F_q with the stated good-reduction compactification, pullback by the q-power Frobenius is a K_0-linear tensor autoequivalence. For p-power Frobenius before iteration it is σ-semilinear. Unit and endpoint fibre identifications give actions on tensor paths and all finite universal path modules. Frobenius preserves the length filtration; preservation of the Hodge filtration is not part of the statement.

**Hypotheses.**

- Smooth special fibre descending to F_q; K_0=Frac W(F_q).
- Use the overconvergent unipotent category, not arbitrary F-isocrystals defined by choosing a matrix.

**Proof.**

1. Use CLS Proposition 2.4.2. Its induction on unipotent length reduces full faithfulness to H^0 and essential surjectivity of extensions to H^1, on which Frobenius is invertible.
2. Pullback is tensor and preserves the unit; q-power iteration removes coefficient semilinearity over K_0.
3. Transport its functor and fibre identifications through tensor-paths and finite-path-module.

**Checks.**

- Frobenius pullback of the unit is the unit.
- A p-power map over W(F_q)\[1/p\] is semilinear unless its coefficient Frobenius has been iterated q times appropriately.

<a id="nc-2-frobenius-normalization"></a>

#### 2.21. Normalized universal Frobenius

*Theorem* `NC.2/frobenius-normalization`

Proposed module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/UnipotentFundamentalGroup`, namespace `TauCetiRoadmap.AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty.NC2`.

At a Frobenius-fixed special endpoint b_0, pullback of the universal pointed isocrystal (𝒜_n(b_0),1) is universal. There is exactly one pointed horizontal isomorphism Φ_n:F\*𝒜_n(b_0)≅𝒜_n(b_0) carrying the identified base fibre pointer to 1. It commutes with length transition maps, yields the identity on A_0, and on the graded pieces induces the quotient of the tensor powers of Frobenius on H^1_rig∨. At other lifts of the same endpoint use rigid-fibre transport to express this normalization.

**Hypotheses.**

- Good-reduction hypotheses and a q-power Frobenius fixing the special endpoint.
- The comparison of the base fibres is specified; an unnormalized horizontal isomorphism is not canonical.

**Proof.**

1. Apply the tensor autoequivalence to the universal pointed evaluation property; the endpoint identification preserves its pointer.
2. Use the unique pointed isomorphism of universal-pointed. Uniqueness forces compatibility with all transitions.
3. On the augmentation generators the map is the H^1-dual Frobenius; multiplicativity and quotient compatibility give its action on tensor graded pieces.

**Checks.**

- At length zero Φ_0 sends 1 to 1 and is identity.
- Multiplying a universal Frobenius map by a nonidentity source automorphism changes the pointer normalization and is excluded.

#### 2.22. Nonabelian Berthelot–Ogus comparison

*Comparison* `NC.2/berthelot-ogus`

Proposed module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/UnipotentFundamentalGroup`, namespace `TauCetiRoadmap.AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty.NC2`.

For a smooth proper pair (Xcal,Dcal) over W(F_q), with Dcal finite étale, and Y=Xcal_K0−Dcal_K0, analytification is a K_0-linear tensor equivalence C_dR(Y)≃C_rig(Y_0). For an integral lift x of a special endpoint, its fibre comparison ι_x is rigid-fibre evaluation. Hence the groups, tensor path schemes, universal objects and finite path modules compare canonically, with coefficient extension if needed. For x,y in one residue disc, the induced de Rham path is local parallel transport. For Dcal empty this applies to the proper curve; the affine free-word computation is not applied to the proper curve without taking its quotient.

**Hypotheses.**

- Smooth proper compactification over the unramified DVR with smooth finite étale boundary, possibly empty.
- Only unipotent connections/isocrystals.

**Proof.**

1. Apply CLS Proposition 2.4.1. Use its induction on length, identifying Hom with horizontal H^0 and extension classes with H^1 via algebraic/rigid linear comparison.
2. Compare endpoint fibres by rigid-fibre evaluation; use neutral reconstruction and tensor-isomorphism representability to pass to groups and schemes.
3. Universal pointed uniqueness gives finite-object comparison and compatibility with path composition and all length transitions.

**Checks.**

- The comparison sends the unit to the unit and the universal pointer to the universal pointer.
- On a single residue disc its endpoint comparison is exactly T\_(x→y), not a new arbitrary path choice.

#### 2.23. Frobenius on de Rham paths

*Construction* `NC.2/path-frobenius`

Proposed module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/UnipotentFundamentalGroup`, namespace `TauCetiRoadmap.AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty.NC2`.

Use berthelot-ogus and the endpoint fibre comparisons to transport rigid q-Frobenius to P_dR(b,x) and to M_n^dR(b,x). If b_0,x_0 are Frobenius-fixed lifts in the same respective discs, put τ(g)=T\_(x_0→x)∘g∘T\_(b→b_0). Then φ_n(b,x)=τ∘φ_n(b_0,x_0)∘τ^−1. At the fixed lifts, φ_n(b_0,x_0) is the fibre of Φ_n under the universal evaluation isomorphism. The operators preserve length, commute with composition and the source action, and retain their coefficient semilinearity before q-iteration. They need not preserve Hodge filtration.

**Hypotheses.**

- Good-reduction pair, integral rational endpoints in the good open, and specified Frobenius-fixed lifts when this coordinate formula is used.

**Construction.**

1. Define the action through the actual rigid tensor functor and endpoint identifications, then transfer it through berthelot-ogus.
2. Use universal-frobenius-normalization and finite-path-module evaluation to identify the fixed-lift operator.
3. Change lifts by rigid-fibre transport; naturality gives the conjugation formula and its compatibility with length/composition.

**API.**

- `PathFrobenius.fixedLift` (data): The fixed-lift finite path operator obtained from Φ_n.
- `PathFrobenius.transport` (constructor): Transport the fixed-lift operator by τ.
- `PathFrobenius.changeLift` (characterisation): Changing a disc lift conjugates the path operator by the corresponding two-sided transport.
- `PathFrobenius.comp` (compatibility): Frobenius of a composable pair is the composition of their Frobenius images.
- `PathFrobenius.truncate` (functoriality): The Frobenius operators commute with length transitions.

**Unit tests.**

- `frobenius_fixed_lifts` (degenerate): Identity transport leaves the fixed-lift operator unchanged.
- `frobenius_two_sided` (computation): For linear maps represented by source A and target B, τ(g)=B∘g∘A and the transported operator is τφτ^−1.
- `frobenius_conjugation_fixed` (characterisation): If φ(g)=g, then τφτ^−1 fixes τ(g); reversing one endpoint transport generally fails this equality.

**Checks.**

- At fixed lifts the conjugating transport is identity.
- Changing both endpoints gives two-sided transport in the specified order.

**Uses.**

- BDMTV Sections 5.3–5.4: Makes the Frobenius matrix at an arbitrary point intrinsic.
- NC.3: Provides geometric crystalline path data before imposing Selmer conditions.

<a id="nc-2-frobenius-lang"></a>

#### 2.24. Unipotent Frobenius Lang theorem

*Theorem* `NC.2/frobenius-lang` · planet: **Frobenius Lang theorem**

Proposed module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/UnipotentFundamentalGroup`, namespace `TauCetiRoadmap.AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty.NC2`.

Let U be a pro-unipotent rigid fundamental group of a smooth F_q curve in the stated good-reduction pair. Its q-Frobenius φ has no eigenvalue one on any positive augmentation/Lie graded piece: H^1_rig∨ has weights −1 (proper) or −1 and −2 (open), and the grades are tensor-power quotients. The Lang map L_φ:U→U, g↦g^−1φ(g), is an isomorphism of affine schemes, compatible with finite lower central quotients and scalar extension. This is not asserted to be a group homomorphism. More generally the same proof applies when φ−1 is invertible on every finite Lie graded piece.

**Hypotheses.**

- Good-reduction smooth curve over a finite field and its geometric unipotent group; characteristic-zero coefficients.
- Weight/no-eigenvalue-one hypothesis at every positive grade; a single H^1 eigenvalue statement without its tensor-grade consequence is insufficient.

**Proof.**

1. Import the rigid H^1 weights. Length-algebra bounds positive grades by tensor powers of H^1∨, so all eigenvalues have strictly negative weights and none is one.
2. Solve g^−1φ(g)=h successively in the complete augmentation algebra, where the next correction is determined by the invertible linear map φ−1 on the next grade.
3. Use the coproduct and uniqueness of this solution to show it is group-like. The construction is functorial over coefficient algebras, giving a scheme inverse rather than just a pointwise bijection.

**Checks.**

- For U=G_a and φ=a·id with a≠1, Lang is multiplication by a−1.
- For U=G_a and φ=id, Lang is zero and is not invertible, so the weight hypothesis cannot be dropped.

**Needs.**

- [`NC.2/tannakian-groups`](#nc-2-tannakian-groups) Unipotent fundamental group
- [`NC.2/length-algebra`](#nc-2-length-algebra) Completed path algebra
- [`NC.2/rigid-frobenius-equivalence`](#nc-2-rigid-frobenius-equivalence) Frobenius pullback equivalence
- `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.6/purity-smooth-proper`
- `PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology:RD.6/weights-of-h1-of-affine-curve`

**Sources.**

- [Bes00](#src-bes00), Theorem 3.1, Theorem 3.6 and Proposition 3.8, pp. 7–12: Proves Lang invertibility using the negative-weight augmentation argument.

<a id="nc-2-canonical-frobenius-path"></a>

#### 2.25. Canonical Frobenius path

*Construction* `NC.2/canonical-frobenius-path` · planet: **Canonical Frobenius path**

Proposed module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/UnipotentFundamentalGroup`, namespace `TauCetiRoadmap.AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty.NC2`.

For any two endpoint fibres of the good-reduction unipotent rigid category, the Frobenius action on their tensor path torsor has a unique fixed point p_φ(b,x), rational over the coefficient field. The paths satisfy p_φ(x,y)∘p_φ(b,x)=p_φ(b,y), p_φ(b,b)=1, and are natural under pointed curve maps. They are unchanged after replacing a common Frobenius by a positive power. Through berthelot-ogus they supply tensor-natural horizontal continuation between distinct residue discs, agreeing with rigid-fibre transport inside a disc. These canonical paths do not require a choice of logarithm or a Hodge-filtration-preserving Frobenius.

**Hypotheses.**

- Good-reduction pair and the Frobenius Lang hypothesis; endpoints defined over the coefficient field after a common finite extension if needed.

**Construction.**

1. Trivialize the torsor over a field extension and write φ(p)=p·h. Solving the resulting twisted Lang equation gives a unique fixed path by frobenius-lang.
2. Uniqueness makes the fixed path invariant under descent automorphisms, so it descends to the coefficient field.
3. Identity, composition, pullback, Frobenius power independence and local agreement follow because both sides are fixed tensor paths and the fixed path is unique.

**API.**

- `CanonicalFrobeniusPath.fixed` (characterisation): The canonical path is fixed by the specified Frobenius.
- `CanonicalFrobeniusPath.unique` (extensionality): Any Frobenius-fixed tensor path equals the canonical path.
- `CanonicalFrobeniusPath.comp` (functoriality): Canonical paths compose with endpoint order b→x→y.
- `CanonicalFrobeniusPath.sameDisc` (compatibility): Within one residue disc, canonical continuation is the local horizontal transport.
- `CanonicalFrobeniusPath.power` (compatibility): A common positive Frobenius power gives the same canonical path.

**Unit tests.**

- `canonical_equal_endpoint` (degenerate): The fixed path at equal endpoints is identity.
- `canonical_additive` (computation): For φ(z)=2z+c on an additive torsor in characteristic zero, the unique fixed point is −c.
- `canonical_identity_fails` (non-example): Identity Frobenius on the additive line has more than one fixed point and does not meet the unique-fixed-path hypotheses.

**Checks.**

#### 2.26. Word coordinates and global transport

*Comparison* `NC.2/word-path-bridge`

Proposed module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/UnipotentFundamentalGroup`, namespace `TauCetiRoadmap.AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty.NC2`.

In the affine universal connection and its proper extendable quotient, the tensor path p_φ(a,c) corresponds under finite-path-module and affine trivialization to the truncated word element I(a,c)=1+Σ\_(0&lt;\|w\|≤n)(∫\_a^c w)w, with the outermost integral matching left-prepending. For endpoints in one residue disc the coefficients are exactly the imported L1 local iterated integrals. For endpoints in different discs they are the imported Coleman coefficients selected by the canonical Frobenius path. Consequently the two-sided transport of a finite path module is v↦I(x_0,x) v I(b,b_0). This map intertwines the endpoint Frobenius operators. The local coefficient formula and the global Frobenius identification are separate dependencies.

**Hypotheses.**

- Good-reduction compactification, affine open, chosen H^1 forms and consistent word convention.
- Global Coleman realization and Frobenius-normalized continuation imported from L1.

**Proof.**

1. Identify a horizontal solution of affine-universal with its coefficient recursion; imported local word expansions satisfy the recursion and initial value, so agree on each disc.
2. For cross-disc endpoints use canonical-frobenius-path. Its uniqueness and the L1 Frobenius Coleman realization identify the global solution; local integration alone cannot prove this.
3. Apply affine-composition to the two endpoint transports to obtain the ordered word product, and pass to the proper quotient if appropriate.

#### 2.27. Crystalline coordinate path comparison

*Theorem* `NC.2/crystalline-path-coordinates` · planet: **Crystalline path comparison**

Proposed module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/UnipotentFundamentalGroup`, namespace `TauCetiRoadmap.AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty.NC2`.

Let (Xcal,Dcal) be a smooth proper good-reduction pair over W(F_q), with Dcal a relative finite étale divisor, and let b,x be integral sections of Ycal=Xcal−Dcal. For the geometric unipotent étale path scheme P_et(b,x), O(P_et) is an ind-crystalline G_K0-representation. There is a canonical comparison D_cris(O(P_et))≅O(P_rig(b_bar,x_bar)) and, after the rigid/de Rham identification, its scalar extension is O(P_dR(b,x)). It is compatible with Frobenius, the Hodge filtration after de Rham extension, tensor structures, endpoint composition and the coordinate coactions; at b=x it is a Hopf-algebra comparison. Every finite-dimensional Galois-stable subspace occurring in the coordinate union is crystalline. This is a nonlinear geometric comparison; the ordinary comparison for H^1 alone does not imply it.

**Hypotheses.**

- Unramified K_0=Frac W(F_q), smooth proper model and relative smooth boundary, integral endpoints.
- Olsson’s relative setup is specialized to the unit local system/isocrystal: trivial reductive hull and zero, hence nilpotent, local monodromy.
- Filtered compatibility uses the associated filtered crystalline objects, not a Frobenius-preserved Hodge filtration.

**Proof.**

1. Apply the unit specialization of Olsson’s pointed schematic comparison, obtained from the multiplicative crystalline/étale cochain comparison over the enlarged crystalline period ring. The group/path comparison is its degree-zero homotopy consequence.
2. Use Olsson’s finite Galois-stable coordinate-piece argument and descent from the enlarged ring to B_cris. The admissibility/subspace lemmas ensure genuine continuous crystalline finite pieces.
3. Use tensor compatibility to identify coordinate coactions and endpoint composition; rigid/de Rham evaluation identifies the endpoint Frobenius. Filtered association supplies strict de Rham compatibility. The missing general multiplicative cochain comparison input is recorded explicitly as a gap, rather than replaced by H^1 comparison.

**Checks.**

- For b=x the comparison respects augmentation, multiplication and coproduct.
- For the unit coordinate subspace it is the usual comparison of Q_p with K_0.

#### 2.28. Finite crystalline path comparison

*Comparison* `NC.2/finite-path-comparison`

Proposed module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/UnipotentFundamentalGroup`, namespace `TauCetiRoadmap.AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty.NC2`.

Under crystalline-path-coordinates, each finite M_n^et(b,x) is crystalline and D_cris(M_n^et(b,x))≅M_n^rig(b_bar,x_bar); identifying with the de Rham fibre gives a filtered Frobenius comparison after scalar extension. The comparisons commute with length transitions, bilinear composition and the source algebra action. On grade n they make the diagram from D_cris((H^1_et∨)^⊗n)≅(H^1_dR∨)^⊗n to the corresponding quotient length grades commute; a proper curve’s grade is not asserted to equal the entire tensor power. For finite ramified extensions K/K_0 of an existing good-reduction pair, D_cris takes values over K_0 and D_dR over K; base change of the established crystalline data supplies the K version. No new ramified-model comparison is inferred without a descent theorem.

**Hypotheses.**

- Hypotheses of crystalline-path-coordinates; finite path modules identified by universal evaluation.
- For the base-change clause, the model and endpoints descend to the displayed unramified pair.

**Proof.**

1. Identify O(P_et) with the union of M_n^et∨, using length-algebra and finite-path-module. Each finite dual is a Galois-stable crystalline subobject of the ind-coordinate ring.
2. Use exact tensor duality of D_cris on crystalline representations to dualize the finite coordinate comparison. Compatibility with augmentation and coactions identifies the precise universal length piece, not just a vector space with matching dimension.
3. Use H^1 comparison on the augmentation generator and tensor exactness on its quotient grades. Extend coefficients along the imported period-functor base change for models that descend.

**Checks.**

- At n=0 this is the unit comparison; at n=1 its nontrivial grade is the dual H^1 comparison.
- At proper genus g and n=2 the comparison carries the cup-product quotient relation; it does not remove that relation.

#### 2.29. Depth one and the Jacobian

*Comparison* `NC.2/depth-one-jacobian`

Proposed module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/UnipotentFundamentalGroup`, namespace `TauCetiRoadmap.AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty.NC2`.

For a smooth proper geometrically connected curve X/k with rational b and Jacobian J, the Abel–Jacobi morphism a_b:X→J induces canonical abelian realization identifications U_et⟨1⟩≅V_pJ as an additive group with Galois action, and U_dR⟨1⟩≅H^1_dR(X)∨≅H^1_dR(J)∨ as additive filtered groups. Their good-reduction comparison is the ordinary Jacobian Tate-module/de Rham comparison. At a proper local good-reduction field, F^0 H^1_dR(X)∨=ann H^0(X,Ω¹), and the quotient by F^0 is Lie(J). P_et⟨1⟩(b,x) is the rational Kummer torsor for \[x−b\]∈J(k), and the de Rham linear path periods are the ordinary integrals of one-forms. For an open curve, H^1 has additional boundary directions and the corresponding generalized Jacobian replaces J.

**Hypotheses.**

- Proper smooth geometrically connected curve, rational b; coefficient p in the étale realization.
- Good reduction is required only for crystalline comparison and the local filtered statement.
- The Jacobian and Abel–Jacobi construction are imported from JacobianChallenge; the cohomological bridges are separate inputs, including the existing SF.3 Tate/H^1 node and the recorded de Rham compatibility requirement.

**Proof.**

1. The first augmentation/Lie graded piece is Ext^1(1,1)∨=H^1∨, so central depth one is its vector group.
2. Import the Jacobian and the pointed Abel–Jacobi morphism from JacobianChallenge B–F, and the untwisted étale H^1/Tate-module identification and Abel–Jacobi pullback from SF.3/tate-module-etale-h1. Dualize with the same covariance. For endpoint compatibility, pull back the finite étale multiplication-by-p^r covers of J along a_b: their fibre over x is the division-point torsor of \[x−b\], and the fibre over b has its zero lift. Passing to the Tate-module inverse limit and rationalizing gives the Kummer torsor. The exact de Rham Abel–Jacobi H^1 comparison and proper curve Hodge calculation are additional requirements, not assertions supplied by the current upstream B–F layers.
3. Apply the linear abelian-scheme comparison and the dual Hodge filtration. The annihilator description gives Lie(J) as the quotient; integration on linear paths is already supplied by Coleman L1.

**Checks.**

- For a genus-g proper curve the depth-one vector group has dimension 2g and its F^0 has dimension g.
- For P¹ the proper depth-one group is trivial; puncturing twice gives the one-dimensional boundary realization of G_m.
- For an elliptic curve with origin b, the Abel–Jacobi map is the identity, and the depth-one torsor is its usual rational Kummer torsor.

<a id="nc-2-finite-cover-boundary"></a>

#### 2.30. Finite covers are not unipotent points

*Theorem* `NC.2/finite-cover-boundary`

Proposed module `TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/UnipotentFundamentalGroup`, namespace `TauCetiRoadmap.AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty.NC2`.

The geometric pro-unipotent Q_p group does not recover the full profinite fundamental group or all finite étale covers. In characteristic zero, G_m has nontrivial finite étale covers t↦t^m for m&gt;1, while its de Rham unipotent group is G_a and its geometric Q_p-unipotent étale realization is the additive Tate realization Q_p(1). The additive rational point group is uniquely m-divisible for each m&gt;0 and has no nontrivial finite abstract group quotient. It therefore cannot replace the profinite finite-cover classifier. A finite-rank unipotent representation and a finite covering set are different objects.

**Hypotheses.**

- Geometric characteristic-zero G_m and Q_p coefficients.
- No comparison between realisations is used without its coefficient extension.

**Proof.**

1. Apply affine-universality to the one-generator H^1 of G_m, or the continuous representation equivalence to its procyclic geometric p-adic monodromy, to obtain the additive unipotent realization.
2. Use the imported finite-cover theory to exhibit the degree-m étale power map.
3. Any finite quotient of a divisible abelian group is divisible, and the only finite divisible abelian group is trivial. The full geometric profinite group has the displayed nontrivial quotient, so its finite-cover information cannot be reconstructed from the additive Q_p points.

**Checks.**

- The cover t↦t² remains nontrivial even though the additive Q_p point group has no quotient of order two.
- No statement that all rational points of a pro-unipotent group determine all finite covers is admitted.

<a id="layer-nc-3"></a>

## NC.3. Nonabelian cohomology and Selmer varieties

This layer supplies the cohomological domain of nonabelian Chabauty. It has two parts. The **cohomological core** is continuous nonabelian H¹ of a topological group G acting continuously by automorphisms on a topological group U, with no geometric input: cocycles, gauge classes, the connecting maps for a subgroup that need not be normal, discrete finite-quotient descent, inflation and restriction, functoriality in coefficients and source, inner twisting and gauge transport, twisted kernels and their quotients, the invariant action on kernel cohomology and the orbit description of coefficient fibres, and the classification of equivariant topological torsors. The **geometric part** compares the core with Tau Ceti's abelian continuous cohomology, constructs the central obstruction to continuous H², passes to algebra-valued cohomology functors for unipotent groups over period rings, proves their representability by affine varieties, and defines local conditions, global Selmer varieties and Kim's central dimension bound. NC.4 consumes the local and global Selmer varieties and their localization maps; NC.5 and NC.6 consume the dimension statements.

**The core.** The conventions are those of [Conventions](#conventions): c(gh) = c(g)·g(c(h)), the gauge action (u·c)(g) = u·c(g)·g(u)⁻¹, H¹(G, U) the pointed orbit set. Neither library has this; Mathlib's only nonabelian H¹ is the Čech one of presheaves of groups on a site, and Tau Ceti's `ContCohomology` is additive. For a closed equivariant embedding A ≤ B, not necessarily normal, the invariant left cosets (B/A)^G map to H¹(G, A) by a connecting map, and the sequence 1 → A^G → B^G → (B/A)^G → H¹(G, A) → H¹(G, B) is exact as pointed sets; for a normal subgroup the quotient continues the sequence. No continuous section of B → B/A is needed for this. For a compact group with discrete coefficients every class comes from a finite discrete quotient, and H¹ is the colimit over open normal subgroups along inflation. Twisting by a cocycle c identifies H¹(G, U_c) with H¹(G, U), sending the base point to [c]; this is the tool for computing fibres of H¹(G, B) → H¹(G, C) away from the base point, which are orbits of the invariant group of the twisted quotient acting on the cohomology of the twisted kernel. The lemma-level groups below are the declaration-sized steps of these assembled theorems, which are stated first.

**The abelian comparison and the central obstruction.** For a commutative topological module M, the unchanged underlying function identifies H¹(G, Multiplicative M) with `ContCohomology.H1 G M`, naturally in compatible pairs of source and coefficient maps and compatibly with inflation and the finite-quotient colimit; the pinned `explicitFiniteQuotientColimit1` is the universal-property certificate of the cocone whose apex is `AddCommGrpCat.of (H1 G M)`. For a central extension with a homeomorphism of the central subgroup onto the kernel, the positive defect of a lift lands in the pinned Z², changing the lift by a continuous central cochain a changes it by d¹a, and the resulting class in H²_cont is independent of choices; its zero fibre is exactly the image of H¹ of the extension.

**Algebra-valued cohomology and representability.** A Galois coefficient family assigns to every commutative K-algebra R a topological group P(R) with jointly continuous G-action, functorially in R; its cohomology functor is R ↦ H¹(G, P(R)). The geometric instance is P_n(R) = U⟨n⟩(B ⊗_K R), for a complete topological field B of characteristic zero with a continuous action of a compact group G, F = B^G and [F : K] finite, with the inductive-limit topology of Kim's 2005 paper (§1, Lemmas 1–5). Under finite-dimensionality of H⁰, H¹, H² of the central vector layers and vanishing of their H⁰, the cohomology at each finite depth is represented by a finitely generated K-algebra: each extension step is a noncanonical product of the vector H¹ with the scheme-theoretic zero fibre of the obstruction (Kim 2005, Proposition 2). The invariant-coset functor is represented in the same way, with the central vector quotient invariants as the factor (the corrected form of Kim 2005, Proposition 3, source correction E1). Filtered affine torsors over B ⊗_K R are compared with point torsors only after the algebraic triviality, strict filtered trivialization and effective descent inputs are proved on every coefficient algebra.

**Local conditions and Selmer varieties.** A local condition is a neutral fibre: H¹_f and H¹_g are the kernels, on all coefficient algebras, of the maps to H¹ with coefficients in B_cris and B_dR, and the unramified condition is neutral restriction to inertia. Closedness of these loci is a theorem, proved by an explicit sufficient criterion (universal neutralizations giving finite linear equations on every algebra), not a consequence of describing an image on field points. The global Selmer functor of a number field k, a finite ramification set T and a finite set Σ of selected places is the subfunctor of H¹(G_{k,T}, U⟨n⟩(R)) whose localizations satisfy every chosen local condition; when the global and local functors are affine of finite type and the conditions are closed, it is a closed affine subscheme. For a central extension by a vector group V, every nonempty geometric fibre of the Selmer depth map is a torsor under the vector Selmer space of V, which gives dim Sel(U⟨n+1⟩) ≤ dim Sel(U⟨n⟩) + dim Sel(V) (Kim 2009, §4, pp. 127–129); at p this needs surjectivity of the invariant points over B_cris ⊗ R for the crystalline group over K₀. At depth one the Selmer variety is the linear Selmer space of the Jacobian, and the Heisenberg group gives a nonzero depth-two obstruction through the local cup product.

**Ownership.** ReductiveGroups owns the group-scheme dictionary, homogeneous quotients and unipotent groups; ProfiniteCohomology owns discrete continuous cohomology; ArithmeticGaloisDuality D7 owns local duality with rational coefficients; SelmerIwasawaCohomology owns the linear unramified and Bloch–Kato conditions; PadicHodgeTheory owns the period rings and their actions.

The six planets of this layer are the Nonabelian cohomology set H¹(G, U), the Exact sequence of nonabelian cohomology, Torsors and nonabelian H¹, Cohomology varieties, the Selmer variety and the Selmer dimension bound.

<a id="nc3-main"></a>

### The assembled theorems: functoriality, exactness, central extensions, twisting and torsors

<a id="nc-3-functoriality"></a>

#### 3.1. Functoriality of nonabelian H⁰ and H¹

*Lemma* `NC.3/functoriality`

Proposed module `TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/NonabelianCohomology/Functoriality`, namespace `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology`.

(a) A continuous G-equivariant group homomorphism f : U → U′ induces a homomorphism H⁰(G, U) → H⁰(G, U′) and maps Z¹(G, U) → Z¹(G, U′), c ↦ f ∘ c, and H¹(G, U) → H¹(G, U′), preserving base points, compatible with identities and composition, and with f(u·c) = f(u)·(f ∘ c). (b) A continuous group homomorphism φ : G′ → G, with G′ acting on U through φ, induces the restriction maps H⁰(G, U) → H⁰(G′, U) (inclusion) and Z¹(G, U) → Z¹(G′, U), c ↦ c ∘ φ, and H¹(G, U) → H¹(G′, U), base point preserving and functorial; in particular for a closed subgroup H ≤ G there is restriction H¹(G, U) → H¹(H, U). Maps of pointed sets that are compatible in this way are what the exact sequences (NC.3/exact-sequence) are built from.

**Hypotheses.**

- G is a topological group and U a topological group with an action of G by group automorphisms (MulDistribMulAction G U) such that the action map G × U → U is continuous (ContinuousSMul G U). In (a) U′ satisfies the same hypotheses and f is continuous with f(g•u) = g•f(u); in (b) φ is continuous and G′ acts on U by g′•u = φ(g′)•u.

**Proof.**

1. The coefficient-map leaves supply part (a). The new source-restriction leaves supply part (b) on actual cocycles, gauge-orbit classes and fixed subgroups, with identity/composition and mixed coefficient/source squares. Their subgroup comparisons identify the previously constructed restrictions. Geometric/additive and local-condition comparisons remain separate obligations.
2. (a) f ∘ c is continuous and f(c(gh)) = f(c(g))·f(g•c(h)) = f(c(g))·g•f(c(h)); f(u·c) = f(u)·(f∘c) because f(u c(g) (g•u)⁻¹) = f(u) f(c(g)) (g•f(u))⁻¹. So the map descends to orbits and sends the trivial cocycle to the trivial cocycle.
3. (b) c ∘ φ is continuous and (c∘φ)(g′h′) = c(φg′)·φ(g′)•c(φh′); the U-actions correspond, so the map descends.
4. Identities and composition hold on cocycles, hence on classes.
5. For repointed twisting comparisons under source restriction, import the direct twisted-source map, its proved translation square, representative-change naturality and translated composition law. The separately recorded geometric localization and local-condition identifications remain open; the abstract square does not establish them.
6. Apply H1.map to the actual restricted twisted-kernel inclusion using its joint action continuity. The native quotient action and H¹ comparison are supplied by NC.3/twisted-quotient-action through NC.3/twisted-quotient-h1-repointed-fibre; the continuous equivalence requires surjectivity and a quotient map. The single-gauge lift in NC.3/twisted-kernel-h1-mapped-converse gives the converse image statement when f is surjective, without requiring a continuous section. General inclusion injectivity is governed by the invariant action, not by functoriality alone. Geometric local-condition compatibility remains open.

**API.**

<a id="nc-3-abelian-comparison"></a>

#### 3.2. Comparison with abelian continuous cohomology

*Comparison* `NC.3/abelian-comparison`

Proposed module `TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/NonabelianCohomology/Basic`, namespace `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology`.

Let M be a commutative topological group written additively, with a continuous action of G by additive automorphisms, and U = Multiplicative M. With the induced action on U (Mathlib has no instance for it, so one is supplied), Z¹(G, U) is Tau Ceti's group of explicit continuous 1-cocycles ContCohomology.Z1 G M (cocycles c(gh) = c(g) + g•c(h), in Mathlib's IsCocycle₁ convention), the action of U on Z¹ is translation by the coboundaries d⁰(m)(g) = g•m − m up to sign, and the class map induces a bijection of pointed sets H¹(G, U) ≅ ContCohomology.H1 G M, sending the base point to 0. Consequently H¹(G, U) inherits a commutative group structure, H⁰(G, U) = ContCohomology.H0 G M, and for discrete G the cocycles are Mathlib's groupCohomology.IsMulCocycle₁ maps (the factor order being immaterial for commutative M).

**Hypotheses.**

- M a commutative topological additive group with a continuous DistribMulAction of G; G a topological group.

**Proof.**

1. The multiplicative cocycle identity for Multiplicative M is additive: c(gh) = c(g) + g•c(h); continuity is the same condition. This is Tau Ceti's d¹-kernel description (ContCohomology.d1_apply: d¹f(g,h) = g•f(h) − f(gh) + f(g)).
2. The action: (m·c)(g) = m + c(g) − g•m = c(g) − (d⁰m)(g), so orbits are cosets of B¹ = range d⁰ (Tau Ceti ContCohomology.B1) inside Z¹, and the orbit set is Z¹/B¹ = ContCohomology.H1 G M.
3. Invariants: FixedPoints.subgroup of the multiplicative action is FixedPoints.addSubgroup of the additive one (Tau Ceti ContCohomology.H0).
4. For discrete G and commutative M, c(gh) = c(g)·g•c(h) and Mathlib's IsMulCocycle₁ c(gh) = g•c(h)·c(g) coincide.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.instMulDistribMulActionMultiplicative` (constructor): A DistribMulAction of G on the additive group M induces a MulDistribMulAction of G on Multiplicative M (not an instance in Mathlib at the pin), and continuity of the action transfers.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.equivContCohomology` (compatibility): Z¹(G, Multiplicative M) ≃ ContCohomology.Z1 G M, the identity on underlying functions.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.equivContCohomology` (compatibility): H¹(G, Multiplicative M) ≃ ContCohomology.H1 G M, compatible with the class maps.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.equivContCohomology_one` (compatibility): The base point goes to 0.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H0.equivContCohomology` (compatibility): H⁰(G, Multiplicative M) corresponds to ContCohomology.H0 G M.

**Checks.**

- For trivial action, both sides are the continuous homomorphisms G → M (Tau Ceti ContCohomology.H1EquivOfSmulEqSelf).

<a id="nc-3-normal-h1-kernel"></a>

#### 3.3. Exactness for a normal coefficient subgroup

*Theorem* `NC.3/normal-h1-kernel`

Proposed module `TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/NonabelianCohomology/ExactSequence`, namespace `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology`.

Let π:B → C be a continuous open surjective equivariant homomorphism to a topological G-group C, with ker π=i(A). For y ∈ H¹(G,B), π\_\*(y)=1 if and only if y lies in the image of i\_\*:H¹(G,A) → H¹(G,B). No continuous section of π is required.

**Hypotheses.**

- G, A and B are groups with topologies; A and B are topological groups.
- Continuous actions of G on A and B by automorphisms; i:A → B is a closed embedding and group homomorphism commuting with G.
- C is a topological group with continuous G-action by automorphisms; π is equivariant, continuous, open, surjective and has kernel i(A).

**Proof.**

1. Choose a continuous cocycle d representing y. Triviality of π\_\*y supplies x ∈ C with π(d(g))=x(g•x)⁻¹.
2. Lift the single element x to b ∈ B by surjectivity; the gauge b⁻¹•d takes values in ker π=i(A). Restrict it to A using unique pointwise preimages, and transfer continuity with the embedding continuous_iff theorem. The cocycle law follows by equivariance and injectivity.
3. Its H¹ class maps to y because it is a gauge transform of d. Conversely π∘i=1, so every class in the image is killed. Openness allows application to the canonical topological-group quotient; it is not used to lift a whole function.
4. The later native twisted-kernel range lemmas give both directions for the quotient neutral fibre; for surjective f the mapped neutral fibre also equals the kernel-H¹ image. Translation gives the original fibre over \[f∘c\]. Only one constant gauge element is lifted; neither a continuous section nor a quotient-map assumption on f is needed for this mapped range equality.
5. The named-native-kernel and abstract-embedded-kernel comparisons now transport these image criteria. For an abstract i:A→U, topological embedding and range(i)=ker(f) supply inverse continuity and uniqueness of each point preimage. These comparisons do not give unconditional H¹ injectivity. The invariant-action/orbit nodes classify the remaining ambiguity; central H² and geometric/local-condition interfaces remain open.

**Checks.**

- Canonical quotient by a closed normal subgroup is an instance; the H⁰ connecting cocycle for a nonnormal subgroup does not require this theorem.

<a id="nc-3-exact-sequence"></a>

#### 3.4. Kernel of inclusion in nonabelian cohomology

*Theorem* `NC.3/exact-sequence` · planet: **Exact sequence of nonabelian cohomology**

Proposed module `TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/NonabelianCohomology/ExactSequence`, namespace `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology`.

For an equivariant closed embedding i:A → B of topological G-groups and x ∈ H¹(G,A), i\_\*(x)=1 if and only if there exist b ∈ B and c ∈ Z¹(G,A) such that x=\[c\] and i(c(g))=b⁻¹(g•b) for every g. Equivalently, the classes killed by inclusion are exactly the connecting classes of invariant left cosets. Normality and a continuous quotient section are not required.

**Hypotheses.**

- G, A and B are groups with topologies; A and B are topological groups.
- Continuous actions of G on A and B by automorphisms; i:A → B is a closed embedding and group homomorphism commuting with G.

**Proof.**

1. Represent x by c. By the inherited H¹ basepoint characterisation, i\_\*x=1 iff i(c(g))=u(g•u)⁻¹ for one u ∈ B and all g. Put b=u⁻¹ to obtain the displayed formula.
2. Conversely that formula makes the image cocycle the B-coboundary of b⁻¹, so its class is the basepoint.
3. The formula supplies membership in i(A) for each g and therefore an admissible connecting-cocycle input. Its image identity and injectivity identify it with c. Change of lift and the separate fixed-orbit theorem give the coset interpretation.
4. For a nonneutral coefficient-map fibre, H1.twistEquiv_map_fibre replaces the fibre over \[f∘c\] by the neutral fibre of the actual twisted coefficient map. The later native quotient, named-kernel and embedded-kernel comparisons supply the corresponding abstract realizations with their own explicit continuity and surjectivity hypotheses. Geometric local-condition identifications remain open.
5. For cohomologous representatives use H1.changeRepresentative, its concrete gauge realization and composition law. The source and coefficient naturality squares are supplied. Full representative-change compatibility of the transported kernel orbit classification and geometric local conditions remains a separate obligation; it does not strengthen this inclusion-kernel theorem.

**Checks.**

- Kim's crystalline condition: for U_n(R) ≤ U_n(B_cr ⊗ R), the image of H⁰(G_v, U_n(B_cr ⊗ R)/U_n(R)) → H¹(G_v, U_n(R)) is the set of crystalline torsors (Kim 2009, §3); this is (a) for a subgroup that is not normal.
- Exactness is of pointed sets: two elements of H¹(G, A) with the same image in H¹(G, B) need not differ by an element of (B/A)^G unless one of them is the base point; the fibres over other points are described after twisting (NC.3/twisting).

<a id="nc-3-twisting"></a>

#### 3.5. Twisting by a cocycle

*Construction* `NC.3/twisting`

Proposed module `TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/NonabelianCohomology/Basic`, namespace `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology`.

Let c ∈ Z¹(G, U). The twisted group ₍c₎U is U with the action g ⋆ u := c(g)·(g•u)·c(g)⁻¹, again a continuous action by automorphisms. The map τ_c : Z¹(G, ₍c₎U) → Z¹(G, U), c′ ↦ (g ↦ c′(g)·c(g)), is a bijection carrying the trivial cocycle to c and the twisted-conjugation action of U on the left to that on the right; it induces a bijection of underlying sets H¹(G, ₍c₎U) ≅ H¹(G, U) sending the source base point to \[c\]; it becomes a pointed equivalence only when the target is repointed at \[c\]. Twisting is compatible with G-stable subgroups (for cocycles with values in them) and with quotients by normal ones, so that fibres of the maps in NC.3/exact-sequence over \[c\] become fibres over the base point after twisting.

**Hypotheses.**

- G is a topological group and U a topological group with an action of G by group automorphisms (MulDistribMulAction G U) such that the action map G × U → U is continuous (ContinuousSMul G U). c a continuous cocycle.

**Construction.**

1. g ⋆ − is an automorphism of U (conjugation composed with the automorphism g•−), and (gh) ⋆ u = c(gh)(gh•u)c(gh)⁻¹ = c(g) g•c(h) g•(h•u) g•c(h)⁻¹ c(g)⁻¹ = g ⋆ (h ⋆ u) by the cocycle identity; continuity from continuity of c and of the action.
2. τ_c(c′) is a cocycle for U: c′(gh)c(gh) = c′(g)·(g ⋆ c′(h))·c(g)·g•c(h) = c′(g)c(g)·g•(c′(h)c(h)). The inverse is c″ ↦ c″·c⁻¹. For u ∈ U, τ_c(u·c′)(g) = u c′(g)(g ⋆ u)⁻¹ c(g) = u c′(g) c(g) (g•u)⁻¹ = (u·τ_c(c′))(g).
3. Hence the bijection of orbit sets; the trivial cocycle maps to c.
4. Compatibility with subgroups and quotients: twisting by a cocycle with values in a G-stable subgroup A preserves A; if A is normal every twist preserves A, and the quotient map U → U/A is equivariant for the twists by c and by its image.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist` (constructor): The type synonym ₍c₎U of U with the twisted action g ⋆ u = c(g)(g•u)c(g)⁻¹.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.smul_def` (characterisation): g ⋆ u = c(g)·(g•u)·c(g)⁻¹.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.continuousSMul` (other): The twisted action is continuous.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Z1.twistEquiv` (constructor): The bijection Z¹(G, ₍c₎U) ≃ Z¹(G, U), c′ ↦ c′·c.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistEquiv` (constructor): The induced bijection H¹(G, ₍c₎U) ≃ H¹(G, U).
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.H1.twistEquiv_one` (compatibility): twistEquiv sends the base point to the class of c.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.self` (compatibility): Twisting by the trivial cocycle is the original action.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.toOriginal` (compatibility): The actual underlying group identification j_c:Twist(c)≃\*U is native MulEquiv.refl U. It preserves multiplication and the original topology, but need not preserve the original G-action.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.mem_fixed_iff` (characterisation): For x∈Twist(c), x belongs to H⁰(G,Twist(c)) if and only if c(g)·g(j_c(x))=j_c(x)·c(g) for every g∈G.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Twist.toOriginal_apply` (simp): For every actual x∈Twist(c), j_c(x) is exactly x regarded in U. This is the native identity equivalence on the underlying group, not an unspecified automorphism.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.twist_trivial` (degenerate): Twisting by the trivial cocycle gives back U with its action, and twistEquiv is the identity.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.twist_abelian` (computation): For U commutative, g ⋆ u = g•u for every c, and twistEquiv is translation by c.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.twist_S3` (computation): For G = ℤ/2 acting trivially on S₃ and c sending the generator to a transposition τ, the twisted action is conjugation by τ, whose invariants form the subgroup {1, τ} of order 2.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.twist_changes_invariants` (non-example): A twist need not be isomorphic to U as a G-group: for G = ℤ/2 acting trivially on S₃ and c(σ) = τ a transposition, H⁰(G, ₍c₎S₃) = {1, τ} has order 2 while H⁰(G, S₃) = S₃ has order 6; and twistEquiv sends the base point to \[c\], not to the base point.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.twist_commutative_action` (compatibility): If the original multiplication on U commutes, the actual twisted action g⋆x agrees with the original action g(x), for every c.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.twist_transposition_invariants` (computation): For the same discrete S₂→S₃ transposition cocycle with trivial original action, x∈H⁰(G,Twist(c)) if and only if x=1 or x=τ. The twisted action has exactly these two invariants, whereas the original trivial action fixes all six elements.

**Checks.**

- For trivial action and U commutative, twisting by any c does not change the action, and τ_c is translation by c.

**Uses.**

- [`NC.3/central-extension`](#nc-3-central-extension): The freeness hypothesis is stated for twisted invariants.

#### 3.6. Central extensions: the action of H¹(G, Z) and the connecting map to H²

*Theorem* `NC.3/central-extension`

Proposed module `TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/NonabelianCohomology/ExactSequence`, namespace `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology`.

Let Z ≤ B be a closed G-stable subgroup contained in the centre of B, and C := B/Z. (a) The abelian group H¹(G, Z) (NC.3/abelian-comparison) acts on H¹(G, B) by \[z\]·\[c\] := \[g ↦ z(g)c(g)\], and the fibres of H¹(G, B) → H¹(G, C) are exactly the orbits of this action. (b) Suppose the projection B → C has a continuous (set-theoretic) section s. Then there is a connecting map δ² : H¹(G, C) → H²(G, Z), Tau Ceti's explicit continuous H² (ContCohomology.H2 of Z written additively), sending the class of c̄ to the class of the 2-cocycle (g, h) ↦ c(g)·(g•c(h))·c(gh)⁻¹ for the continuous lift c = s ∘ c̄; and the image of H¹(G, B) → H¹(G, C) is δ²⁻¹(0). (c) If, for every c ∈ Z¹(G, B), the group C twisted by the image of c (NC.3/twisting) has only the trivial G-invariant element, then the action in (a) is free, so each nonempty fibre is a principal homogeneous space of H¹(G, Z). The convention in (b) is the positive defect matching Tau Ceti's additive d¹. Kim arXiv v1, printed p.5, defines dc(g,h)=c(gh)(g•c(h))⁻¹c(g)⁻¹, its inverse. Thus δ² here is the negative of Kim's printed connecting class under the additive identification of the central coefficient; their zero loci agree.

**Hypotheses.**

- G is a topological group and B a topological group with an action of G by group automorphisms (MulDistribMulAction G B) such that the action map G × B → B is continuous (ContinuousSMul G B). Z closed, G-stable and central in B. For (b), a continuous section of B → C (for unipotent algebraic groups an algebraic splitting of the extension exists, as in Kim's proof). For (c), the stated vanishing of twisted invariants.

**Proof.**

1. (a) z·c is a continuous cocycle because Z is central: z(gh)c(gh) = z(g)(g•z(h))c(g)(g•c(h)) = (z(g)c(g))·g•(z(h)c(h)). The action is compatible with twisted conjugation by B (central z commutes with u), so it descends to classes; it preserves the image in H¹(G, C). Conversely if \[c₁\], \[c₂\] have the same image, replace c₂ by u·c₂ so that the images in Z¹(G, C) agree (lift one element of C); then z := c₁⁻¹c₂ is Z-valued, continuous and, Z being central, a cocycle.
2. (b) For the lift c = s ∘ c̄, the defect (g, h) ↦ c(g)(g•c(h))c(gh)⁻¹ lies in Z (its image in C is 1), is continuous, and satisfies the 2-cocycle identity in Z (a direct computation using centrality). Changing c̄ within its class or changing the lift by a Z-valued continuous 1-cochain changes the defect by a 2-coboundary of a continuous cochain, so δ² is well defined into Z²/B² with Tau Ceti's B² (coboundaries of continuous cochains). δ²\[c̄\] = 0 iff the lift can be corrected by a continuous Z-valued cochain to a cocycle, i.e. iff \[c̄\] lifts to H¹(G, B).
3. Sign comparison: the inverse of c(g)(g•c(h))c(gh)⁻¹ is c(gh)(g•c(h))⁻¹c(g)⁻¹, exactly Kim's printed boundary. In central additive coefficients, taking inverse negates the 2-cochain and its class. Tau Ceti's d¹a(g,h)=g•a(h)−a(gh)+a(g) fixes the positive convention. For a changed lift c′(g)=z(g)c(g), centrality gives D(c′)=D(c)+d¹z in additive notation. The independence and obstruction-exactness interfaces must use this convention; negation does not change whether the obstruction vanishes.
4. (c) If z·c = u·c with u ∈ B, then projecting to C gives ū·c̄ = c̄, i.e. ū is invariant for the action twisted by c̄; by hypothesis ū = 1, so u ∈ Z and z(g) = u(g•u)⁻¹ is a coboundary of Z (Kim's argument).
5. Identify the central subgroup with the actual kernel of its quotient projection, then use the named or abstract embedded-kernel comparison. The inner action on a central kernel is the original restricted action. The native quotient has its descended jointly continuous action. Its continuous H¹ comparison with the coefficient target requires surjectivity and a quotient map; the image-converse argument instead lifts one constant gauge element and requires only surjectivity.
6. The later invariant-action and orbit-quotient nodes supply abstract kernel fibre classification, including the repointed fibre over \[f∘c\]. They do not construct the central H² obstruction: genuine continuous cochain conversion, independence under lift/representative change and compatibility with Tau Ceti B² remain explicitly open and the H² signature stays OMITTED. Unipotent algebraic splittings, point topologies, filtered-affine torsor comparison, representability and local conditions also remain open.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.central_defect_sign_C3_C9` (computation): In the trivial-action C₉→C₃ extension, the least-residue section has positive defect 3 at (2,1), and the inverse convention has value 6; the values differ. These correspond to 1 and −1 in the central C₃. The native ZMod example proves this arithmetic discrimination, without claiming to construct the missing continuous H² class map.

**Checks.**

- For the lower central series of a unipotent group U with H⁰(G, U^i/U^{i+1}) = 0, (c) applies at every step, which is how Kim shows H¹(G, U\_{n+1}) ≅ H¹(G, U^{n+1}/U^{n+2}) × δ²⁻¹(0) (Kim 2005, Proposition 2).
- Without the section hypothesis, H¹(G, C) → H²(G, Z) need not be definable with continuous cochains; (a) and (c) do not need it.
- For the trivial-action central extension 0→C₃→C₉→C₃→0, use the lift s taking least residues. At (g,h)=(2,1), D=s(2)+s(1)−s(0)=3 in C₉, while the printed Kim boundary is −D=6. Identifying the central subgroup by a↦3a gives 1 and −1 in C₃. They are different. The current typed arithmetic test checks the lifts/defects only; a test of their actual H² classes requires the omitted central obstruction interface.

#### 3.7. Equivariant topological torsors and their isomorphisms

*Definition* `NC.3/equivariant-topological-torsors`

Proposed module `TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/NonabelianCohomology/Torsor`, namespace `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology`.

For topological groups G and U with a jointly continuous G-action by automorphisms on U, a (G,U)-torsor is a NONEMPTY topological space P with a continuous right U-action, every orbit map u↦p·u a homeomorphism, and a jointly continuous left G-action satisfying g(p·u)=(gp)·(gu). An isomorphism P≅Q is a homeomorphism commuting with both actions. Existence of such an isomorphism defines an equivalence relation on torsors. A point p defines the actual continuous cocycle c_p by gp=p·c_p(g). A continuous cocycle c gives the torsor model U with right multiplication and g⋆u=c(g)·g(u), up to the harmless universe lift represented by its specified homeomorphism U≅P_c. Package the underlying right-action torsor as native Torsor Uᵐᵒᵖ P with IsTopologicalTorsor P; only the compatible continuous G-action and its semilinearity are new data.

**Hypotheses.**

- G and U are topological groups. The G-action on U is by group automorphisms and is jointly continuous.
- The carrier P is nonempty; a free transitive action stated without nonemptiness would also admit the empty space. Orbit maps have continuous inverses, not merely continuous bijections.

**Construction.**

1. Reuse native Torsor Uᵐᵒᵖ P and IsTopologicalTorsor P, including native nonemptiness, free transitivity and continuous scalar division. Their orbit homeomorphism is Homeomorph.smulConst p; compose with MulOpposite.opHomeomorph to obtain U≃P. Conversely the original right-action/homeomorphic-orbit description gives the native continuous scalar division by choosing one point and using its global coordinates, so this is the same mathematical object. Add only the semilinear continuous G-action. Reflexivity, symmetry and composition of action-compatible homeomorphisms prove the isomorphism relation is a setoid.
2. The inverse of the orbit homeomorphism sends gp to c_p(g). Semilinearity and cancellation yield c_p(gh)=c_p(g)·g(c_p(h)); its continuity is composition with the continuous G-orbit map.
3. At p·u the cocycle is u⁻¹c_p(g)g(u), exactly inverse-gauge translation under the existing Z1 action. An isomorphism carries p to a point with the same cocycle.
4. In the model P_c, associativity of g⋆u=c(g)g(u) is the cocycle law. Joint continuity follows from the cocycle and original action. Right multiplication is semilinear, and left translation by a fixed point is a homeomorphism.
5. These are authored topological abstractions of the pointwise calculation in Kim Proposition 1. Its filtered affine-algebra hypotheses, scheme descent and representability are not consequences of this abstraction.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor` (constructor): The semilinear G-action bundle over native Torsor Uᵐᵒᵖ P and IsTopologicalTorsor P; native torsor theory supplies nonemptiness and the homeomorphic orbit maps.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.Iso` (constructor): An isomorphism P→Q is a homeomorphism respecting the right U-action and the left G-action.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.Iso.ext` (extensionality): Two torsor isomorphisms are equal when their underlying functions agree at every point.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.Iso.refl` (constructor): The identity homeomorphism is a torsor isomorphism P→P.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.Iso.symm` (functoriality): A torsor isomorphism P→Q has an inverse torsor isomorphism Q→P.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.Iso.trans` (functoriality): Composing torsor isomorphisms P→Q and Q→R gives an isomorphism P→R.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.orbitHomeomorph` (constructor): For p∈P, the map u↦p·u is bundled as the native homeomorphism U≅P.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.orbitHomeomorph_apply` (simp): The orbit homeomorphism at p evaluates at u to p·u.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.ofCocycle` (constructor): For c∈Z¹(G,U), construct the semilinear torsor model with action g⋆u=c(g)g(u).
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.ofCocycleHomeomorph` (compatibility): The model P_c has a specified native homeomorphism U≅P_c, so universes do not force a definitional equality of carriers.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.ofCocycleHomeomorph_right` (simp): The model homeomorphism sends xy to the right translate by y of the image of x.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.ofCocycleHomeomorph_left` (simp): The G-translate of the model image of x equals the model image of c(g)g(x).
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.cocycle` (constructor): The unique continuous cocycle c_p with gp=p·c_p(g).
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.cocycle_spec` (characterisation): gp=p·c_p(g) for every g.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.cocycle_change_point` (relation): c\_(p·u)=u⁻¹·c_p under the existing gauge action.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.cocycle_map_iso` (compatibility): For an action-compatible homeomorphism e:P→Q, c\_(e(p))=c_p.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.cocycle_ofCocycle` (simp): The cocycle of the model at the image of 1 is exactly c.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.isoSetoid` (characterisation): The setoid relation on actual torsors is existence of an action-compatible homeomorphism, using its identity, inverse and composition.

**Unit tests.**

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.torsor_orbit_at_identity` (degenerate): The orbit homeomorphism at p sends 1 to p.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.torsor_coboundary_isomorphic` (characterisation): For every u∈U, the model of the coboundary u·g(u)⁻¹ is isomorphic as a (G,U)-torsor to the model of the trivial cocycle.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.torsor_gauge_isomorphic` (compatibility): The models of u·c and c are isomorphic as equivariant topological torsors.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.torsor_nonneutral_no_fixed_point` (non-example): If \[c\]≠1, the model P_c has no G-fixed point; an interface forgetting the G-action would wrongly identify it with the trivial torsor.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.tests.torsor_inequivalent_not_isomorphic` (non-example): If \[c\]≠\[d\], there is no action-compatible homeomorphism P_c→P_d, even though both underlying spaces are homeomorphic to U.

**Checks.**

- The empty space is excluded explicitly.
- Do not quotient all torsor homeomorphisms: both the G-action and the U-action must be preserved.
- The model of a nonneutral cocycle has no G-fixed point; a gauge change gives an isomorphic model.

**Uses.**

- [`NC.3/torsor-classification`](#nc-3-torsor-classification): Supplies the nonempty carrier, semilinearity, point cocycle and actual isomorphism relation whose quotient is classified by H¹.
- AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty:NC.0 and NC.2 path-torsor targets: Specifies the topological torsor interface; geometric/algebraic realization and their extra structures require separate comparisons.

#### 3.8. Torsors under U with compatible G-action are classified by H¹(G, U)

*Theorem* `NC.3/torsor-classification` · planet: **Torsors and nonabelian H¹**

Proposed module `TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/NonabelianCohomology/Torsor`, namespace `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology`.

A (G, U)-torsor is a nonempty topological space P with a continuous right action of U that is free and transitive, such that for one (equivalently every) p ∈ P the orbit map U → P, u ↦ p·u, is a homeomorphism, together with a continuous left action of G satisfying g•(p·u) = (g•p)·(g•u). For p ∈ P let c_p(g) ∈ U be the unique element with g•p = p·c_p(g). Then c_p ∈ Z¹(G, U), c\_{p·u} = u⁻¹·c_p under the twisted-conjugation action, so \[P\] := \[c_p\] ∈ H¹(G, U) is independent of p and of the isomorphism class of P; P ↦ \[P\] is a bijection from isomorphism classes of (G, U)-torsors to H¹(G, U), the trivial torsor U corresponds to the base point, and P has a G-fixed point iff \[P\] is the base point. The inverse sends \[c\] to U with the twisted G-action g ∗ u := c(g)·(g•u).

**Hypotheses.**

- G is a topological group and U a topological group with an action of G by group automorphisms (MulDistribMulAction G U) such that the action map G × U → U is continuous (ContinuousSMul G U). Torsors are topological, with the orbit maps homeomorphisms; isomorphisms of torsors are homeomorphisms compatible with both actions.

**Proof.**

1. Cocycle: (gh)•p = g•(p·c_p(h)) = (g•p)·(g•c_p(h)) = p·c_p(g)·g•c_p(h), and freeness gives c_p(gh) = c_p(g)·g•c_p(h). Continuity: c_p is the composite of g ↦ g•p with the inverse of the orbit homeomorphism.
2. Change of point: g•(p·u) = p·c_p(g)·(g•u) = (p·u)·u⁻¹c_p(g)(g•u), so c\_{pu}(g) = u⁻¹c_p(g)(g•u) = (u⁻¹·c_p)(g). An isomorphism of torsors carries p to a point with the same cocycle.
3. Inverse: for c ∈ Z¹, the formula g ∗ u := c(g)(g•u) is a continuous action (cocycle identity) compatible with right multiplication, and its cocycle at the point 1 is c. Cohomologous cocycles give isomorphic torsors (left multiplication by u), and a torsor is isomorphic to the one built from c_p via the orbit map at p.
4. A G-fixed point p has c_p = 1; conversely, if c_p(g) = u·(g•u)⁻¹ for all g, then g•(p·u) = p·c_p(g)·(g•u) = p·u, so p·u is fixed.

**API.**

- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.classOf` (constructor): The class \[c_p\] is independent of p.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.classOf_eq_mk_cocycle` (compatibility): For every point p, classOf(P)=\[c_p\].
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.classOf_ofCocycle` (simp): classOf(P_c)=\[c\].
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.classOf_eq_classOf_iff` (characterisation): classOf(P)=classOf(Q) if and only if there exists an action-compatible homeomorphism P→Q.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.classOf_surjective` (other): Every continuous H¹ class is the class of a topological torsor model.
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.classification` (equivalence): The actual quotient of torsors by existence of action-compatible homeomorphisms is equivalent to H¹(G,U).
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.classification_mk` (simp): The equivalence sends the quotient class of P to classOf(P).
- `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.Torsor.classOf_eq_one_iff` (characterisation): classOf(P)=1 if and only if P has a G-fixed point.

**Checks.**

- After constructing the geometric-to-topological torsor comparison recorded as a gap, a path torsor from a base point b to a rational point x has class \[P(x)\] in H¹(G_K,U), the target used by NC.4. The abstract topological classification alone does not supply the comparison.
- After the separate Galois-descent/effectivity comparison, Poonen's §5.12 algebraic torsor classification agrees with the point-space class map for G=Gal(k_s/k), U=H(k_s) discrete, in the smooth algebraic group scope. An arbitrary equivariant homeomorphism is not yet an algebraic torsor isomorphism.
