<a id="nc-3-depth-two-cup-obstruction"></a>

#### 3.359. A nonzero depth-two obstruction

*Application* `NC.3/depth-two-cup-obstruction`

Proposed module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/NonabelianChabauty/Cohomology`, namespace `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.NC3`.

Let X,Y,Z be continuous topological additive G-modules and β:X×Y→Z a continuous G-equivariant bilinear pairing. The Heisenberg extension U=X×Y×Z has law (x,y,z)(x′,y′,z′)=(x+x′,y+y′,z+z′+β(x,y′)). For cocycles a∈Z1(G,X), b∈Z1(G,Y), the section g↦(a(g),b(g),0) has positive defect β(a(g),g·b(h)); its H2 class is the oriented cup product \[a\]∪\_β\[b\]. It lifts iff that class is zero. For actual local Galois G=G_k with k/Qp finite, X=Qp, Y=Z=Qp(1) and the scalar pairing, local Tate duality supplies a,b with nonzero cup product in H2(G_k,Qp(1))≃Qp; that depth-two class does not lift. This example tests obstruction theory, not the H0-vanishing representability hypothesis, since X has nonzero invariants.

**Hypotheses.**

- Continuous bilinear G-equivariant β.
- actual continuous cup comparison.
- local p-adic duality with nonzero H1(Qp) for the nonzero Galois specialization.

**Proof.**

1. Use bilinearity for associativity, inverse and central kernel; the projection to X×Y is split by z=0 as a continuous set map.
2. Evaluate positiveDefect and identify β(a(g),g·b(h)); use continuous-central-obstruction and central-lift-exactness.
3. Import the continuous cup convention and rational local Tate duality. For V=Qp, H0 has dimension 1 and H2 is dual to H0(Qp(1))=0; the local Euler characteristic therefore gives dim H1(Qp)=1+\[k:Qp\]&gt;0. Choose a nonzero class and a dual Qp(1) class with nonzero pairing, identified by the local invariant with H2(Qp(1))≃Qp.
4. As a separate explicit sign check take discrete G=Z², X=Y=Z=Q, trivial action and coordinate homomorphisms. The two-cochain m(g)n(h) is not a coboundary because all trivial-action one-cochain coboundaries on abelian G are symmetric, while it takes 1 and 0 on the swapped coordinate generators.

**Checks.**

- The cup order is a(g) paired with g·b(h); swapping source sign negates its H2 class but preserves nonliftability; the actual Galois example requires the already planned rational p-adic duality supplier and the requested continuous cup-convention comparison.

<a id="layer-nc-4"></a>

## NC.4. Unipotent Albanese maps and Chabauty–Kim loci

This layer attaches to each local point of a curve its finite-depth de Rham period, compares that period with the local crystalline path class, and pulls the global Selmer image back to a set of local candidates. Its finiteness theorem has a strict dimension hypothesis, and its depth-one comparison says exactly when the resulting locus is the classical Chabauty locus.

**Datum and indexing.** For the local construction fix a finite extension K/ℚ_p and a smooth geometrically connected hyperbolic curve X/K with a smooth proper O_K-model X̄ and a finite étale boundary D, possibly empty; put 𝒳 = X̄ ∖ D and choose b ∈ 𝒳(O_K). Hyperbolic means 2g − 2 + deg D > 0. The domain is the integral tube 𝒳(O_K). For global containment take a number field F, R = O_{F,S}, the corresponding good pair over R and a finite ramification set T containing S and the places above p; a selected good place v ∉ S has completion K. Depth n is the quotient U⟨n⟩ of NC.2 (Kim's U_{n+1}). Write H_n = F⁰U⟨n⟩_dR and Q_n = U⟨n⟩_dR/H_n, the represented quotient by right multiplication; H_n need not be normal, so Q_n is a homogeneous space. Paths are right torsors and the period is the class of u with p_φ·u = p_H; in the affine word coordinates of NC.2 the ordered representative is I⁻¹γ.

**Maps and loci.** The local de Rham Albanese map j_n: 𝒳(O_K) → Q_n(K) sends x to the period of P_n(b, x); its coordinates are iterated Coleman integrals, and Kim's density theorem says that its image on every residue disc is Zariski dense in Q_n. The crystalline period map from the local crystalline H¹ of U⟨n⟩ to Q_n is a morphism of schemes natural on all coefficient algebras. The global étale path-class map sends an S-integral point to the class of its path torsor in the global Selmer variety, and the fundamental square says that localization followed by the crystalline period is the local Albanese map. There are three loci: the exact crystalline-image locus, the de Rham period-image locus and the locus cut out by the reduced Zariski closure of the geometric image; each contains the global points, and they need not be equal. The finiteness chain needs an annihilator only for the closure.

**Why the hypotheses are what they are.** At K = ℚ_p a strict bound dim S_n &lt; dim Q_n makes the geometric image closure proper, and affineness and integrality of Q_n give a nonzero regular function f vanishing on it. Discwise density makes f ∘ j_n nonzero on every residue disc; on integral points the disc parameter lies in the maximal ideal, and after rescaling the restricted series converges on the compact ring of integers, so Strassmann's bound (EffectiveDiophantineMethods ED.4) applies; a disc that is merely an open geometric p-adic disc would not do, and an analytic-zero theorem for preconnected domains cannot be used on a totally disconnected disc. For K ≠ ℚ_p the period target is the Weil restriction of Q_n, density in Q_n does not give density there, and the general criterion keeps explicit discwise nonvanishing. At depth one the Selmer period image is linear and already closed; its locus is cut out by the annihilator of W_S, the classical one by that of W_MW ⊆ W_S, and the two agree exactly when W_S = W_MW. No additional local condition or Tate–Shafarevich contribution is suppressed in that comparison.

**Ownership.** NC.2 supplies the path torsors, Hodge filtration, Frobenius, the affine word realization and the nonlinear and Jacobian comparisons; NC.3 the continuous nonabelian cohomology, local conditions, Selmer functors, their conditional representability and localization; ColemanIntegration L1 Coleman functions, the word algebra and residue-disc expansions; EffectiveDiophantineMethods ED.4 Strassmann's bound, abelian logarithms and classical Chabauty; SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.0 and SF.1 dimension, image closures and quotient sheaves; ReductiveGroups Layers 3 and 5 homogeneous quotients and unipotent torsors, with the split-unipotent refinements requested below; ReductiveGroupsPartII Weil restriction.

The planets are the Admissible torsor period, the Unipotent Albanese map, the Kim density theorem, the Crystalline period map, the Chabauty–Kim locus and the Chabauty–Kim finiteness criterion.

### Admissible torsors and the unipotent Albanese map

<a id="nc-4-admissible-period"></a>

#### 4.1. The period of an admissible path torsor

*Construction* `NC.4/admissible-period` · planet: **Admissible torsor period**

Proposed module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/ChabautyKim/Albanese`, namespace `TauCeti.ChabautyKim`.

Let K be a characteristic-zero p-adic field and U_n the finite-depth de Rham unipotent group of NC.2. Write H_n=F⁰U_n, a closed split unipotent subgroup, not assumed normal, and Q_n=U_n/H_n for the represented quotient by right multiplication. On a commutative K-algebra R, an admissible right U_n-torsor T has the NC.2 finite coordinate filtration, a compatible Frobenius with a unique fixed point p_φ, and a Hodge reduction F⁰T with an R-point p_H. Define admissiblePeriod(T)=\[u\] in Q_n(R), where p_φ·u=p_H. Changing p_H to p_H·h changes u to uh for h∈H_n(R), hence preserves its class. Quotient representability and triviality of split-unipotent torsors over affine bases are imported inputs. Native point reduction: for a Torsor U_nᵒᵖ T, u is the underlying U_n element of p_H divided by p_φ in the opposite group; the point quotient is Mathlib's left-coset carrier U_n/H_n with relation u⁻¹v∈H_n.

**Hypotheses.**

- U_n and its filtered/Frobenius path structure come from NC.2; Frobenius Lang invertibility uses the positive-weight hypotheses there, not an arbitrary automorphism of an arbitrary unipotent group.
- All R are commutative K-algebras, including nonreduced ones; H_n is smooth split unipotent and the Hodge torsor is trivial over Spec R.

**Construction.**

1. Use the imported homogeneous quotient sheaf and its affine representation; the affine torsor-vanishing input identifies Q_n(R) with right-multiplication orbits U_n(R)/H_n(R).
2. Use the NC.2 Frobenius Lang scheme isomorphism after coefficient extension to obtain the unique fixed section on every affine coefficient algebra; identify T(R) with U_n(R), retaining the right-action order. The field-endpoint canonical-path theorem alone does not supply this all-algebra step.
3. Hodge points differ by right multiplication by H_n; quotient this difference.

**API.**

- `admissiblePeriod_eq_mk` (characterisation): The period is the coset of the unique u with p_φ·u=p_H.
- `admissiblePeriod_hodge_change` (relation): For h∈H_n(R), replacing p_H by p_H·h leaves the period unchanged.
- `admissiblePeriod_eq_iff` (extensionality): For fixed p_φ, the periods of p_H and p′\_H coincide iff u⁻¹u′∈H_n(R).
- `admissiblePeriod_self` (simp): Choosing p_H=p_φ gives \[1\].
- `admissiblePeriod_transport` (functoriality): A right U_n-equivariant isomorphism of torsor point carriers preserving the two chosen points preserves the period.

**Unit tests.**

- `admissiblePeriod_identity` (computation): On the self-torsor Uᵒᵖ, with p_φ=op(1) and p_H=op(g), the period is \[g\], not \[g⁻¹\].
- `admissiblePeriod_right_change` (compatibility): On that self-torsor, for h∈H, the periods of op(g) and op(gh) agree, even for nonnormal H.
- `admissiblePeriod_left_change_fails` (non-example): In S₃ take H generated by h=(01), g=(12). With p_φ=1, the periods of g and hg differ, although those of g and gh agree.
- `admissiblePeriod_inverse_fixed_path` (non-example): In the self-torsor for U=Multiplicative(ℚ), H={1}, put g=ofAdd(1), p_φ=op(g) and p_H=op(1). The period is \[g⁻¹\], and differs from \[g\]. This catches replacing the ordered ratio by the forward fixed-path coordinate or ignoring p_φ.

**Checks.**

- No group structure on Q_n is asserted when H_n is nonnormal.
- For the neutral filtered Frobenius torsor with p_H=p_φ, the period is \[1\].

**Uses.**

- Kim §1 Proposition 1, pp.105–106: Classifies separately trivialized filtered/Frobenius torsors.
- NC.4 local-albanese and crystalline-period: Provides a common de Rham target for geometric paths and crystalline torsors.

#### 4.2. Admissible torsors and the Hodge quotient

*Comparison* `NC.4/admissible-classification`

Proposed module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/ChabautyKim/Albanese`, namespace `TauCeti.ChabautyKim`.

Under the hypotheses of admissible-period, the period gives a natural bijection, for every commutative K-algebra R, between isomorphism classes of admissible U_n-torsors and Q_n(R). Isomorphisms preserve the right torsor action, coordinate filtration, Frobenius and Hodge filtration. This represents the finite-level admissible-torsor functor, rather than merely classifying K-points. The Hodge structure is the full NC.2 normalized multiplicative filtration; a reduction to H_n without that structure is not silently substituted for it.

**Hypotheses.**

- Admissibility, split-unipotent affine torsor vanishing and normalized filtered structure as in admissible-period.

**Proof.**

1. An isomorphism preserves p_φ by its uniqueness and maps Hodge points to Hodge points, so periods agree.
2. For equal cosets, the unique p_φ-compatible torsor isomorphism differs in Hodge coordinates by an element of H_n, and preserves the normalized filtration.
3. For g∈U_n(R), use the standard filtered torsor U_n,R with Frobenius φ_g(h)=g⁻¹φ(gh); its fixed point is g⁻¹ and its Hodge point 1, giving period \[g\].
4. Apply the finite central quotient to Kim Proposition 1 and verify scalar-extension naturality.

**Checks.**

- The twisted Frobenius satisfies φ_g(hk)=φ_g(h)φ(k); it is generally not a group homomorphism.
- The construction works on R=K\[ε\]/(ε²), not just reduced points.

#### 4.3. The finite-depth de Rham Albanese map

*Construction* `NC.4/local-albanese` · planet: **Unipotent Albanese map**

Proposed module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/ChabautyKim/Albanese`, namespace `TauCeti.ChabautyKim`.

Fix a smooth geometrically connected hyperbolic curve X/K, a smooth proper O_K-model X̄ with finite étale boundary D (possibly empty), the open model 𝒳=X̄∖D and b∈𝒳(O_K). Use U_n=U/Γ\_{n+1} for n≥1 and the right path torsor P_n(b,x) from b to x. Define localAlbanese_n:𝒳(O_K)→Q_n(K) by x↦admissiblePeriod(P_n(b,x)). The map is a p-adic analytic map on each residue disc, with local coordinates furnished by iterated Coleman integrals and an algebraic Hodge trivialization. It is not asserted to be a morphism of algebraic K-schemes. At b it equals \[1\]. Kim's U\_{n+1} is this U_n; Kim U_1 is trivial and Kim U_2 is our depth one.

**Hypotheses.**

- The base point is integral and the compactification and boundary have good reduction at the chosen p-adic place.
- NC.2 supplies the canonical Frobenius path and normalized Hodge reduction.
- For an arbitrary ramified K/ℚ_p, assume the endpoint-compatible rigid/de Rham and crystalline geometric comparisons for this model and these endpoints. The cited NC.2 berthelot-ogus and crystalline-path-coordinates nodes cover unramified models; finite-path-comparison extends only models and endpoints descending to that setup. General ramified-model comparison is requested explicitly, not inferred from coefficient extension.

**Construction.**

1. Push the NC.2 tensor path family to the n-th central quotient.
2. Apply admissible-classification fibrewise, independent of the chosen local Hodge section.
3. Use the word-path comparison of NC.2 and Coleman local expansions for discwise analyticity.

**API.**

- `localAlbanese_apply` (data): At x the map is admissiblePeriod of the two chosen paths in P_n(b,x).
- `localAlbanese_base` (simp): The normalized constant path at b gives localAlbanese_n(b)=\[1\].
- `localAlbanese_reindex` (functoriality): Reindexing the endpoint family along f:Y→𝒳(O_K) composes localAlbanese_n with f.
- `localAlbanese_hodge_change` (relation): A pointwise change p_H(x)↦p_H(x)h(x), with h(x)∈H_n(K), preserves the function.
- `localAlbanese_tower` (compatibility): For m≤n, the induced quotient q_nm satisfies q_nm∘localAlbanese_n=localAlbanese_m.

**Unit tests.**

- `localAlbanese_self_family` (degenerate): For every endpoint, if the Hodge and fixed paths coincide, the resulting family is constant \[1\].
- `localAlbanese_trivial_hodge` (computation): For the Uᵒᵖ self-torsor family indexed by g∈U, H={1}, p_φ(g)=1 and p_H(g)=op(g), the value at g is \[g\].
- `localAlbanese_fibre_change` (compatibility): For arbitrary h(x)∈H, the self-torsor endpoint family op(g(x)h(x)) gives the same map as op(g(x)).

**Checks.**

- The depth-zero extension is the constant map to a point; depth one is nontrivial.
- The base point maps to the neutral coset and higher-depth maps project to lower-depth maps.

**Uses.**

- Kim Theorem 1, p.93 and proof pp.111–114: Supplies the transcendental curve image in the period variety.
- NC.4 kim-loci and NC.5 quadratic height functions: Pulls local Selmer conditions and period equations back to local points.

#### 4.4. Iterated integrals as Albanese coordinates

*Comparison* `NC.4/iterated-coordinates`

Proposed module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/ChabautyKim/Albanese`, namespace `TauCeti.ChabautyKim`.

On an affine open of X_K choose the NC.2 universal connection and its algebraic trivialization g, and choose an algebraic Hodge trivialization p_H=gγ. Let p_φ(x)u(x)=g(x). Then localAlbanese_n(x) is the class of u(x)γ(x) in Q_n. In the NC.2 affine trivialization the Frobenius path has word element I(b,x), while g has coordinate 1; hence u=I(b,x)⁻¹ and the period representative is I(b,x)⁻¹γ(x). The coefficients of I are the imported Coleman iterated integrals; coefficients of I⁻¹ are their antipode combinations. Kim’s variable u in his proof must not be identified with NC.2’s forward path element without transporting the trivialization convention. In the convention dI\_{iw}=ω_i I_w, the first letter is the outermost integration, I\_∅=1, and the coefficients of uγ are ∑\_{w=ab}(I⁻¹)\_aγ_b, preserving multiplication order. On proper curves use the imported maximal extending quotient of an affine universal connection; do not treat all affine words as independent coordinates on the proper group. Regular functions on Q_n pull back to Coleman functions, analytic on every ordinary residue disc.

**Hypotheses.**

- Good-reduction datum of local-albanese; the affine trivializations and word-path identification are the NC.2 imported constructions.
- Only ordinary discs of 𝒳 are evaluated; logarithmic boundary germs are not added to the integral-point domain.

**Proof.**

1. Use the ordered torsor equation p_φuγ=p_H and the existing shuffle/deconcatenation word realization.
2. The Hodge factor γ is algebraic, so finite polynomial coordinate expressions are Coleman functions.
3. Pass from the affine group to the central quotient and to the proper extending quotient when required.

**Checks.**

- A bare list of single integrals cannot encode depth two.
- The empty coefficient is 1, and reversing factors u and γ changes noncommuting coordinates.

#### 4.5. Kim density on every residue disc

*Theorem* `NC.4/residue-disc-density` · planet: **Kim density theorem**

Proposed module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/ChabautyKim/Albanese`, namespace `TauCeti.ChabautyKim`.

For local-albanese's smooth hyperbolic good-reduction pair over a finite extension K/ℚ_p, n≥1, and every nonempty integral residue disc B⊆𝒳(O_K), the image localAlbanese_n(B) is Zariski dense in the geometrically integral affine K-variety Q_n. Equivalently any regular f∈O(Q_n) that vanishes on this whole disc is zero. The conclusion is K-Zariski density, not automatic ℚ_p-Zariski density in Res\_{K/ℚ_p}Q_n. Density is asserted separately on each disc, so a nonzero regular equation has nonzero analytic pullback on every disc.

**Hypotheses.**

- All good-reduction and integrality hypotheses of local-albanese.
- n≥1 in our indexing, corresponding to Kim n+1≥2; hyperbolicity means 2g−2+deg D&gt;0.

**Proof.**

1. Kim Lemma 4 proves the affine forward horizontal word coefficients independent over algebraic functions via complex monodromy and induction on word length.
2. For the group-like shuffle series, inversion sends a length-r word coefficient to (−1)^r times the reversed-word coefficient. Thus the inverse coefficients retain this independence. Right multiplication by the algebraic Hodge factor γ is unitriangular in word length, with γ_empty=1. Hence the corrected representative I⁻¹γ is dense in the affine group and its image in Q_n is dense.
3. Use the surjective proper extending quotient to pass from an auxiliary affine curve to the proper curve. Choose a finite étale boundary divisor avoiding the chosen disc; it need not be a K-rational point in a different disc. This repairs the unsupported point choice on Kim p.111 (E-NC4-4), and its integral chart interface is requested from L1.
4. On another nonempty disc choose an integral lift c. Canonical path composition gives I(b,x)=I(c,x)I(b,c); multiplication by the constant group-like factor, inversion and the algebraic Hodge correction preserve the triangular independence argument. This proves density for the original base point on every disc, rather than inferring it merely from global density.

**Checks.**

- At our depth one the image in Lie(J) is dense even if the local curve has analytic dimension one and g&gt;1.
- The ℚ_p-Weil restriction dimension cannot replace dim_K Q_n in a single-place argument without a stronger density/nonvanishing input.

### Crystalline periods and étale path classes

<a id="nc-4-crystalline-period"></a>

#### 4.6. The represented crystalline period map

*Construction* `NC.4/crystalline-period` · planet: **Crystalline period map**

Proposed module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/ChabautyKim/Albanese`, namespace `TauCeti.ChabautyKim`.

Let K/ℚ_p be finite and let L_n=H¹_f(G_K,U_n^et) be the represented finite-depth crystalline torsor functor of NC.3. The NC.2 filtered, Frobenius and multiplicative period comparisons send a crystalline torsor T over a ℚ_p-algebra R to an admissible de Rham U_n-torsor over K⊗\_{ℚ_p}R. Compose with admissible-classification to obtain a natural transformation D_n(R):L_n(R)→Q_n(K⊗R), and hence a morphism of ℚ_p-schemes crystallinePeriodMap_n:L_n→Res\_{K/ℚ_p}Q_n. On ℚ_p-points the target is Q_n(K). The neutral torsor maps to \[1\]. No inverse of D_n is asserted. Native affine reduction takes the resulting pullback d\*:O(Res Q_n)→O(L_n) and sends an R-point c to c∘d\*; deriving d\* from crystalline torsors remains part of the nonlinear supplier interface.

**Hypotheses.**

- Representability over all ℚ_p-algebras and coefficient-compatible crystalline conditions, as in NC.3.
- The nonlinear comparison respects multiplication, both path augmentations, torsor coactions, Hodge filtration and Frobenius; linear H¹ comparison alone is insufficient.
- For K≠ℚ_p the represented target is the Weil restriction, not Q_n as a ℚ_p-scheme by omission of its field.
- For an arbitrary ramified K/ℚ_p, assume the endpoint-compatible rigid/de Rham and crystalline geometric comparisons for this model and these endpoints. The cited NC.2 berthelot-ogus and crystalline-path-coordinates nodes cover unramified models; finite-path-comparison extends only models and endpoints descending to that setup. General ramified-model comparison is requested explicitly, not inferred from coefficient extension.

**Construction.**

1. Apply the nonlinear coordinate-period functor to each crystalline torsor, together with the finite coordinate filtrations.
2. Use admissible-classification over K⊗R.
3. Check naturality on coefficient rings; import the Weil restriction adjunction and apply represented-functor naturality to produce the scheme morphism.

**API.**

- `crystallinePeriodMap_apply` (data): On affine R-points, c is sent to c∘d\*, where d\* is the crystalline period pullback.
- `crystallinePeriodMap_coeff` (functoriality): For α:R→R′, α∘(c∘d\*)=(α∘c)∘d\*.
- `crystallinePeriodMap_neutral` (simp): Under compatible augmentations ε_L∘d\*=ε_Q, the neutral point maps to the neutral point.
- `crystallinePeriodMap_tower` (compatibility): The represented period morphism commutes with each finite-depth projection.
- `crystallinePeriodMap_ext` (extensionality): Equality of pullbacks is detected by all coefficient points, including the universal point of the affine source.

**Unit tests.**

- `crystallinePeriodMap_identity` (computation): For d\*=id_A and any R-point c:A→R, the point reduction sends c to c.
- `crystallinePeriodMap_universal` (characterisation): At R=O(L_n) and c=id, the point reduction returns d\* itself.
- `crystallinePeriodMap_dual_numbers` (non-example): For A=ℚ\[t\], R=ℚ\[ε\]/(ε²), d\*=id and c(t)=ε, the output still sends t to ε≠0. Passing to reduced points would give the wrong output.

**Checks.**

- Nilpotent coefficient maps are retained, and D_n commutes with depth projection.
- For K=ℚ_p no Weil restriction is needed; invertibility is not a prerequisite of the finiteness argument.

**Uses.**

- Kim §2, p.119 and §3, p.121: Turns global Selmer localization into algebraic period equations.
- NC.4 fundamental-diagram: Identifies the period of each local geometric path.

<a id="nc-4-local-etale-albanese"></a>

#### 4.7. The local étale path-class map

*Construction* `NC.4/local-etale-albanese`

Proposed module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/ChabautyKim/Albanese`, namespace `TauCeti.ChabautyKim`.

For the good-reduction datum of local-albanese, define localEtaleAlbanese_n(x)=\[P_n^et(b,x)\]∈H¹_f(G_K,U_n^et)(ℚ_p) for x∈𝒳(O_K). The right geometric étale path torsor has continuous G_K-action and its ind-coordinate ring is crystalline by the NC.2 nonlinear good-reduction comparison. The cocycle class is independent of a chosen geometric path used to express it. It is a class in a pointed set, not an element of a group at nonabelian depth. The base point gives the neutral class. The crystalline condition is proved for these geometric path torsors; it is not inferred from unrestricted extension-closure of crystalline representations.

**Hypotheses.**

- Integral endpoints and good smooth proper compactification with finite étale boundary.
- NC.2 nonlinear path comparison and NC.3 represented crystalline torsor interpretation.
- For an arbitrary ramified K/ℚ_p, assume the endpoint-compatible rigid/de Rham and crystalline geometric comparisons for this model and these endpoints. The cited NC.2 berthelot-ogus and crystalline-path-coordinates nodes cover unramified models; finite-path-comparison extends only models and endpoints descending to that setup. General ramified-model comparison is requested explicitly, not inferred from coefficient extension.

**Construction.**

1. Take the NC.2 finite geometric path torsor with restricted continuous G_K-action.
2. Apply the NC.3 torsor-to-cocycle comparison and quotient the full gauge action.
3. Use NC.2 crystalline path coordinates to place the class in the specified local subfunctor.

**API.**

- `localEtaleAlbanese_path` (characterisation): The class is the class of the actual right G_K-path torsor P_n^et(b,x).
- `localEtaleAlbanese_base` (simp): localEtaleAlbanese_n(b) is neutral.
- `localEtaleAlbanese_path_change` (relation): Expressing the same torsor through another geometric path gives the same gauge-orbit class.
- `localEtaleAlbanese_tower` (functoriality): Projecting U_n→U_m sends the class at x to localEtaleAlbanese_m(x).

**Unit tests.**

- `localEtaleAlbanese_base_test` (degenerate): At x=b the endpoint torsor contains the identity path fixed by G_K and gives the neutral class.
- `localEtaleAlbanese_kummer_test` (compatibility): For a proper curve at depth one, the class at x is the rational Tate-module Kummer class of AJ_b(x).
- `localEtaleAlbanese_gauge_test` (characterisation): If a path representative p is changed to p·a, the resulting cocycle is gauge equivalent and the output class is unchanged for every a, not just G_K-fixed a.

**Checks.**

- A change of geometric path changes a cocycle by the gauge action, not by naive addition of a coboundary.
- At depth one the map agrees with the rational p-adic Kummer class of x−b for a proper curve.

**Uses.**

- Kim §2, pp.119–120: Gives the local side of the global-to-local path diagram.
- NC.4 kim-loci: Defines the exact crystalline-image locus before passage through D_n.

<a id="nc-4-global-etale-albanese"></a>

#### 4.8. The global étale path-class map

*Construction* `NC.4/global-etale-albanese`

Proposed module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/ChabautyKim/Albanese`, namespace `TauCeti.ChabautyKim`.

Let F be a number field, R=O\_{F,S}, 𝒳/R a smooth hyperbolic curve with smooth proper compactification and finite étale boundary, and b∈𝒳(R). Fix p and T containing S and every p-adic place, and assume the NC.2 geometric G_F-actions on U_n^et and every permitted path torsor factor continuously through G\_{F,T}. For x∈𝒳(R), define globalEtaleAlbanese_n(x)=\[P_n^et(b,x)\]∈Sel_T(U_n)(ℚ_p), provided every chosen local condition contains the local path class of each permitted global point. In particular at the selected good place v∉S over p use the crystalline condition. Good places outside T have unramified path classes; additional bad-place conditions must be justified, not discarded. In the proper case take D empty, S containing bad reduction places, and 𝒳(R)=X(F) by properness. At b the map is neutral if all selected conditions contain the neutral path class.

**Hypotheses.**

- Integral global base point and chosen good place v∉S with completion K.
- T is finite. At each finite place outside T, inertia acts trivially on U_n^et and on every permitted geometric path torsor, giving actual continuous G\_{F,T}-actions. NC.2 etale-galois supplies G_F-actions but does not prove this factorization; the good-integral-model specialization theorem is requested from NC.2.
- Every imposed local condition is coefficient-stable and contains the geometric local classes relevant to 𝒳(R); Selmer representability is an additional input when the scheme is used.

**Construction.**

1. Take the geometric path with its continuous G_F-action and use the explicit inertia-triviality/factorization input to descend the group and torsor actions to G\_{F,T}. Good-model factorization is a separate supplier theorem, not a consequence of etale-galois alone.
2. Use NC.3 torsor comparison to form the nonabelian cohomology class.
3. Verify membership at all imposed local conditions; then factor through the existing Selmer functor.
4. For a proper curve apply the valuative criterion at the places outside S to identify the global domain.

**API.**

- `globalEtaleAlbanese_path` (characterisation): The underlying global cohomology class is the class of P_n^et(b,x).
- `globalEtaleAlbanese_base` (simp): The global base point gives the neutral class when that class obeys every local condition.
- `globalEtaleAlbanese_localize` (compatibility): At v, localization is localEtaleAlbanese_n of the image of x in 𝒳(O_K).
- `globalEtaleAlbanese_tower` (functoriality): Depth projection carries the global class to the corresponding lower-depth path class.
- `globalEtaleAlbanese_conditions` (characterisation): Membership in Sel_T is exactly membership of every localized path class in its imposed local subset.

**Unit tests.**

- `globalEtaleAlbanese_base_test` (degenerate): The identity path at b is globally fixed, so the output is the neutral Selmer point when admitted by the conditions.
- `globalEtaleAlbanese_kummer_test` (compatibility): For a proper curve at depth one, the underlying class is κ(AJ_b(x)) in the rational Tate-module Selmer space.
- `globalEtaleAlbanese_local_test` (characterisation): The selected p-adic localization of the global class of x equals the crystalline local path class of that same point, with the same base point.

**Checks.**

- Imposing an arbitrary bad-place condition need not preserve global-point containment.
- The claim concerns S-integral points for an open curve and rational points for a proper curve; it does not replace one by the other.

**Uses.**

- Kim diagram at the end of §2, p.120: Supplies the Selmer point witnessing membership of every global point in the local locus.
- NC.4 rational-integral-containment: Preserves all stated bad-place hypotheses in the containment theorem.

- [`NC.3/selmer-representability`](#nc-3-selmer-representability) Selmer representability

#### 4.9. The global Selmer period morphism

*Construction* `NC.4/selmer-period`

Proposed module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/ChabautyKim/Albanese`, namespace `TauCeti.ChabautyKim`.

For the NC.3 represented finite-type global Selmer scheme S_n and local crystalline scheme L_n at the chosen good p-adic place K, let loc_n:S_n→L_n be the supplied localization morphism. Define selmerPeriod_n=crystallinePeriodMap_n∘loc_n:S_n→Res\_{K/ℚ_p}Q_n as a morphism of ℚ_p-schemes. At K=ℚ_p its target is Q_n. At ℚ_p-points it evaluates localization followed by the crystalline period; its scheme-theoretic image and Zariski closure are taken using the full morphism, not the set of ℚ_p-rational source points. For K≠ℚ_p its base change followed by the Weil-restriction counit gives an auxiliary K-morphism (S_n)\_K→Q_n; this is only used with the corresponding K-dimension bound and geometric image closure.

**Hypotheses.**

- All NC.3 representability and local-condition hypotheses, and crystalline-period hypotheses.
- Localization lands in the crystalline scheme at the selected place.

**Construction.**

1. Import localization rather than reconstructing continuous cohomology or the Selmer scheme.
2. Compose the represented morphisms; at a test algebra the Yoneda map is composition with the same morphism.
3. Use the imported Weil restriction counit for the auxiliary K-morphism if needed.

**API.**

- `selmerPeriod_def` (characterisation): The morphism is loc_n followed by D_n.
- `selmerPeriod_point` (data): For a coefficient point s, its image is D_n(loc_n(s)).
- `selmerPeriod_precompose` (functoriality): Precomposing a source-point map commutes with evaluation of the composite.
- `selmerPeriod_tower` (compatibility): The period morphisms commute with condition-preserving depth projections.
- `selmerPeriod_neutral` (simp): Compatible neutral points are carried to the neutral period.

**Unit tests.**

- `selmerPeriod_identity_local` (degenerate): If D is the identity morphism, selmerPeriod(loc,D)=loc.
- `selmerPeriod_identity_global` (degenerate): If loc is the identity morphism, selmerPeriod(loc,D)=D.
- `selmerPeriod_point_associativity` (compatibility): For every actual test-object point s:B→S, s followed by selmerPeriod equals (s followed by loc) followed by D.

**Checks.**

- The composite has a source and target over the same coefficient field.
- The construction retains all global local conditions and does not identify Selmer points with rational curve points.

**Uses.**

- Kim §3, pp.120–121: Its geometric image supplies the annihilating regular equation.
- NC.4 kim-loci: Its rational point image defines the de Rham locus.

**Needs.**

- [`NC.4/crystalline-period`](#nc-4-crystalline-period) The represented crystalline period map
- [`NC.3/selmer-localization-naturality`](#nc-3-selmer-localization-naturality) Localization and depth functoriality

#### 4.10. Compatibility of global paths, localization and periods

*Comparison* `NC.4/fundamental-diagram`

Proposed module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/ChabautyKim/Albanese`, namespace `TauCeti.ChabautyKim`.

For every x∈𝒳(R) satisfying global-etale-albanese's hypotheses, write ι_v(x)∈𝒳(O_K) for its local image. Then loc_n(globalEtaleAlbanese_n(x))=localEtaleAlbanese_n(ι_v(x)), crystallinePeriodMap_n(localEtaleAlbanese_n(y))=localAlbanese_n(y) for all y∈𝒳(O_K), and consequently selmerPeriod_n(globalEtaleAlbanese_n(x))=localAlbanese_n(ι_v(x)), interpreting Res\_{K/ℚ_p}Q_n(ℚ_p)=Q_n(K). These equalities commute with depth projection and coefficient extension wherever defined. No assertion that every local point is global, or that D_n is invertible, is included.

**Hypotheses.**

- The same curve, base point, central quotient and good place are used in all four maps.
- The nonlinear comparison respects the two endpoint augmentations, filtrations, torsor structures and Frobenius.
- For an arbitrary ramified K/ℚ_p, assume the endpoint-compatible rigid/de Rham and crystalline geometric comparisons for this model and these endpoints. The cited NC.2 berthelot-ogus and crystalline-path-coordinates nodes cover unramified models; finite-path-comparison extends only models and endpoints descending to that setup. General ramified-model comparison is requested explicitly, not inferred from coefficient extension.

**Proof.**

1. Restrict the global path Galois action to G_K to get the local path torsor, and use the naturality of NC.3 H¹ restriction.
2. Identify the period functor of the étale path with its geometric de Rham path by the imported NC.2 multiplicative comparison.
3. Apply admissible-classification, then compose localization and D_n.

**Checks.**

- At depth one it is the Kummer/logarithm diagram for AJ_b.
- The same nonabelian gauge-orbit class is used before and after restriction.

<a id="nc4-loci"></a>

### Chabauty–Kim loci and finiteness

<a id="nc-4-kim-loci"></a>

#### 4.11. The exact, period-image and closed-image loci

*Definition* `NC.4/kim-loci` · planet: **Chabauty–Kim locus**

Proposed module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/ChabautyKim/Albanese`, namespace `TauCeti.ChabautyKim`.

Put Y=𝒳(O_K), j_n=localAlbanese_n, j_n^et=localEtaleAlbanese_n, and ℓ_n=selmerPeriod_n on ℚ_p-points (interpreted in Q_n(K)). Define crystallineLocus_n={y∈Y:∃s∈S_n(ℚ_p), loc_n(s)=j_n^et(y)} and deRhamLocus_n={y∈Y:∃s∈S_n(ℚ_p), ℓ_n(s)=j_n(y)}. Let Z_n be the reduced Zariski closure of the geometric image of the full scheme morphism ℓ_n in Res\_{K/ℚ_p}Q_n; define closedDeRhamLocus_n={y∈Y:j_n(y)∈Z_n(ℚ_p)}. Then crystallineLocus_n⊆deRhamLocus_n⊆closedDeRhamLocus_n. The first inclusion uses the fundamental-diagram; equality requires a separate saturation/injectivity property of D_n. The second inclusion need not be equality: taking the geometric image closure does not promise a ℚ_p-rational Selmer lift. For a K-valued auxiliary morphism use its own geometric image closure and call the resulting enlarged locus by that morphism, not by an unexplained change of scalars. Native set reductions take the supplied maps between actual point carriers, and for the closed locus the supplied point subset Z_n(ℚ_p); computing that subset from the scheme morphism is a separate geometric interface.

**Hypotheses.**

- The same domains, coefficient points, local conditions and good place are used in all maps.
- Z_n is the closure of the scheme image, not the p-adic closure and not merely the closure of rational source points.

**Construction.**

1. Define the two inverse images of set-theoretic point images.
2. Import the closed reduced subscheme attached to the scheme-image closure for the third definition.
3. Apply the commutative comparison triangle and the inclusion of each source-point image in the geometric image closure.

**API.**

- `crystallineLocus_mem` (characterisation): y belongs iff its actual crystalline class has a ℚ_p-rational global Selmer lift.
- `deRhamLocus_mem` (characterisation): y belongs iff its actual de Rham period has a ℚ_p-rational Selmer preimage under ℓ_n.
- `closedDeRhamLocus_mem` (characterisation): y belongs iff its period lies in the point subset of the geometric image closure.
- `kimLoci_inclusions` (relation): Under D_n∘j_n^et=j_n, the three loci are included in order.
- `deRhamLocus_mono` (functoriality): Enlarging the supplied global period image enlarges its inverse-image locus.
- `kimLoci_ext` (extensionality): Equality of supplied point maps, images and closed-image point subsets gives equality of the corresponding loci.

**Unit tests.**

- `kimLoci_identity` (degenerate): For any point map j:Y→Q and global period map id_Q, deRhamLocus(j,id)=Y.
- `kimLoci_empty_source` (degenerate): For an empty global point carrier, deRhamLocus is empty, regardless of the local point map.
- `kimLoci_square_image` (non-example): On ℚ-points of A¹ let ℓ(u)=u² and j(t)=t. The point −1 is absent from the image locus but belongs to the closed-image locus since the geometric scheme image is dense in A¹. This tests the image/closure distinction, not the p-adic topology.

**Checks.**

- These are sets of local points, not sets of de Rham periods; no injectivity of j_n is assumed.
- A positive-dimensional or all-target closed image alone supplies no finiteness.

**Uses.**

- Kim §3, p.121: These are the local candidate sets to which the analytic finiteness argument applies.
- NC.5 quadratic Chabauty and ED.6 certified candidates: Height equations cut out a computable enlargement and need the same distinction between containment and equality.

**Needs.**

- [`NC.4/fundamental-diagram`](#nc-4-fundamental-diagram) Compatibility of global paths, localization and periods
- [`NC.4/selmer-period`](#nc-4-selmer-period) The global Selmer period morphism

**Sources.**

- [Kim09](#src-kim09), §3, intersection description p.121; diagram pp.95 and 120: The source traps global periods in the intersection with the Selmer image. The three inverse-image definitions make explicit the two enlargements used in that argument.

<a id="nc-4-locus-compatibilities"></a>

#### 4.12. Depth projection and change of conditions for the loci

*Theorem* `NC.4/locus-compatibilities`

Proposed module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/ChabautyKim/Albanese`, namespace `TauCeti.ChabautyKim`.

For m≤n suppose the quotient U_n→U_m induces maps S_n→S_m, L_n→L_m and Q_n→Q_m preserving every chosen local condition and commuting with the local and global period diagrams. Then crystallineLocus_n⊆crystallineLocus_m and deRhamLocus_n⊆deRhamLocus_m; the corresponding closed-image loci are nested because the continuous algebraic quotient maps carry the higher geometric image closure into the lower one. For two systems of conditions on the same global functor, inclusion C_v⊆C′\_v at every place gives inclusion of all three loci from the more restrictive to the less restrictive system. At fixed depth, if D_n is injective on local crystalline ℚ_p-points, then crystallineLocus_n=deRhamLocus_n; more generally equality follows if the localization image is saturated under D_n on the local geometric classes. No unconditional equality with the closed-image locus or with the rational point set is asserted.

**Hypotheses.**

- Represented diagram maps exist and preserve the specified local conditions.
- For the last assertion, injectivity or the stated saturation is an additional hypothesis.

**Proof.**

1. Project a Selmer-point witness and use diagram commutativity for the image loci.
2. For the closed-image locus, continuity sends a point of a closure into the closure of the target image.
3. For equality of crystalline and period loci, pull a D_n equality back using injectivity or saturation.

**Checks.**

- The decreasing tower is an inclusion of local-point sets even though every j_n is generally many-to-one.
- Dropping a local condition enlarges the locus; it cannot provide a stronger containment bound.

**Needs.**

- [`NC.4/kim-loci`](#nc-4-kim-loci) The exact, period-image and closed-image loci
- [`NC.3/selmer-localization-naturality`](#nc-3-selmer-localization-naturality) Localization and depth functoriality
- [`NC.2/central-quotients`](#nc-2-central-quotients) Lower central depth
- `SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0`

**Sources.**

- [Kim09](#src-kim09), Finite-depth diagrams pp.93 and 120, and Selmer conditions p.95: The source’s compatible tower and point images imply the stated functorial inclusions; the equality criterion is a direct consequence with its additional hypothesis.

<a id="nc-4-rational-integral-containment"></a>

#### 4.13. Global points lie in the Chabauty–Kim loci

*Theorem* `NC.4/rational-integral-containment`

Proposed module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/ChabautyKim/Albanese`, namespace `TauCeti.ChabautyKim`.

In the global good-reduction datum, with all imposed local conditions verified on every allowed geometric path, ι_v(𝒳(R))⊆crystallineLocus_n⊆deRhamLocus_n⊆closedDeRhamLocus_n for every n≥1. In the proper case the first term is the image of X(F). This supplies a global Selmer witness for each integral or rational point. If a locus is finite, so is the global domain, since the field inclusion F→K induces an injective map on points of the F-scheme X. The theorem claims neither the reverse containment nor equality of the intersection with the global set.

**Hypotheses.**

- All hypotheses of global-etale-albanese and fundamental-diagram, including all bad-place local conditions.
- For the final implication use the faithful field inclusion; it does not require injectivity of the Albanese map.

**Proof.**

1. For x∈𝒳(R), globalEtaleAlbanese_n(x) is the required Selmer witness and its localization equals the local class.
2. Apply kim-loci inclusions.
3. Use injectivity of scalar extension along F→K on rational points to pull back a finite local-point set.

**Checks.**

- For a proper curve the statement bounds every rational point, including those outside an arbitrary chosen affine patch.
- For an open curve it bounds only the selected S-integral domain.

<a id="nc-4-regular-pullback"></a>

#### 4.14. Pullback of regular period functions

*Construction* `NC.4/regular-pullback`

Proposed module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/ChabautyKim/Albanese`, namespace `TauCeti.ChabautyKim`.

For A_n=O(Q_n) and Y=𝒳(O_K), define regularAlbanesePullback_n:A_n→(Y→K) by f↦(y↦f(j_n(y))). It is a K-algebra homomorphism, and iterated-coordinates shows its image consists of the corresponding Coleman functions on ordinary integral discs. The algebra-valued refinement targets the imported Coleman function algebra once its native carrier and the geometric evaluation bridge are available; the function-valued map itself is fully expressible on K-points viewed as K-algebra homomorphisms A_n→K. Disc-density implies that restriction of this map to any nonempty residue disc is injective. If f vanishes on the global Selmer geometric image closure, its pullback vanishes on the de Rham and closed-image loci, and hence on allowed global points.

**Hypotheses.**

- The period variety is affine and geometrically integral over K; use the geometric K-variant of the image closure if K≠ℚ_p.
- Local point evaluation and Coleman membership follow the NC.2/L1 word-path convention.

**Construction.**

1. Compose actual algebra-valued K-points with the coordinate algebra element f, preserving sums, products, constants and one.
2. Apply iterated-coordinates for Coleman membership.
3. Apply residue-disc-density for injectivity and kim-loci definitions for the vanishing claim.

**API.**

- `regularAlbanesePullback_apply` (data): For an actual K-point j(y):A_n→K, the value at y is j(y)(f).
- `regularAlbanesePullback_add` (simp): Pullback of f+g is the sum of the two pullbacks.
- `regularAlbanesePullback_mul` (simp): Pullback of fg is the product of the two pullbacks.
- `regularAlbanesePullback_const` (compatibility): A scalar r∈K pulls back to the constant function r.
- `regularAlbanesePullback_reindex` (functoriality): Reindexing local points along a map composes each pulled-back function with that map.
- `regularAlbanesePullback_injective_disc` (characterisation): If j(B) is K-Zariski dense, pullback to B is injective.

**Unit tests.**

- `regularAlbanesePullback_affine_coordinate` (computation): For A=K\[t\], Y=K and j(a) evaluation at a, the pullback of t at a is a.
- `regularAlbanesePullback_product_test` (computation): For the same family, the pullback of t(t+1) at a is a(a+1), so an additive-only substitute fails.
- `regularAlbanesePullback_unit_test` (non-example): For that family over a nontrivial field, pullback of 1 is the nonzero constant 1, including at a=0; a derivative or normalized primitive is not this map.

**Checks.**

- A nonzero regular f cannot pull back to the zero function on an entire nonempty residue disc.
- Individual vanishing values are allowed; injectivity is not injectivity of j_n on points.

**Uses.**

- Kim §3, p.121: Creates the nonzero scalar analytic function whose zero set bounds the local locus.

<a id="nc-4-selmer-annihilator"></a>

#### 4.15. A regular equation from a small Selmer image

*Theorem* `NC.4/selmer-annihilator`

Proposed module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/ChabautyKim/Albanese`, namespace `TauCeti.ChabautyKim`.

Let k be a characteristic-zero field, S a finite-type affine k-scheme, Q a geometrically integral affine finite-type k-scheme, and ℓ:S→Q a k-morphism. Let Z be the reduced closed subscheme whose underlying set is the closure of the geometric image of ℓ. If dim S&lt;dim Q, then dim Z≤dim S, Z≠Q, and there exists a nonzero f∈O(Q) vanishing on Z. The same conclusion holds under the weaker hypothesis dim Z&lt;dim Q. Here dimensions are Krull dimensions of schemes, not vector-space ranks of their coordinate rings. Nilpotents of S are retained in ℓ but do not enlarge the topological image; f need only vanish on the reduced closure, not pull back to zero on a nonreduced S. For S empty take Z empty and f=1. At k=ℚ_p, apply this to selmerPeriod_n. For K≠ℚ_p one may apply it instead to the auxiliary K-morphism (S_n)\_K→Q_n under dim\_{ℚ_p}S_n&lt;dim_K Q_n; merely having dim S_n&lt;dim Res Q_n does not give this conclusion in Q_n.

**Hypotheses.**

- Finite type is required for the image dimension bound; Q is integral and affine for a nonzero global regular equation.
- All dimensions and the image morphism are over the same stated field.

**Proof.**

1. For each irreducible component of the reduced source, use the generic fibre dimension formula to bound the dimension of its image closure.
2. Take the finite union of component image closures; strict inequality makes it proper.
3. A proper reduced closed subscheme of an affine integral scheme has a nonzero defining ideal; choose f in that ideal.
4. For the K-variant use the Weil restriction counit and invariance of source dimension under field extension.

**Checks.**

- For ℓ:A¹→A¹ given by u↦u², dimensions are equal and Z=Q, so the theorem supplies no equation even though many k-points have no lift.
- For a constant map into A², a coordinate vanishing at the image point is a possible nonzero f.

<a id="nc-4-finite-annihilator-locus"></a>

#### 4.16. Finiteness under discwise nonvanishing

*Theorem* `NC.4/finite-annihilator-locus`

Proposed module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/ChabautyKim/Albanese`, namespace `TauCeti.ChabautyKim`.

Let K/ℚ_p be finite and let Y=𝒳(O_K) be the integral tube in a smooth proper good-reduction compactification with finite étale boundary removed. Let j:Y→Q(K) have Coleman-analytic regular-function pullbacks on each ordinary residue disc. If Z⊊Q is a closed subset and some f∈O(Q), f≠0, vanishes on Z and f∘j is not identically zero on each nonempty integral residue disc, then {y∈Y:j(y)∈Z(K)} is finite. In particular the image-defined locus contained in that set is finite. Every disc has K-points parametrized by m_K=πO_K; the pullback on the open geometric disc has a convergent power series, and substituting t=πs produces a nonzero restricted series on the compact closed unit disc O_K. Strassmann then gives finitely many zeros in each disc, and there are finitely many residue discs. The statement supplies finiteness, not an effective uniform bound or equality with global points.

**Hypotheses.**

- Finite extension K is essential for compactness and a finite residue field; the full C_p-disc is not the domain.
- The local functions are analytic on the whole ordinary open geometric residue disc and nonzero on each integral disc.
- Only integral discs disjoint from the removed boundary are used; no open punctured-disc compactness assertion is made.

**Proof.**

1. Use the existing good-reduction residue-disc parameterization from L1 and the finiteness of 𝒳(k).
2. Rescale t=πs: convergence at a real radius strictly between \|π\| and 1 implies the rescaled coefficients tend to zero.
3. Use the ED.4 Strassmann theorem on each nonzero rescaled series.
4. Take a finite union of finite zero sets, then its subset cut out by Z.

**Checks.**

- If f∘j vanishes identically on one disc, that disc may remain wholly in the locus and the criterion does not apply.
- An arbitrary nonzero function analytic only on an open disc need not have finitely many zeros throughout that geometric disc.

**Needs.**

- [`NC.4/regular-pullback`](#nc-4-regular-pullback) Pullback of regular period functions
- `ColemanIntegration:L1/residue-disc-parametrisation`
- `ColemanIntegration:L1/word-algebra-local-expansion`
- `EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.4/strassmann-bound`
- `ColemanIntegration:L1`

**Used by.** [`NC.4/dimension-finiteness`](#nc-4-dimension-finiteness).

**Sources.**

- [Kim09](#src-kim09), §3, the Coleman-function zero-set argument, p.121: Kim bounds the integral local set by zeros on finitely many residue discs. The rescaling specifies the compact domain needed to apply the imported Strassmann theorem.

<a id="nc-4-dimension-finiteness"></a>

#### 4.17. Conditional Chabauty–Kim finiteness

*Theorem* `NC.4/dimension-finiteness` · planet: **Chabauty–Kim finiteness criterion**

Proposed module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/ChabautyKim/Albanese`, namespace `TauCeti.ChabautyKim`.

Let X/ℚ be smooth geometrically connected hyperbolic, with integral global base point b and the good models, ramification set and local conditions of global-etale-albanese. Choose p∉S and depth n≥1. Assume the NC.3 global Selmer functor is represented by a finite-type affine scheme S_n and the crystalline comparison gives the morphism ℓ_n:S_n→Q_n at K=ℚ_p. If dim S_n&lt;dim Q_n, then closedDeRhamLocus_n, deRhamLocus_n and crystallineLocus_n are finite, and consequently 𝒳(ℤ\[S⁻¹\]) is finite. If X is proper, X(ℚ) is finite. One may replace the inequality by a proper geometric image closure together with a nonzero regular annihilator; Kim discwise density supplies the needed nonvanishing. No assertion that a depth satisfying the inequality exists is included: Kim Conjecture 1 and motivic conjectural dimension inputs remain hypotheses, not theorems of NC.4. For a number field F, use finite-annihilator-locus with its explicit K-nonvanishing hypothesis, or the auxiliary K-morphism bound dim S_n&lt;dim_K Q_n; a bound against dim\_{ℚ_p}Res Q_n alone is insufficient without stronger Weil-restriction discwise density.

**Hypotheses.**

- All local conditions contain the allowed global path classes, including bad places.
- The nonlinear comparison and representability inputs are supplied; they remain imported plans with their recorded gaps.
- The strict dimension inequality is a verified or assumed mathematical input, never silently concluded from the theorem.

**Proof.**

1. Use selmer-annihilator to choose a nonzero regular equation for the geometric Selmer period image closure.
2. Use residue-disc-density and regular-pullback to obtain a nonzero analytic function on every integral disc.
3. Apply finite-annihilator-locus and the three locus inclusions.
4. Use rational-integral-containment and the injective field embedding to deduce global finiteness.

**Checks.**

- For a proper genus-g curve at depth one the target has dimension g; the source dimension is a Selmer dimension, not automatically the Mordell–Weil rank.
- The statement applies even when the period map itself is not injective.

#### 4.18. The depth-one Albanese and abelian logarithm

*Comparison* `NC.4/depth-one-period`

Proposed module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/ChabautyKim/Albanese`, namespace `TauCeti.ChabautyKim`.

For a proper smooth geometrically connected genus-g curve X/ℚ with b∈X(ℚ) and good reduction at p, use NC.2's abelianization U_1^et=V_pJ and the filtered de Rham identification U_1^dR=H¹_dR(X/ℚ_p)^∨, H_1=Ann(H⁰(X,Ω¹)), Q_1≃Lie(J). With the Lie identification normalized to the endpoint Kummer/Abel–Jacobi comparison, the local crystalline path class is κ_p(AJ_b(x)) and the identified de Rham period is log_J(AJ_b(x)). Pairing with ω∈H⁰(X,Ω¹) gives the single Coleman integral ∫\_b^xω. Fix the convention explicitly: in NC.2's universal connection d−∑T_iω_i the forward Frobenius path has coefficient +I_i; our torsor ratio has representative I⁻¹γ, so its raw first-level coordinate is γ_i−I_i. The Lie comparison sends the raw quotient coordinate with the compensating sign to the usual logarithm; it does not identify +I_i with that raw torsor ratio. This sign normalization leaves linear-subspace loci unchanged. For an open curve the generalized Jacobian/boundary contribution is a separate input, and is not identified with the proper Jacobian in this node.

**Hypotheses.**

- Proper curve and NC.2's de Rham H¹/Hodge–Abel–Jacobi bridge; good-reduction rational Tate-module comparison.
- Use the same path direction b→x and the displayed ratio convention in every realization.

**Proof.**

1. Import the NC.2 depth-one group and cohomology bridge; do not reconstruct J, the Tate module or the Hodge exact sequence.
2. Use the NC.3 depth-one comparison for the actual Kummer class.
3. Use ED.4’s abelian logarithm and Coleman/abelian integral comparison, transporting the raw coordinate sign through the normalized Lie identification.

**Checks.**

- Depth one here is Kim U_2, and Q_1 has dimension g; depth zero is trivial.
- For x=b every pairing is zero; for a differential the derivative of the paired period is ω, with the above sign normalization.

#### 4.19. The precise classical Chabauty comparison

*Comparison* `NC.4/depth-one-locus`

Proposed module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/ChabautyKim/Albanese`, namespace `TauCeti.ChabautyKim`.

In depth-one-period's proper setting, let W_S⊆Lie(J)(ℚ_p) be the image of the linear global Selmer space under the normalized logarithmic period map, and W_MW=span\_{ℚ_p}{log_J(P):P∈J(ℚ)}. The de Rham image locus at depth one is {x∈X(ℚ_p):log_J(AJ_b(x))∈W_S}, equivalently the common zero set of ∫\_b^xω for all linear forms ω∈Ann(W_S). The image is already a closed linear subspace, so its period-image and geometric-closed-image loci coincide in this linear setting. For the usual local conditions the Mordell–Weil Kummer map lies in the Selmer space, giving W_MW⊆W_S; if additional conditions are imposed, this containment must be an explicit hypothesis. The classical common-annihilator Chabauty locus is obtained by replacing W_S with W_MW, and is a subset of the Selmer locus under that containment. If W_S=W_MW, the two loci agree. A rank bound rank J(ℚ)&lt;g gives dim W_MW&lt;g and classical finiteness by the imported ED.4 theory, but gives finiteness of the full depth-one Selmer locus only with dim W_S&lt;g (e.g. W_S=W_MW). No vanishing of a Tate–Shafarevich contribution or equality Selmer=Mordell–Weil is assumed without a stated extra input. The common-annihilator locus is logarithmically saturated; it is not asserted equal to AJ_b⁻¹ of the literal topological closure of J(ℚ).

**Hypotheses.**

- All depth-one-period hypotheses; the represented depth-one Selmer space and period map are linear over ℚ_p.
- Containment of the whole Mordell–Weil Kummer image is needed when comparing its classical locus with a refined Selmer locus.
- Equality of the two period subspaces is a separate hypothesis.

**Proof.**

1. Import the linear rational Tate-module Selmer and Kummer comparison from NC.3.
2. Identify the first de Rham map with the logarithm by depth-one-period.
3. Use the baseline double-annihilator identity to express membership in W_S by all annihilating linear forms.
4. Use ED.4 annihilating differentials and residue-disc zero bounds for classical finiteness; retain the separate Selmer dimension input.

**Checks.**

- If W_S=Lie(J) and W_MW is proper, the full Selmer locus is X(ℚ_p) while the classical locus can be finite.
- For W=0 the period-image locus is the zero logarithm fibre; for W=Lie(J) it is the whole local curve.
- The annihilator formulation preserves constants of integration through the same global base point b.

<a id="layer-nc-5"></a>

## NC.5. Quadratic Chabauty and height equations

This layer produces finite p-adic height loci containing the rational points of a proper curve over ℚ. Its two principal results are the rank criterion r &lt; g + ρ_ℚ − 1 for finiteness of the depth-two Chabauty–Kim locus and, when r = g and the logarithm of the Mordell–Weil group is an isomorphism, the construction of quadratic Chabauty pairs and their basis-certified determinant equations.

**Objects.** X/ℚ is smooth, projective and geometrically connected of genus g > 1 with a rational point b, J is its Jacobian and p a prime of good reduction. Put V = V_pJ, H = H¹_dR(X/ℚ_p) and W = H⁰(X_{ℚ_p}, Ω¹)*. The arithmetic invariant is ρ_ℚ = rank NS(J/ℚ) of rationally defined classes, never the geometric Picard number. A nice correspondence is a rational divisor class Z on X × X, symmetric up to the two pullback subspaces, whose H¹ ⊗ H¹ Künneth component is nonzero and whose endomorphism of H¹ has trace zero. Its cup-zero alternating class gives a Galois-equivariant surjection from the central graded piece of the depth-two group onto ℚ_p(1), and so the height quotient U_Z, a central extension of V by ℚ_p(1). Its universal module of augmentation length two is A/I³; length and lower central depth are separate indices.

**Heights.** Every height uses one continuous idele-class character with nonzero p-component and a chosen Hodge splitting, with h = h_p + Σ_{v≠p} h_v. The local height at p is a function of the Frobenius and Hodge data of the twisted height module; away from p the local heights take finitely many values, which vanish at potentially good primes. The away-place correction set is the negative sum Υ = {−Σ t_v} (the sign of source correction E504). A quadratic Chabauty pair is a function θ on X(ℚ_p) with data (Υ, E, c, B) such that on every residue disc (AJ_b, θ) is given by convergent power series and is Zariski dense on every nonempty open subdisc, and θ(x) − B(AJ_b(x), E·AJ_b(x) + c) lies in Υ for every rational point x; the residual height locus is then a finite set containing X(ℚ). The determinant criterion turns the pair into explicit equations, valid only when the chosen feature vectors form a certified basis.

**The worked consumer.** The split Cartan curve X_s(13) is the consumer of this layer, owned by EffectiveDiophantineMethods ED.6, which plans its model, rank, Hecke classes, height matrices and the complete point computation. The published result (BDMTV19, Theorem 1.1, p. 886) is that its monic quartic model has exactly seven rational points. The data: p = 17, g = r = ρ_ℚ = 3, real multiplication by the cubic field ℚ(α), α³ + 2α² − α − 1 = 0; two nice classes from the Hecke correspondences T₇ and T₁₁; twenty residue discs of the smooth F₁₇-points. The supplementary code passes the wrong Hodge vector to one tensor helper at the exceptional disc (source correction E507), so ED.6 must replay that disc with the corrected vector and full root certificates. This layer creates no worked-curve node and no reverse dependency on ED.6.

**Ownership.** AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A2 and A6 supply Néron–Severi, its injection into symmetric Hom and its rank, and the Rosati involution; NC.2 the finite path groups and modules, the crystalline comparison and the depth-one identification; NC.3 the torsors, twisting, central extensions and the exact sequence for a closed embedding; NC.4 the Selmer varieties with a Mordell–Weil cut and the finiteness machinery; SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0, L2 and L4 the Kummer and local conditions; PadicHodgeTheory R06.2 and R06.5 D_cris and the comparison for H¹; ColemanIntegration L1 Coleman integrals; MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles MC.0 correspondences; HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions RP.1 the Mordell–Weil theorem and the Kummer map. Generic mixed extensions and p-adic heights have no stage yet; their contract is recorded as an open obligation of this layer, and no stage identifier is invented for them.

The planets are the Nice correspondence, the Quadratic Chabauty rank criterion, the Depth-two height module, the Quadratic Chabauty pair and the Quadratic Chabauty determinant.

### Rational classes and the rank obstruction

<a id="nc-5-nice-correspondence"></a>

#### 5.1. Nice rational correspondence

*Definition* `NC.5/nice-correspondence` · planet: **Nice correspondence**

Proposed module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/Chabauty/Quadratic`, namespace `TauCetiRoadmap.AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty.NC5`.

Let X/Q be smooth, proper and geometrically connected, of genus g&gt;1, with b in X(Q). In C=Pic(X×X)⊗Q let P be the sum of the two pullback subspaces. A correspondence Z is nice when swap\*Z−Z belongs to P, its H1⊗H1 Kunneth component cl(Z) is nonzero, and the induced endomorphism E_Z of H1 has trace zero. Nontrivial means nonzero in this component, not merely a nonzero divisor or Picard class. The same predicate applies after scalar extension, but a p-adic class is not thereby a rational correspondence.

**Hypotheses.**

- The Kunneth cycle-class map, correspondence action and principal polarization come from their geometric owners.
- Rational coefficients permit subtracting the scalar trace part.

**Construction.**

1. Form the pullback subspace in the rational Picard group and impose symmetry in its quotient.
2. Extract the H1⊗H1 component; impose its nonvanishing and trace zero. On supplied native modules the three conditions are an explicit predicate.

**API.**

- `IsNiceCorrespondence.nonzero` (relation): A nice class is nonzero.
- `IsNiceCorrespondence.smul` (compatibility): Multiplication by a nonzero coefficient preserves niceness.
- `IsNiceCorrespondence.add_pullback` (compatibility): Adding d in the pullback subspace preserves niceness when swap(d)−d stays in that subspace and both trace and cl vanish on it.

**Unit tests.**

- `nice_nonzero_primitive` (computation): For C=Q², P=0, swap=id, trace=first coordinate and cl=second coordinate, (0,1) is nice.
- `nice_nonzero_trace` (non-example): With these data (1,1) is not nice.
- `nice_zero_class` (non-example): For trace=0 and cl=second coordinate, the nonzero element (1,0) is not nice.

**Checks.**

- Zero and a nonzero pullback class cannot be nice.
- Symmetry modulo pullbacks is distinct from equality of divisors under swapping.

**Uses.**

- BDMTV §2.3: Selects a nonzero primitive rational cycle for a one-dimensional central quotient.
- NC.5 worked curve: Distinguishes certified rational Hecke correspondences from arbitrary p-adic Tate classes.

**Lean boundary.** Native linear predicate and its three API items/tests are present. Pic(X×X), cycle action and the geometric instantiation IsNiceCorrespondence.geometric are omitted at G1.

**Waits for.** [G501](#gap-anabeliangeometryandnonabelianchabauty-g501).

**Needs.**

- `AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A2/abelian-neron-severi`
- `MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles:MC.0`
- `LinearMap.ker` (Mathlib)

**Used by.** [`NC.5/nice-trace-criterion`](#nc-5-nice-trace-criterion); [`NC.5/depth-two-quotient`](#nc-5-depth-two-quotient).

<a id="nc-5-nice-trace-criterion"></a>

#### 5.2. Primitive class and trace criterion

*Theorem* `NC.5/nice-trace-criterion`

Proposed module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/Chabauty/Quadratic`, namespace `TauCetiRoadmap.AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty.NC5`.

For a symmetric rational correspondence Z on X whose Jacobian is absolutely simple, its Kunneth tensor is alternating (with the graded Kunneth sign). Its cup product is zero exactly when E_Z has trace zero, under the trace H2(X)(1)≅coefficient field. Consequently Z is nice exactly when cl(Z) is nonzero and cup(cl(Z))=0. The nonzero qualification is essential; the zero correspondence satisfies the latter equation alone.

**Hypotheses.**

- X and the polarization as in nice-correspondence.
- Use the duality conventions of H1 and V=H1_et(Xbar,Qp)\*, with their Tate twist.

**Proof.**

1. Import the rational NS-to-Rosati-symmetric-Hom identification from A2; the alternating tensor is its cohomological realization.
2. The correspondence trace equals cup followed by H2 trace. Combine with the explicit nonzero condition; do not use the unqualified converse in the printed Lemma2.4.

**Checks.**

- A primitive zero class is rejected.
- The Kunneth sign explains why geometric symmetry gives an alternating H1 tensor.

**Lean boundary.** Full geometric signature is omitted at G1; the native IsNiceCorrespondence predicate keeps nonvanishing explicit.

**Waits for.** [G501](#gap-anabeliangeometryandnonabelianchabauty-g501).

#### 5.3. Depth-two height quotient

*Construction* `NC.5/depth-two-quotient`

Proposed module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/Chabauty/Quadratic`, namespace `TauCetiRoadmap.AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty.NC5`.

Put V=VpJ and W2=coker(Qp(1)→∧²V), the cup-dual relation. The imported proper depth-two group has central exact sequence 1→W2→U2→V→1. A nonzero alternating cup-zero rational cycle class gives a G_Q-equivariant surjection q_Z:W2→Qp(1). Define U_Z=U2/ker(q_Z), as an fpqc group-scheme quotient, so 1→Qp(1)→U_Z→V→1 is central and its commutator is q_Z applied to the imported commutator. At the linear central grade the carrier is W2/ker q_Z, identified with Qp(1) by the existing first isomorphism theorem.

**Hypotheses.**

- A nonzero alternating cup-zero rational cycle class supplies q_Z by duality.
- The kernel is closed, normal and Galois stable; characteristic zero and finite type come from NC.2.
- A nice correspondence supplies this class under nice-trace-criterion, which retains its absolutely-simple-J hypothesis. The general rank criterion instead obtains primitive classes directly from rational NS and does not use that hypothesis.

**Construction.**

1. Use the proper cup-dual presentation of U2, not the affine free fundamental group.
2. Factor the cycle functional through W2 because it kills the cup-dual relation. Nonzero to a one-dimensional target is surjective.
3. Import the schematic central pushout and preserve the Galois action; use the native module quotient only for its central grade.

**API.**

- `DepthTwoHeightQuotient.centralMap` (projection): The central projection is the native quotient map W2→W2/ker q.
- `DepthTwoHeightQuotient.centralEquiv` (equivalence): For surjective q, the central quotient is linearly equivalent to its Tate target.
- `DepthTwoHeightQuotient.centralEquiv_apply` (simp): The equivalence takes the class of z to q(z).
- `DepthTwoHeightQuotient.centralMap_eq_zero` (characterisation): The central class of z is zero exactly when q(z)=0.
- `DepthTwoHeightQuotient.central_exact` (structure): The geometric central extension has the stated kernel, projection and commutator.

**Unit tests.**

- `quotient_coordinate` (computation): For q:Q²→Q the first coordinate, (3,5) and (3,0) give the same central class and q is surjective.
- `quotient_zero_map` (degenerate): For q=0 every central class vanishes.
- `quotient_retains_nonzero_class` (non-example): For the coordinate projection, the class of (1,0) is nonzero.

**Checks.**

- The centre is a Tate line only for a nonzero functional.
- Retain the proper cup relation and the schematic quotient.

**Uses.**

- BDMTV §3.4: Supplies the group acting on the height module.
- NC.4 / NC.5: Projects the depth-two Selmer locus to a smaller height quotient without losing rational points.

**Lean boundary.** The geometric DepthTwoHeightQuotient constructor is explicitly omitted. Its central module carrier and four API signatures are native. Geometric quotient, projection, central_exact and commutator are individually omitted at G1; an abstract quotient of point groups is insufficient.

#### 5.4. Quadratic Chabauty rank criterion

*Theorem* `NC.5/rank-picard-criterion` · planet: **Quadratic Chabauty rank criterion**

Proposed module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/Chabauty/Quadratic`, namespace `TauCetiRoadmap.AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty.NC5`.

Let X/Q be smooth, projective and geometrically connected with genus g&gt;1 and rational basepoint, J its Jacobian, p a prime of good reduction, r=rank J(Q), and rho_Q=rank NS(J/Q). With the NC.4 Selmer locus defined by crystalline conditions at p, actual local Kummer images at all bad places and projection to the global Mordell–Weil Kummer image, r&lt;g+rho_Q−1 implies X(Qp)\_2 is finite. It contains X(Q). No equality between global H1_f(G_T,V) and J(Q)⊗Qp, no ordinary-reduction hypothesis and no replacement of rho_Q by the geometric Picard number are assumed.

**Hypotheses.**

- Use p-adic coefficients and the reduced Selmer variety convention of BD I §2.3, as fixed in NC.4.
- The number field is Q; the extra unit and splitting hypotheses for other fields are outside this selected theorem.

**Proof.**

1. From A2/A6 import rational NS and its symmetric-Hom injection and finite rank. Primitive rational NS classes form a space of dimension rho_Q−1 after removing the theta/trace direction.
2. Push U2 to an extension of V by rho_Q−1 Tate lines. The global crystalline/unramified Tate-line kernel has dimension zero over Q, using the S-unit/Kummer and local conditions; finite bad Kummer images contribute no dimension. The Mordell–Weil cut bounds the global Selmer dimension by r.
3. The local crystalline quotient has dimension g+rho_Q−1 by strict extension classification and the Bloch–Kato dimension formula. The strict inequality gives non-dominance. Import NC.4 discwise density and analytic finiteness to conclude.

**Checks.**

- When rho_Q=1 the strict bound reduces to r&lt;g.
- The boundary r=g+rho_Q−1 does not assert finiteness.
- A larger geometric NS rank without rational descent does not improve this bound.

**Lean boundary.** The geometric locus and dimension theorem signature are omitted at G1 and the NC.4 contract. The node is a theorem plan, not a numerical surrogate.

**Waits for.** [G501](#gap-anabeliangeometryandnonabelianchabauty-g501); [G504](#gap-anabeliangeometryandnonabelianchabauty-g504).

#### 5.5. Admissible de Rham Tate class

*Definition* `NC.5/admissible-tate-class`

Proposed module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/Chabauty/Quadratic`, namespace `TauCetiRoadmap.AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty.NC5`.

For H=H1_dR(X/Qp) with Frobenius phi at a good prime p, define admissibility of Z in H⊗H by five explicit conditions: Z≠0; (phi⊗phi)(Z)=pZ; Z belongs to Fil1(H⊗H); cup(Z)=0; and swap(Z)=−Z. The filtration is the tensor filtration; phi is on H1, not on its Tate dual. These are necessary conditions for a nice rational correspondence, and they do not construct one.

**Hypotheses.**

- The geometric specialization is over Qp, so phi is linear; a ramified coefficient-field extension requires its imported semilinear comparison.
- Nonvanishing is retained from the opening paragraph of §4.4, p.913; it accompanies the four displayed de Rham conditions.

**Construction.**

1. Use the native tensor product, its commutor and the tensor of phi with itself.
2. Impose membership in the supplied tensor filtration and the kernel of cup, with the eigenvalue and alternating condition.
3. Keep algebraicity and rational descent as separate evidence in nice-class-realization.

**API.**

- `IsAdmissibleTateClass.nonzero` (relation): An admissible class is nonzero.
- `IsAdmissibleTateClass.smul` (compatibility): A nonzero scalar multiple remains admissible.
- `IsAdmissibleTateClass.not_zero` (characterisation): The zero tensor is never admissible.

**Unit tests.**

- `tate_wedge_eigenvalue` (computation): For H=Q², phi=diag(1,2), Fil1=all and cup=0, e1⊗e2−e2⊗e1 is admissible with eigenvalue2. This is a linear test, not a geometric curve.
- `tate_zero_rejected` (degenerate): With the same data zero is rejected.
- `tate_symmetric_tensor_rejected` (non-example): With phi=diag(1,2), Fil1=all and cup=0, e1⊗e2+e2⊗e1 is rejected although it is nonzero and has eigenvalue2. This isolates the alternating condition.
- `tate_wrong_frobenius` (non-example): The nonzero wedge is rejected with phi=id and required eigenvalue2.
- `tate_wrong_filtration` (non-example): With phi=diag(1,2), cup=0 and Fil1=zero, the nonzero wedge is rejected. All other conditions hold.
- `tate_nonzero_cup_rejected` (non-example): With phi=diag(1,2) and Fil1=all, the wedge is rejected by the linear test functional cup(x⊗y)=x1\*y2, since its value is1. All other conditions hold; this test functional is not asserted to be a geometric alternating cup pairing.

**Checks.**

- Changing to the dual Frobenius without the twist changes the eigenvalue and is rejected.
- Admissibility is never used as an algebraic-cycle lifting theorem.

**Uses.**

- BDMTV §4.4 / §5.4: Defines the linear conditions used to construct the specialized height connection.
- NC.5 worked curve: Checks the cohomological matrices only after rational Hecke-cycle provenance is supplied.

**Lean boundary.** Native tensor predicate, API and all six linear tests elaborate with admitted proofs. Its H1_dR geometric instantiation uses the imported period/cycle interface at G1.

#### 5.6. Realization of a rational nice class

*Theorem* `NC.5/nice-class-realization`

Proposed module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/Chabauty/Quadratic`, namespace `TauCetiRoadmap.AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty.NC5`.

A nonzero rational nice correspondence produces an admissible de Rham Tate class at every good prime, under the tensor-compatible crystalline cycle comparison. Only this forward implication is asserted. An arbitrary p-adic linear combination satisfying the admissibility conditions need not belong to the rational algebraic-correspondence space, even when the two stated Picard ranks agree.

**Hypotheses.**

- Use the rational class, its symmetric Hom/NS realization and the good-reduction crystalline cycle class, with tensor and cup compatibility.
- The nice-to-alternating implication here uses nice-trace-criterion, including absolute simplicity. For the general rank theorem, rational NS classes give alternating classes on H2(J) directly; that theorem does not depend on this specialized correspondence implication.

**Proof.**

1. A rational divisor cycle has the required Frobenius eigenvalue and Hodge filtration by cycle comparison.
2. Apply the alternating and cup/trace criterion and injectivity on rational divisor classes.
3. The proposed converse would confuse the intersection of a rational lattice with a filtration with the intersection of its p-adic span; it is excluded.

**Checks.**

- Input includes an actual rational cycle, with no inferred lift from de Rham linear algebra.
