- `EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.3`

**Sources.**

- [Kim09](#src-kim09), §3, statement of the weak Jannsen conjecture, Observation 3 and its proof, pp.125–126: Shows for affine curves that a uniform vanishing of H² in large twists bounds H² of the tensor powers by an exponential of base below m, which suffices for Conjecture 1.

<a id="nc-6-cm-rank-one-finiteness"></a>

#### 6.14. Integral points on punctured CM elliptic curves of rank one

*Theorem* `NC.6/cm-rank-one-finiteness`

Proposed module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/Anabelian/Frontiers`, namespace `TauCeti.Anabelian`.

Let E/Q be an elliptic curve with complex multiplication, X = E ∖ {O} with its minimal model 𝒳 and an integral base point b ∈ 𝒳(Z) (if 𝒳(Z) is empty there is nothing to prove), p an odd prime of good reduction and T the bad primes together with p. Assume that the Bloch–Kato Selmer group H¹_f(G_Q, V_pE) has dimension one (this holds, for example, when E(Q) has rank one and Ш(E)\[p^∞\] is finite). Let Sel_T(U⟨n⟩) be the refined Selmer variety of classes potentially unramified at the primes of T other than p and potentially crystalline at p. Then dim Sel_T(U⟨2⟩) ≤ 1 &lt; 2 = dim U_dR⟨2⟩/F⁰, so the integral points 𝒳(Z) form a finite set, without any conjectural input.

**Hypotheses.**

- CM ensures potentially good reduction everywhere (good reduction over Q(E\[12\])), which defines the potentially unramified conditions.
- Selmer rank one is a hypothesis on V_pE; rank E(Q) = 1 alone does not give it without finiteness of Ш(E)\[p^∞\] (source issue E-NC6-kim-rank-one).
- The base point is integral, as NC.2–NC.4 require; Kim §4 does not fix one, and the finiteness statement is empty when 𝒳(Z) = ∅.

**Proof.**

1. Depth-two graded piece: gr_2 U = Λ²H₁ ≅ Q_p(1) (NC.6/graded-central-dimensions with m = 2).
2. The refined central sequence 0 → Sel_T(gr_2 U) → Sel_T(U⟨2⟩) → Sel_T(U⟨1⟩) is exact in the torsor sense (NC.3/central-selmer-dimension), so dim Sel_T(U⟨2⟩) ≤ dim Sel_T(H₁) + dim Sel_T(Q_p(1)).
3. Sel_T(Q_p(1)) = Z^× ⊗ Q_p = 0 (SIC L0/s-unit-kummer-identification). Sel_T(H₁) = H¹_f(G_Q, V_pE): at ℓ ≠ p the local H¹ of V_pE vanishes for potentially good reduction (weights), and at p potentially crystalline classes are de Rham, where H¹_g = H¹_f for V_pE; it has dimension one by hypothesis (SIC L4/elliptic-finite-kummer).
4. On the de Rham side F⁰(gr_2 U_dR) = 0 because F⁰H₁ ∧ F⁰H₁ = 0, so dim U_dR⟨2⟩/F⁰ = 3 − 1 = 2.
5. The refined conditions are finer than Kim's, so NC.4/locus-compatibilities and NC.4/dimension-finiteness give finiteness.

**Checks.**

- The congruent-number curve y² = x³ − 25x has CM by Z\[i\] and E(Q) of rank one, generated modulo torsion by (−4, 6); with Ш(E)\[p^∞\] finite it satisfies the hypothesis.
- The depth used is 2 in this roadmap's indexing (Kim's U_3).

<a id="nc-6-pseudo-null-implies-dimension"></a>

#### 6.15. Pseudo-nullity implies the dimension conjecture for punctured CM curves

*Theorem* `NC.6/pseudo-null-implies-dimension`

Proposed module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/Anabelian/Frontiers`, namespace `TauCeti.Anabelian`.

Let E/Q have complex multiplication, X = E ∖ {O}, p an odd prime of good reduction, F_1 = Q(E\[p\]), F\_∞ = Q(E\[p^∞\]), G\_∞ = Gal(F\_∞/F_1), Λ = Z_p\[\[G\_∞\]\] (for p odd of good reduction, p is unramified in the CM field K, K ⊆ F_1 and G\_∞ is open in 1 + p(O_K ⊗ Z_p) ≅ Z_p², so Λ ≅ Z_p\[\[T_1, T_2\]\] is a regular local domain), and I the Galois group of the maximal abelian unramified pro-p extension of F\_∞ in which the primes above T split completely. Assume the Coates–Sujatha conjecture that I, a finitely generated Λ-module, is pseudo-null. Then KimDimensionConjecture holds for X (working over F_1, which suffices because corestriction is surjective on H²), and hence 𝒳(Z) is finite.

**Hypotheses.**

- The pseudo-nullity of the finitely generated Λ-module I is a hypothesis; p is odd, so that G\_∞ is torsion-free of rank two and Λ is the integrally closed domain of PMIA L4/pseudo-null.
- The H² estimate is reduced to F_1; local terms are bounded as in h2-growth-bound with g = 1.

**Proof.**

1. It suffices to bound dim H²(G_T, H₁^{⊗n}) by a polynomial in n; the local contributions are bounded as in NC.6/h2-growth-bound, so it suffices to bound Ш²_T(H₁^{⊗n}).
2. By Poitou–Tate this is dual to Sel⁰_T(H¹^{⊗n}(1)). The Hochschild–Serre sequence for F\_∞/F_1 in continuous cohomology of the inverse system H¹(Ē, Z/p^i)^{⊗n}(1) (Jannsen; requested from D7) identifies it, after inverting p, with Hom_Λ(I, H¹^{⊗n}(1)): the terms H^j(G\_∞, H¹^{⊗n}(1)) ⊗ Q vanish for j = 1, 2 and n ≠ 2, because G\_∞ contains homotheties u ∈ 1 + p^r Z_p of T_pE (the CM image is open in (O_K ⊗ Z_p)^×), which are central and act on H¹^{⊗n}(1) by the scalar u^{2−n} ≠ 1.
3. Pseudo-nullity makes I ⊗ Q_p finite-dimensional: the Z_p-torsion of I maps to zero in every Q_p-vector space, and I′ = I/I\[p^∞\] is pseudo-null with p a nonzerodivisor, so dim I′/pI′ ≤ 0, I′/pI′ is finite, and I′ is finitely generated over Z_p by Nakayama's lemma for compact modules. (Kim asserts finite generation of I itself over Z_p, citing Greenberg 1978; that fails for p-torsion pseudo-null modules such as Λ/(p, T_1): source issue E-NC6-kim-pseudonull-fg.) A Frobenius element of G\_∞ therefore has finitely many eigenvalues on I ⊗ Q_p, and by weights Hom_Λ(I, H¹^{⊗n}(1)) = 0 for n ≫ 0.
4. Conclude as in vanishing-implies-dimension with the polynomial bound.

**Checks.**

- The hypothesis is about F\_∞ = Q(E\[p^∞\]), a two-dimensional p-adic Lie extension of F_1 in the CM case.
- With g = 1 the local bound is polynomial in n, and d_n \~ 2^n/n for m = 2.

**Needs.**

- [`NC.6/kim-dimension-conjecture`](#nc-6-kim-dimension-conjecture) Kim's dimension conjecture
- [`NC.6/h2-growth-bound`](#nc-6-h2-growth-bound) Kim's H² estimate
- [`NC.6/vanishing-implies-dimension`](#nc-6-vanishing-implies-dimension) Selmer vanishing implies the dimension conjecture
- `PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L4/pseudo-null`
- `ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.4/poitou-tate`
- `ArithmeticGaloisDuality:D7`

**Sources.**

- [Kim09](#src-kim09), §4, Observation 4 and its proof, pp.130–131: Derives Conjecture 1 for a punctured CM curve from the pseudo-nullity conjecture of Coates and Sujatha through Poitou–Tate, Hochschild–Serre and a weight argument; the finite-generation claim on p.131 is replaced by the weaker statement the weight argument uses (source issue E-NC6-kim-pseudonull-fg).

<a id="nc-6-genus-zero-dimension"></a>

#### 6.16. The dimension conjecture for the thrice-punctured line

*Theorem* `NC.6/genus-zero-dimension`

Proposed module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/Anabelian/Frontiers`, namespace `TauCeti.Anabelian`.

Let X = P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞} over Z\[1/S\] with S a finite set of primes, b ∈ 𝒳(Z\[1/S\]) an S-integral base point (if 𝒳(Z\[1/S\]) is empty there is nothing to prove), and p ∉ S an odd prime. Then KimDimensionConjecture(X, p) holds, hence X(Z\[1/S\]) is finite (Siegel's theorem for this curve). Explicitly gr_n U ≅ Q_p(n)^{r_n} with r_n the Witt numbers for m = 2, F⁰ = 0 on U_dR so dim Q_n = Σ\_{k ≤ n} r_k, and dim S_n ≤ \|S\|·2 + Σ\_{3 ≤ k ≤ n, k odd} r_k, which is smaller for n large.

**Hypotheses.**

- S finite, p ∉ S odd (the supplier request to ArithmeticKTheory N.5 is for odd p); T = S ∪ {p}; the base point is S-integral, as in Kim 2005 p.17.
- Uses Soulé's computation of H¹(G_T, Q_p(k)): zero for even k ≥ 2 and one-dimensional for odd k ≥ 3.
- Kim 2005 also takes p large compared with the depth for its comparison maps; here the comparison is that of NC.4, for every prime of good reduction.

**Proof.**

1. H₁ = Q_p(1)² and gr_n U is a quotient of H₁^{⊗n}, so gr_n U ≅ Q_p(n)^{r_n} with r_n from NC.6/graded-central-dimensions.
2. H¹_f(G_T, Q_p(1)) = Z\[1/S\]^× ⊗ Q_p has dimension \|S\| (SIC L0/s-unit-kummer-identification); H¹(G_T, Q_p(k)) = 0 for even k ≥ 2 and has dimension one for odd k ≥ 3 (Soulé; ArithmeticKTheory N.5).
3. The central-extension fibration gives dim S_n ≤ 2\|S\| + Σ\_{odd 3 ≤ k ≤ n} r_k (NC.3/central-extension).
4. Since the Hodge filtration of H¹_dR is F¹ = everything, F⁰U_dR is trivial and dim Q_n = Σ\_{k ≤ n} r_k; the even-degree terms make the difference positive for large n.
5. Finiteness follows from NC.4/dimension-finiteness.

**Checks.**

- S = ∅: 𝒳(Z) is empty, and the depth-one dimensions, which need no base point, are dim H¹_f(G_T, Q_p(1)²) = 0 &lt; 2 = dim Q_1.
- S = {2}: depth 1 gives 2 = 2, depth 2 gives 2 &lt; 3, in agreement with BDCKW §8.2.

**Needs.**

<a id="nc6-eventual"></a>

### Kim's conjecture on eventual equality

<a id="nc-6-kim-conjecture"></a>

#### 6.17. Kim's conjecture on eventual equality

*Definition* `NC.6/kim-conjecture` · planet: **Kim's conjecture**

Proposed module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/Anabelian/Frontiers`, namespace `TauCeti.Anabelian`.

Let 𝒳 → Spec Z be a regular minimal model of a hyperbolic curve over Q in one of the three cases of BDCKW §2.1 (P¹ minus a reduced horizontal divisor with at least three geometric points; the regular minimal model of a smooth proper curve of genus ≥ 2; or the complement of a nonempty reduced horizontal divisor in the regular minimal model of a smooth proper curve of genus ≥ 1), b an integral point or integral tangent vector, p an odd prime of good reduction and T a finite set of primes containing p and the bad primes. Let U⟨n⟩ be the depth-n quotient of the Q_p-unipotent étale fundamental group (BDCKW's U_n), j_v: 𝒳(Z_v) → H¹(G_v, U⟨n⟩) the local unipotent Kummer maps, and Sel_n(𝒳) = ⋂\_{v ≠ p} loc_v⁻¹(Im j_v) ⊆ H¹_f(G_T, U⟨n⟩), with the scheme structure given by the sum of the ideals (each Im j_v is finite and is the base point for v ∉ T). Put X(Z_p)\_n = j_p⁻¹(loc_p(Sel_n(𝒳))) ⊆ 𝒳(Z_p). These sets decrease with n, contain 𝒳(Z), and do not depend on T or b. The proposition KimConjecture(𝒳, p) states that X(Z_p)\_n = 𝒳(Z) for all sufficiently large n (BDCKW Conjecture 3.1). For a finite set S of primes with p ∉ S, dropping the conditions at v ∈ S gives Sel\_{n,S}(𝒳), X(Z_p)\_{S,n} ⊇ 𝒳(Z\[1/S\]), and the S-integral proposition KimConjecture_S(𝒳, p): X(Z_p)\_{S,n} = 𝒳(Z\[1/S\]) for n large (BDCKW §8.1). Both are open and are stated as named propositions; BDCKW do not formulate a version over other number fields (§3.2), and none is stated here.

**Hypotheses.**

- 𝒳 a regular minimal Z-model as in BDCKW §2.1; p odd of good reduction for 𝒳 and b.
- In NC.4 terms, X(Z_p)\_n is the crystalline locus crystallineLocus_n for the stringent local conditions C_v = Im j_v at v ≠ p and the crystalline condition at p.
- Depth indexing: U⟨n⟩ = U/Γ\_{n+1}U, so n = 1 is the abelian depth.
- When b is an integral tangent vector (as for P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞} over Z, which has no integral point), the Selmer scheme, the local Kummer maps and the loci use NC.2–NC.4 at the tangential fibre functor: recorded gap on tangential base points.

**Construction.**

1. Represent H¹_f(G_T, U⟨n⟩) and the localisation maps (NC.3/selmer-functor, NC.3/selmer-representability).
2. Finiteness of Im j_v for v ≠ p (Kim–Tamagawa, as cited by BDCKW 2.5) and triviality for good v ∉ T make Sel_n(𝒳) a closed subscheme; define X(Z_p)\_n through the local Kummer map j_p (NC.4/kim-loci).
3. Monotonicity in n and containment of 𝒳(Z) follow from NC.4/locus-compatibilities and NC.4/rational-integral-containment.
4. Independence of T and b: BDCKW §2.8 (inflation lemma for closed normal subgroups) and §2.9 (twisting by the path torsor P(b, c)).
5. Define the propositions as eventual equality.

**API.**

- `kimLocus` (data): X(Z_p)\_n = j_p⁻¹(loc_p(Sel_n(𝒳))) ⊆ 𝒳(Z_p).
- `kimLocus_antitone` (relation): X(Z_p)\_{n+1} ⊆ X(Z_p)\_n for every n ≥ 1.
- `integral_subset_kimLocus` (relation): 𝒳(Z) ⊆ X(Z_p)\_n for every n.
- `kimConjecture_iff_exists_subset` (characterisation): KimConjecture(𝒳, p) holds if and only if X(Z_p)\_n ⊆ 𝒳(Z) for some n, by the two previous items.
- `kimLocus_eq_crystallineLocus` (compatibility): X(Z_p)\_n equals NC.4's crystallineLocus_n for the stringent local conditions.
- `kimLocus_indep_T` (compatibility): For T ⊆ T′ both containing p and the bad primes, the Selmer schemes for T and T′ are isomorphic compatibly with loc_p, so X(Z_p)\_n does not depend on T.
- `kimLocus_indep_basepoint` (compatibility): Twisting by the path torsor P(b, c) identifies the Selmer schemes for integral base points b and c compatibly with loc_p and the Kummer maps, so X(Z_p)\_n does not depend on b.
- `kimConjectureS` (data): The S-integral proposition: X(Z_p)\_{S,n} = 𝒳(Z\[1/S\]) for n large, with KimConjectureS ∅ = KimConjecture.
- `EventualEquality` (other): The form on families of sets: L n = G for all large n; KimConjecture is the instance L n = X(Z_p)\_n, G = 𝒳(Z).
- `eventualEquality_iff_exists_subset` (characterisation): For an antitone family L with G ⊆ L n for all n, eventual equality holds if and only if L n ⊆ G for some n.
- `eventualEquality_iInter` (relation): For an antitone family, eventual equality with G implies ⋂\_n L n = G; the converse fails (kimConjecture_not_intersection).

**Unit tests.**

- `kimConjecture_thrice_punctured_p5` (computation): For 𝒳 = P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞} over Z with the tangential base point at 0 and p = 5, X(Z_5)\_1 = ∅ = 𝒳(Z), so the conjecture holds from depth 1 (BDCKW §6.1).
- `kimLocus_thrice_punctured_p7` (computation): For the same 𝒳 and p = 7, X(Z_7)\_1 = {ζ_6, ζ_6⁵} ≠ 𝒳(Z) = ∅: equality is eventual, not at depth 1 (BDCKW §6.2).
- `kimConjecture_not_intersection` (non-example): Eventual equality is stronger than ⋂\_n X(Z_p)\_n = 𝒳(Z): for the decreasing family L_n = G ∪ {m ∈ ℕ : m ≥ n} with G finite, the intersection is G but no L_n equals G, so a definition by the intersection would accept it.
- `kimConjectureS_empty` (degenerate): For S = ∅ the S-integral Selmer scheme is Sel_n(𝒳) and KimConjectureS reduces to KimConjecture.
- `kimLocusS_half_contains` (computation): For P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞} over Z\[1/2\] and an odd prime p, the three points 2, −1 and 1/2 lie in X(Z_p)\_{{2},2}, the zero set of 2Li_2(z) + log(z)log(1 − z) (BDCKW §8.2).

**Checks.**

- For P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞} over Z and p = 5, X(Z_5)\_1 = ∅ = 𝒳(Z) (NC.6/thrice-punctured-depth-one).
- For P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞} over Z and p = 7, X(Z_7)\_1 consists of the two primitive sixth roots of unity, so equality fails at depth 1.

**Uses.**

- BDCKW §§5–8: The conjecture is tested by computing X(Z_p)\_n for punctured elliptic curves, the thrice-punctured line and Fermat curves.
- BDCKW §3.4: Presented as the unipotent counterpart of the surjectivity in the section conjecture and of finiteness of Ш.
- [`NC.6/thrice-punctured-depth-one`](#nc-6-thrice-punctured-depth-one): The depth-one instance proved in BDCKW §6.1.
- EffectiveDiophantineMethods ED.6: Certified enumeration compares a computed finite locus with the known global points; equality at some depth is what makes such a comparison exhaustive.

- [`NC.3/selmer-functor`](#nc-3-selmer-functor) Selmer functor

<a id="nc-6-thrice-punctured-depth-one"></a>

#### 6.18. Kim's conjecture at depth one for the thrice-punctured line

*Application* `NC.6/thrice-punctured-depth-one`

Proposed module `TauCeti/NumberTheory/Anabelian/Frontiers`, namespace `TauCeti.Anabelian`.

Let 𝒳 = P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞} over Z with the tangential base point at 0. Then 𝒳(Z) = ∅. At depth 1, U⟨1⟩ = Q_p(1)², Sel_1(𝒳) = 0 and j_p(z) = (log z, log(1 − z)), so X(Z_p)\_1 is the set of z ∈ Z_p with z and 1 − z both roots of unity, which is the set of primitive sixth roots of unity lying in Z_p. Hence for p = 3 or p ≡ 2 mod 3, X(Z_p)\_1 = ∅ and KimConjecture(𝒳, p) holds from depth 1. For p ≡ 1 mod 3, X(Z_p)\_1 = {ζ_6, ζ_6⁵}; Sel_2(𝒳) = 0 by Soulé's vanishing H¹(G_T, Q_p(2)) = 0, and X(Z_p)\_2 = ∅ if and only if the p-adic dilogarithm Li_2(ζ_6) is nonzero. BDCKW report that Li_2(ζ_6) ≠ 0 for 3 ≤ p &lt; 10⁵ by a numerical computation; that report is not a theorem of this layer.

**Hypotheses.**

- p odd; 𝒳(Z) = ∅ because z and 1 − z cannot both be units of Z.
- The depth-two statement for p ≡ 1 mod 3 is an equivalence with a nonvanishing condition, not an unconditional equality.
- The tangential base point at 0 uses the recorded gap on tangential base points.

**Proof.**

1. 𝒳(Z) is empty: the only units are ±1, and 1 − 1 = 0, 1 − (−1) = 2.
2. Sel_1(𝒳) = 0: it is (Z^× ⊗ Q_p)² with the stringent conditions (NC.3/depth-one-selmer-comparison, SIC L0/s-unit-kummer-identification).
3. The local Kummer map at the tangential base point has as coordinates the regularised iterated integrals from 0 (NC.4/iterated-coordinates, at the tangential base point: recorded gap): ∫dz/z = log z and ∫dz/(z − 1) = log(1 − z) at depth 1, and the depth-2 coordinate −Li_2(z) (ColemanIntegration L1/punctured-line-coleman-functions). A zero of the p-adic logarithm on Z_p^× is a root of unity, and z, 1 − z both roots of unity forces z to be a primitive sixth root of unity.
4. A primitive sixth root of unity lies in Z_p exactly when p ≡ 1 mod 3.
5. For p ≡ 1 mod 3, Sel_2(𝒳) = 0 because H¹(G_T, Q_p(2)) = 0, so X(Z_p)\_2 is cut out by the depth-2 coordinate −Li_2(z) as well; since Li_2(ζ_6⁻¹) = −Li_2(ζ_6) (ColemanIntegration L2/inversion-relation with log ζ_6 = 0), the two candidates vanish or survive together.

**Checks.**

- p = 5: X(Z_5)\_1 = ∅.
- p = 7: X(Z_7)\_1 = {3, 5} modulo the identification of ζ_6 with the Teichmüller lifts of 3 and 5, the primitive sixth roots of unity mod 7.

**Sources.**

## Supplier contracts

Each contract names its supplier (a layer or target of another roadmap, or a layer of an existing Tau Ceti roadmap), the exact statement this roadmap needs beyond what the supplier already states, and the targets here that consume it. The owner never changes: a contract to an existing Tau Ceti roadmap is a requested refinement of it, not a plan of its content. A target that cites a whole supplier layer does so only through one of these contracts.

The current A6/hom-is-free-of-finite-rank node states the NS conclusion but does not replace this A2 definition/injection. ### Contracts between the layers of this roadmap

Five citations between the layers of this roadmap go to a whole layer rather than to a target, because the consuming layer needs a statement that the supplying layer does not yet state. Each is a contract in the list below and each is recorded as an open obligation of the consuming layer.

- **NC.1 → NC.0.** The pro-p sharpening of the curve and product effacement, the identification of relative arithmetic group cohomology over the full Galois group, and cofinal hyperbolic Artin-neighbourhood models. NC.0 states the full finite-coefficient property for a given curve, product or tower ([NC.0/smooth-curve](#nc-0-smooth-curve), [NC.0/product-cover-effacement](#nc-0-product-cover-effacement), [NC.0/artin-neighbourhood](#nc-0-artin-neighbourhood)); the pro-p cofinality and the ℤ_p inverse-limit comparison are not consequences of it. Open obligation: NC.1 gap G3 and G4.
- **NC.1 → NC.2.** The two-step ℚ_p Malcev quotient of the geometric pro-p fundamental group, its Lie bracket and its interpretation through unipotent representations. NC.2 builds the unipotent completion of the étale fundamental group of a curve ([NC.2/tannakian-groups](#nc-2-tannakian-groups), [NC.2/central-quotients](#nc-2-central-quotients)), not the Malcev quotient of an abstract pro-p group; this target must be added to NC.2 with no input from NC.1, so that the stage order NC.2 → NC.1 has no cycle. Open obligation: the gap recorded in NC.1 for it.
- **NC.4 → NC.2.** Native families of right path torsors with the full normalized Hodge filtration, Frobenius-fixed sections and condition-preserving depth projections; the two-augmentation multiplicative crystalline comparison (NC.2's first gap); the transport of the forward word element I to the ordered ratio I⁻¹γ; the depth-one Hodge–Abel–Jacobi identification; and the extension of the comparison to ramified good models and integral endpoints. The consuming targets also cite the NC.2 targets that state the unramified forms. Open obligation: NC.4's second and fourth gaps.
- **NC.4 → NC.3.** The crystalline H¹ and Selmer functors as functors on all ℚ_p-algebras with their conditional representability, which NC.3 states ([NC.3/local-condition-geometry](#nc-3-local-condition-geometry), [NC.3/selmer-functor](#nc-3-selmer-functor), [NC.3/selmer-representability](#nc-3-selmer-representability), [NC.3/selmer-localization-naturality](#nc-3-selmer-localization-naturality), cited directly), together with the crystalline period functor natural on all algebras and compatible with the nonlinear endpoint comparison, localization and depth, which it does not. Open obligation: NC.4's third gap.
- **NC.5 → NC.4.** The depth-two Selmer variety of a proper curve with a Mordell–Weil cut and the actual bad-place local images; finiteness of the local images away from p (after Kim–Tamagawa); density of the Albanese map on every open subdisc of a residue disc; the analytic zero theorem on compact charts; and unramifiedness, or potential unramifiedness after finite base change, of the path torsors at places of good or potentially good reduction away from p. NC.4 states density on whole residue discs ([NC.4/residue-disc-density](#nc-4-residue-disc-density)), the loci ([NC.4/kim-loci](#nc-4-kim-loci)) and finiteness under discwise nonvanishing ([NC.4/finite-annihilator-locus](#nc-4-finite-annihilator-locus)), but none of the other statements. Open obligation: the gap recorded in NC.5 for it.

- **layer [NC.0](#layer-nc-0).** Sharpen the positive-genus curve/product effacement interface to geometric pro-p covers and p-power coefficients/twists, then identify relative arithmetic group cohomology over full G_K. Existing full finite-coefficient K(π,1) and product-cover-effacement alone do not assert this pro-p cofinality or the Z_p inverse-limit comparison. Also supply cofinal hyperbolic Artin-neighborhood models of characteristic-zero function fields and the exact geometric fibration sequences used for centre-freeness; the existing artin-neighbourhood node states K(π,1) for a given tower, not existence of the cofinal tower.
  Consumers: [`NC.1/arithmetic-chern-comparison`](#nc-1-arithmetic-chern-comparison) Arithmetic Chern classes on pro-p curve products; [`NC.1/local-galois-centre-free`](#nc-1-local-galois-centre-free) Local Galois centre-freeness.

- **layer [NC.2](#layer-nc-2).** Supply the two-step Q_p Malcev quotient of the geometric pro-p group, its Lie bracket and functorial unipotent representation interpretation without using NC.1 reconstruction.
  Consumers: [`NC.1/weight-zero-quotient`](#nc-1-weight-zero-quotient) Weight-zero two-step quotient.

- **layer [NC.2](#layer-nc-2).** Supply the native right geometric path-torsor families with full normalized Hodge filtration, Frobenius-fixed sections and condition-preserving finite-depth projections. Complete the already recorded two-augmentation multiplicative crystalline comparison, and explicitly transport the forward affine word element I to the ordered ratio I⁻¹γ and the normalized depth-one Hodge–Abel–Jacobi/Lie identification. No general linear Hodge theory is replanned. Extend the rigid/de Rham and nonlinear crystalline path comparisons to arbitrary smooth proper good-reduction pairs over finite ramified O_K, with finite étale boundary and every integral endpoint, preserving both augmentations, coactions, Frobenius and the normalized Hodge filtration. The existing unramified-model results and their coefficient-extension clause do not cover a model or endpoint without descent. For a smooth good integral pair over O\_{F,S}, T containing S and p-adic places, also supply trivial inertia outside T on the geometric unipotent Q_p group and every S-integral endpoint path, and hence their continuous G\_{F,T}-actions; importing G_F-actions alone is insufficient.
  Consumers: [`NC.4/local-albanese`](#nc-4-local-albanese) The finite-depth de Rham Albanese map; [`NC.4/iterated-coordinates`](#nc-4-iterated-coordinates) Iterated integrals as Albanese coordinates; [`NC.4/crystalline-period`](#nc-4-crystalline-period) The represented crystalline period map; [`NC.4/fundamental-diagram`](#nc-4-fundamental-diagram) Compatibility of global paths, localization and periods; [`NC.4/depth-one-period`](#nc-4-depth-one-period) The depth-one Albanese and abelian logarithm; [`NC.4/local-etale-albanese`](#nc-4-local-etale-albanese) The local étale path-class map; [`NC.4/global-etale-albanese`](#nc-4-global-etale-albanese) The global étale path-class map; [`NC.4/residue-disc-density`](#nc-4-residue-disc-density) Kim density on every residue disc.

Neither de Rham-only classes nor a guessed affine coordinate algebra may replace it.

## Open proof obligations

Every target above has a complete prerequisite chain ending in the libraries, in a target of another roadmap, in a supplier contract, or in one of the obligations below. An obligation names the exact missing input and the targets that wait for it; none is papered over by an assumed statement. They fall into four kinds: geometric carriers that the pinned libraries cannot yet express (each layer has one such entry, which also explains which signatures the suggested Lean file omits); supplier statements that no roadmap yet plans (raw étale homotopy, the multiplicative crystalline comparison with two endpoint augmentations, generic p-adic heights, the proper de Rham Abel–Jacobi bridge); proof inputs of this roadmap's own geometric theorems (point topologies, filtered torsor effectivity, closed crystalline loci, tangential base points in the unipotent theory); and source passages that could not be read.

### Layers NC.0 and NC.3 (étale K(π,1) schemes and the cohomological core)

These obligations were recorded with the lemma-level targets of NC.0 and NC.3. Several are now carried, narrowed or discharged by the target-level plans of the same layers:

- *Topologies on points of unipotent groups* is planned by [NC.3/galois-coefficient-family](#nc-3-galois-coefficient-family) and [NC.3/unipotent-point-topology](#nc-3-unipotent-point-topology); what remains is NC.3's G1.
- *Unipotent algebraic groups: lower central series and splittings*: the lower central tower is [NC.2/central-quotients](#nc-2-central-quotients); the algebraic splittings and vector quotients are requested from ReductiveGroups Layers 0, 3 and 5 in the NC.3 contracts.
- *Delegated raw-homotopy, curve and product proof leaves* and *Typed étale comparison carrier* are restated, with their supplier contracts audited, by NC.0's *Inherited geometric product and curve assembly contracts*, *Inherited raw homotopy and elementary fibrations* and *Inherited canonical coefficient comparison at the pinned interfaces* below.
- *Routed Chen and BDMTV additions* is discharged: Chen's tangential specialization and good and symmetric paths are targets of NC.0, and every routed item of Balakrishnan–Dogra–Müller–Tuitman–Vonk is accounted for by an NC.2 or NC.5 target or import (see [Paper routing](#paper-routing)).
- *Remaining continuous cochain and comparison interfaces* is planned by the NC.3 targets on the abelian comparison and the central H² obstruction ([NC.3/canonical-comparison-naturality](#nc-3-canonical-comparison-naturality) through [NC.3/invariant-orbit-transport](#nc-3-invariant-orbit-transport)); what remains is NC.3's G1–G4.
- *Algebraic torsors versus equivariant topological torsors* is planned by [NC.3/filtered-affine-torsor-comparison](#nc-3-filtered-affine-torsor-comparison); what remains is NC.3's G2.
- *Generic raw étale homotopy foundations*, *Raw homotopy comparison outside geometric-unibranch varieties* and *M₀,n moduli and forgetting-mark fibrations* remain open as stated.

<a id="gap-root-gap-1"></a>

**Topologies on points of unipotent groups over topological algebras.** Kim's H¹(G, U(B ⊗\_K R)) uses the inductive-limit topology on B-vector spaces and the induced topology on points of affine schemes (Kim 2005, §1, Lemmas 1–5). The nodes here take U as an abstract topological group; the construction of these topologies and the continuity of the Galois action on points are not built and are needed before the Selmer varieties.

Needed by: layer [NC.3](#layer-nc-3).

<a id="gap-root-gap-2"></a>

**Unipotent algebraic groups: lower central series and splittings.** The continuous-section hypothesis of NC.3/central-extension (b) holds for central extensions of unipotent groups over a field of characteristic 0 by an algebraic splitting (Kim 2005, proof of Proposition 2). Tau Ceti has unipotent-group theory, but this splitting and the lower-central-series quotients as vector groups are not decomposed here.

**Primary source for Labute's dimension formula not read.** The surface-group case of graded-central-dimensions (Σ\_{k\|n} k·d_k = α^n + β^n) is taken from Kim 2009 pp.122–123, which cites Labute, J. Algebra 14 (1970), 16–23. The publisher did not serve that paper to this worker. The formula was checked against the free survey of Linton and Nyberg-Brodda (arXiv:2501.18306, §1.7.6, equation (32), p.62), which gives it in genus 2 and the growth rate g + √(g² − 1) in every genus, and against small cases (g = 1 gives the abelian case; g = 2 gives d_2 = 5 = dim Λ²H₁ − 1 and d_3 = 16). It is also equivalent to the enveloping algebra of the graded Lie algebra having Hilbert series 1/(1 − 2g t + t²) (take logarithms of the PBW product). A follow-up reads Labute 1970 or Labute, Invent. Math. 4 (1967), Théorème 2, and pins the primary locator for all g.

## Corrections to the sources

Each finding gives its place in the source, what is printed (in our own words), the correction the targets above use, the reason, what it affects, whether a correction was already known, and the result of its independent verification. One finding (E-NC6-kim-h1-notation) was rejected on verification and is kept only as a record; the targets use the printed text there. Identifiers are distinct across the roadmap.

Two notes on source versions. Chen's published Proposition 4.2.3(a) identifies the cotangent of the graded tangent line with the original cotangent; a clause of the preprint asserting an inertia action on the original cotangent is absent from the published statement, and the targets follow the published version. "Kim 2008" in the NC.0 targets is the expository *Fundamental groups and Diophantine geometry* ([Kim10](#src-kim10), published 2010), not the 2009 paper on the unipotent Albanese map. The NC.3 representability targets use the correction E1 of Kim 2005, Proposition 3.

- **E1** (misprint, [Kim05](#src-kim05); confirmed).
  Where: arXiv:math/0409456v1, §1, proof of Proposition 3, printed p.10, final displayed product isomorphism (preprint only; version of record not served)
  Printed: H⁰(G,U\_(n+1)^B/U\_(n+1)) ≃ H⁰(G,U_n^B/U_n) × I_n.
  Correction: H⁰(G,U\_(n+1)^B/U\_(n+1)) ≃ H⁰(G,V^B/V) × I_n, where V=U^(n+1)/U^(n+2).
  Reason: The immediately preceding exact sequence has kernel H⁰(G,V^B/V) and image I_n. Its functorial section trivializes that kernel torsor over I_n. The printed H⁰(G,U_n^B/U_n) is the previous-stage ambient base, not the kernel. Substituting the vector-group kernel restores the intended induction. The display was read in the downloaded PDF and visually checked; no claim is made about the subscription version of record.
  Affects: nothing.
  Known: new.
  Verification: The exact-sequence kernel and chosen section determine the vector-group factor. This is an index/object misprint in the v1 proof display; the intended representability claim is unchanged. Verified against the PDF text and page image by this final independent review.

- **E-NC0-inertia-injectivity** (error, [Che24](#src-che24); confirmed).
  Where: Published Definition 4.2.1, p.364 (author-hosted Annals copy)
  Printed: The local punctured-tangent fundamental group is asserted to embed in pi1 of the curve with the point removed, for every smooth curve in the stated scope.
  Correction: Use the induced continuous homomorphism and its image. Local inertia injectivity requires additional hypotheses and is not used for Proposition 4.2.3(b).
  Reason: Over C, take C=P1 and remove only x=infinity. The resulting A1 has no nontrivial connected finite etale covers, so global pi1 is trivial, whereas the punctured tangent has procyclic nontrivial pi1. The local-to-global homomorphism cannot be injective.
  Affects: a stated result.
  Known: new; no existing correction located in the sources searched.
  Verification: Independently read published Definition 4.2.1, p. 364, and the orbit proof on pp. 364–365. For a connected degree-d finite étale cover of A1_C, compactification can ramify only at infinity; Riemann–Hurwitz gives 2g−2=−d−r with r≥1, forcing d=1. Thus the global group is trivial while the punctured-tangent group is nontrivial. Use the inertia image; the orbit theorem survives.

- **E-NC0-punctured-tangent** (misprint, [Che24](#src-che24); confirmed).
  Where: Published Definition 4.2.1, p.364, identification of the punctured tangent with G_m.
  Printed: The displayed affine-line presentation of G_m removes the point 1.
  Correction: Remove 0. The tangent zero section is the puncture; the chosen nonzero tangent is normalized to 1.
  Reason: Removing 1 would exclude the chosen normalized basepoint and retain zero, contradicting both the tangent definition and the subsequent power-map fibre calculation.
  Affects: nothing.
  Known: new; no existing correction located in the sources searched.
  Verification: Independently checked the published display and the normalized tangent in Definition 4.2.1, p. 364: zero is the deleted vector and the specified nonzero vector becomes 1. The displayed deletion of 1 is a misprint; the power-map and orbit proof use the intended deletion of zero.

- **E-NC0-preprint-gauge-order** (error, [Kim10](#src-kim10); confirmed).
  Where: Published Central European Journal of Mathematics 8 (2010), p. 642 (PDF p. 10), cocycle action display; also arXiv:0804.1008v1, PDF p. 9.
  Printed: For cocycles with c(sigma\*tau)=c(sigma) sigma(c(tau)), the displayed proposed gauge value is sigma(l inverse)c(sigma)l.
  Correction: For a right torsor with sigma(p)=p c(sigma), changing p to p·l gives l inverse c(sigma) sigma(l). Its inverse-witness form is l c(sigma) sigma(l inverse).
  Reason: The displayed reversed formula need not preserve the stated cocycle law. In S4 with functional composition, let a=(123), l=(234), let C3 act by conjugation by a, and use c(g^j)=a^(-j). The proposed d has d(g^2)=(243), whereas d(g) g(d(g))=(123). The right-torsor formula follows directly by applying sigma to p·l.
  Affects: a stated result.
  Known: No existing correction located in the author page, listed arXiv history or title/DOI correction searches; reversal confirmed in both preprint and published version.
  Verification: Independently read arXiv v1 p. 9 and the published p. 642, including the rendered page. The same reversed gauge formula occurs in both. Direct evaluation of the C3/S4 example gives d(g)=(143), d(g^2)=(243), and d(g)g(d(g))=(123). The corrected right-torsor gauge obeys all nine C3 products in that model and follows from applying sigma to p·l.

- **E101** (misprint, [M99](#src-m99); confirmed).
  Where: §15 discussion before Corollary 15.3, author-copy p. 76.
  Printed: The finiteness argument names the relative Hom scheme without explicitly restricting the displayed Hom notation to dominant maps. Read literally as all morphisms, that scheme also contains constant maps.
  Correction: Use the dominant/nonconstant relative Hom locus throughout the finite-unramified and shrinking argument. The packet’s moduli request and Hom endpoints make this restriction explicit.
  Reason: Constant maps from a proper geometrically connected curve to Y vary with Y. The tangent pullback has negative degree only for nonconstant maps to a genus-at-least-two target; Hurwitz then bounds their degrees.
  Affects: the proof.
  Known: No separate correction of this notation located in the author’s June 2019 comments. This is a contextual qualification in the author copy, not an assertion that the published theorem is false.
  Verification: Reread author-copy p. 76: H_M=Hom_M(X_M,Y_M) is called finite and unramified by the vanishing of sections of the pulled-back tangent bundle and the Hurwitz degree bound, and both arguments apply only to nonconstant maps; the constant maps form a family isomorphic to Y_M. Nonconstant maps form an open and closed subscheme because the degree is locally constant, so restricting to it repairs the argument. Agrees with the earlier review.

- **E103** (misprint, [M95](#src-m95); confirmed).
  Where: §3.9 node condition, author-copy p. 22.
  Printed: The parenthetical bound on the node exponent is strict: e&lt;d.
  Correction: Use 1≤e≤d, with e invertible on the base. The source itself uses the weak inequality in §3.10, author-copy p. 24.
  Reason: For the identity cover of a nodal curve, d=e=1. More generally a totally ramified node may use e=d; the local degree cannot exceed the total degree.
  Affects: a stated result.
  Known: No correction of this parenthetical bound located in the author’s August 2017 comments; the following proof already uses e≤d. Finding is restricted to the author copy read here.
  Verification: Reread author-copy §3.9, p. 22 (the parenthetical says e is necessarily less than d) against §3.10, p. 24, which uses e≤d to verify condition (1); the identity covering of a nodal curve has d=e=1 and is admissible. None of the three August 2017 comments concerns this bound. Agrees with the earlier review.

- **E104** (gap, [M99](#src-m99); confirmed).
  Where: §5, Proposition 5.4, author-copy p. 34, applying Definition 4.3 and Proposition 4.4 of §4, whose standing hypothesis is that the curve has a K-rational point, author-copy pp. 28–31.
  Printed: Section 4 assumes that the proper curve has a K-rational point and uses a degree-one Picard point over K to define the canonical weight-zero section with which Definition 4.3 compares. Proposition 5.4 asserts that the image section of the target curve Y is J-geometric in the sense of Definition 4.3, but §5 assumes no K-point on Y and no K-point of its degree-one Picard scheme.
  Correction: Apply the test for Y after a finite extension K′ over which Y has a point. Restriction to Γ_K′ is injective on H¹ of the weight-zero quotient, so the condition does not depend on K′ and agrees with Definition 4.3 whenever Y has a K-point. Proposition 5.4 holds in this reading, and its use in the proof of Proposition 7.4 compares only with constant sections defined over finite extensions.
  Reason: The proof of Proposition 4.4 uses a section β of the same curve coming from a K-rational point, and the canonical section of Definition 4.3 is built from a Pic¹(K) point; neither exists in general for the target curve of §5. Over K′ both exist, and corestriction after restriction is multiplication by \[K′:K\], which is invertible on these Q_p-vector spaces, so restriction loses nothing.
  Affects: nothing.
  Known: new.
  Verification: Added by this review after reading author-copy pp. 28–34: §4 states the point hypothesis before Definition 4.3, and §5 applies the definition to the target curve without it. The j-geometric-section node now defines the test after a finite extension and asserts the Pic¹(K) characterization only when Pic¹(K) is nonempty.

Already in degree one I=1+aT gives u=1−aT modulo T², whereas the forward horizontal solution has coefficient +a. NC.4 already uses the correct inverse, and the added nonidentity-path test checks it.

- **E-NC4-4** (gap, [Kim09](#src-kim09); confirmed).
  Where: Published §1, first paragraph of the proof of Theorem 1, p.111.
  Printed: The proper-curve reduction chooses an integral rational point outside the base point residue disc without an extra existence hypothesis.
  Correction: Remove a relative finite étale divisor supported away from the chosen special point; it may have degree greater than one. Apply the extending quotient on that auxiliary affine chart.
  Reason: A smooth proper curve can have only one rational special-fibre point, so every integral rational point lies in the same disc. For example y²+y=x⁵+x³+1 over ℤ₂ has smooth genus-two special fibre with only infinity over 𝔽₂: at x=0,1 the right side is 1 and y²+y=0. At infinity the chart v²+u³v=u+u³+u⁶ is smooth. A different closed special-fibre point lifts to a finite étale divisor; NC.4 already allows this repair.
  Affects: the proof.
  Known: new.
  Verification: A smooth proper curve can have only one rational special-fibre point, so every integral rational point lies in the same disc. For example y²+y=x⁵+x³+1 over ℤ₂ has smooth genus-two special fibre with only infinity over 𝔽₂: at x=0,1 the right side is 1 and y²+y=0. At infinity the chart v²+u³v=u+u³+u⁶ is smooth. A different closed special-fibre point lifts to a finite étale divisor; NC.4 already allows this repair.

  Verification: With one generator the first algebra is K\[T\] and the free-group algebra is K\[z,z⁻¹\]; their units differ. The subsequent primitive-generator coproduct and word connection use the tensor algebra, which is the NC.2/NC.4 convention.

- **E-NC6-kim-conjugation-eigenspaces** (error, [Kim09](#src-kim09); confirmed).
  Where: Publ. RIMS 45 (2009), §3, proof of Proposition 2, p.123 (published version).
  Printed: For n odd, the right-hand side of the Euler characteristic formula, the dimension of the (−1)-eigenspace of complex conjugation on the graded piece Z\_{n+1}\\Z_n, is asserted to be d_n/2, by comparison with complex Hodge theory.
  Correction: The value d_n/2 holds when the graded piece is pure of odd weight, which is the compact case. In general the (−1)-eigenspace has dimension (d_n − τ_n)/2, where τ_n is the trace of complex conjugation on the graded piece, computed from its trace t on H₁ by τ_n = (1/n)Σ\_{e\|n} μ(e) t_e^{n/e} (t_e = t for odd e, t_e = m for even e). Either \|t\| &lt; m and τ_n = o(d_n), or t = −m and conjugation acts by (−1)^n; in both cases the sum of the (+1)-eigenspace dimensions still grows like λ^n/n with λ &gt; g, so Proposition 2 survives with this replacement.
  Reason: For X = P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞} over Q, each graded piece is Q_p(n)^{d_n} and complex conjugation acts on Q_p(n) by (−1)^n, so for odd n the (−1)-eigenspace is the whole piece, of dimension d_n, not d_n/2. In the affine case the graded pieces are mixed (the boundary contributes Tate twists of even weight), and the Hodge-symmetry argument applies only to pure odd weight.
  Affects: the proof.
  Known: new; no erratum found.
  Verification: Checked at p.123 of the published PDF: for n odd the (−1)-eigenspace is said to have dimension d_n/2 by comparison with complex Hodge theory, with no distinction between the open and the compact case. For P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞} the graded piece is Q_p(n)^{d_n} and complex conjugation acts on it by (−1)^n, so for odd n the (−1)-eigenspace is the whole piece. The correction was rederived: in the affine case the graded Lie algebra is free on H₁, the character formula for the involution gives τ_n, the compact part of H₁ has trace 0 and the boundary part trace 1 − r (r real boundary points), so t = −m only for g = 0 with every boundary point real; Proposition 2 survives through the (+1)-eigenspaces.

- **E-NC6-kim-h1-notation** (misprint, [Kim09](#src-kim09); rejected).
  Where: Publ. RIMS 45 (2009), §3, proof of Lemma 6 (p.124) and proof of Observation 3 (p.125).
  Printed: The coefficient module surjecting onto the graded piece in H², and the module in the exact sequence with Q_p(1)^{s−1} in the proof of Observation 3, are written as tensor powers of H¹(X̄, Q_p).
  Correction: Read H₁ = H¹(X̄, Q_p)^∨ in both places: the graded pieces are quotients of H₁^{⊗n}, local duality turns H²(G_w, H₁^{⊗n}) into H⁰(G_w, H¹^{⊗n}(1)), and the extension 0 → Q_p(1)^{s−1} → H₁(X) → H₁(X′) → 0 holds for homology (for cohomology the boundary term is a quotient Q_p(−1)^{s−1}).
  Reason: The lower central quotients of the unipotent fundamental group are generated by its abelianisation H₁, and the subsequent local estimate on p.124 uses the invariants of H¹^{⊗n}(1), which is the local dual of H₁^{⊗n}, not of H¹^{⊗n}.
  Affects: nothing.
  Known: new; no erratum found.
  Verification: In the published PDF (sha256 b06562bc…), checked as rendered page images, pp.124–126 print the homology H₁(X̄, Q_p) with a subscript in every place the finding names: the surjection and the injection in the proof of Lemma 6, and the sequence 0 → W → H₁(X̄, Q_p) → V → 0 with W = Q_p(1)^{s−1} and V = H₁(X̄′, Q_p) in Observation 3. The cohomology H¹ appears only where it is meant: the local dual H⁰(G_w, H¹(X̄, Q_p)^{⊗n}(1)), the weight filtration of H¹ and V ≅ H¹(X̄′, Q_p)(1). A plain-text extraction of the PDF loses the distinction between the subscript and the superscript, which is the likely origin of the finding.

- **E-NC6-kim-purity-open** (error, [Kim09](#src-kim09); confirmed).
  Where: Publ. RIMS 45 (2009), §3, argument after Observation 2, p.122.
  Printed: V_n is said to be pure of weight n − 2.
  Correction: This holds when X is proper. For an affine curve, H¹(X̄) is mixed of weights 1 and 2 and V_n has weights in \[n − 2, 2n − 2\]; the argument still works because all weights are at least n − 2 ≥ 1 for n ≥ 3, so W_0E ∩ V_n = 0.
  Reason: Conjecture 2 is stated for any smooth curve; for X = P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞}, V_n = Q_p(1 − n)^{2^n} is pure of weight 2n − 2, not n − 2.
  Affects: the proof.
  Known: new; no erratum found.
  Verification: p.122 says V_n is pure of weight n − 2, while Conjecture 2 (p.121) is stated for any smooth curve. For affine X the weights of H¹ are 1 and 2 and V_n has weights in \[n − 2, 2n − 2\] (for P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞} it is pure of weight 2n − 2). The splitting argument only needs all weights of V_n to be positive, which holds for n ≥ 3, so the conclusion stands.

- **E-NC6-kim-rank-one** (gap, [Kim09](#src-kim09); confirmed).
  Where: Publ. RIMS 45 (2009), §4, pp.127 and 129.
  Printed: Finiteness of integral points is claimed for CM elliptic curves over Q of rank 1 independently of any conjecture, and the dimension of the refined Selmer group of H¹(Ē, Q_p) is said to be 1 by the rank one hypothesis.
  Correction: The computation needs the Bloch–Kato Selmer group of V_pE to have dimension one. Rank one of E(Q) gives this only together with finiteness of Ш(E)\[p^∞\], which is known for instance when the analytic rank is one (Gross–Zagier and Kolyvagin). State the hypothesis as Selmer rank one.
  Reason: The Selmer group H¹_f(G_Q, V_pE) has dimension rank E(Q) + corank Ш(E)\[p^∞\]; without finiteness of the p-part of Ш the dimension can exceed the rank, and then the depth-two dimension count 1 &lt; 2 is not established.
  Affects: a stated result.
  Known: new; no erratum found.
  Verification: p.127 claims finiteness for CM elliptic curves over Q of rank 1 independently of any conjecture, and p.129 sets the dimension of the refined Selmer group of H₁(Ē, Q_p) equal to 1 by the rank one hypothesis. That group is the Bloch–Kato Selmer group of V_pE (the local H¹ vanishes at ℓ ≠ p and H¹_g = H¹_f at p), of dimension rank E(Q) plus the Z_p-corank of Ш(E)\[p^∞\]; finiteness of Ш(E)\[p^∞\] is needed and is not stated.

- **E-NC6-kim-pseudonull-fg** (error, [Kim09](#src-kim09); confirmed).
  Where: Publ. RIMS 45 (2009), §4, proof of Observation 4, p.131 (published version).
  Printed: Pseudo-nullity of I as a Λ-module is said to imply that I is finitely generated over Z_p (with a reference to Greenberg 1978, §2), from which a Frobenius element has only finitely many eigenvalues on I ⊗ Q_p.
  Correction: Pseudo-nullity gives that I ⊗ Q_p is finite-dimensional, equivalently that I modulo its Z_p-torsion is finitely generated over Z_p. This weaker statement is all the weight argument uses, since every Λ-homomorphism from I to a Q_p-vector space kills the torsion.
  Reason: In the CM case with p odd, G\_∞ ≅ Z_p² and Λ ≅ Z_p\[\[T_1, T_2\]\]. The module Λ/(p, T_1) ≅ F_p\[\[T_2\]\] has support of height two, so it is pseudo-null, but it is an infinite-dimensional F_p-vector space and not finitely generated over Z_p. For a finitely generated pseudo-null I, the quotient I′ = I/I\[p^∞\] has p as a nonzerodivisor, so dim I′/pI′ ≤ dim I′ − 1 ≤ 0; hence I′/pI′ is finite and I′ is finitely generated over Z_p by Nakayama's lemma for compact modules.
  Affects: the proof.
  Known: new; no erratum found.
  Verification: Found by the independent review at the locator; the counterexample and the corrected argument are given in the entry.

  Where: Publ. RIMS 45 (2009), §3, proof of Lemma 6, p.124 (published version).

  Correction: cd_p(G_T) = 2 holds for p odd or for a totally imaginary base field. Over Q with p = 2 the real place makes cd_2(G_T) infinite; the surjection still holds with Q_p-coefficients, because H³(G_T, M) ≅ ⊕\_{v real} H³(G_v, M) is killed by 2 for finite 2-primary M, so H³ vanishes after inverting p.
  Reason: Conjecture 1 and Proposition 2 are over F = Q, and the paper puts no restriction on the prime p of good reduction, so p = 2 is allowed. For F = Q and p = 2, H^r(G_T, Z/2) is the cohomology of the real place for every r ≥ 3 and is nonzero (the statement planned in ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4/cohomological-dimension-bound).
  Affects: nothing.
  Known: new; no erratum found.
  Verification: Found by the independent review at the locator.

- **E-NC6-kim-lemma6-open** (error, [Kim09](#src-kim09); confirmed).
  Where: Publ. RIMS 45 (2009), §3, proof of Lemma 6, p.124 (published version).
  Printed: For w not dividing p the weight filtration W_0 ⊂ W_1 ⊂ W_2 is placed on H¹(X̄, Q_p) itself, coming from Raynaud's uniformisation of the Jacobian, with W_0 isomorphic to Gr_2(−1) and so dim Gr_2 ≤ g.
  Correction: For an affine curve the Raynaud filtration lives on H¹ of the compactification X′. On H¹(X̄) the top graded piece also contains the boundary part, a form of Q_p(−1)^{s−1}, so W_0 ≅ Gr_2(−1) and dim Gr_2 ≤ g fail when s ≥ 2. The displayed local bound stays valid with Gr_2 taken on H¹(X̄) (of dimension at most g + s − 1), equivalently with Gr_2 of H¹(X̄′) plus the boundary term n(s − 1)g^{n−1}, and the estimate P(n)g^n of Lemma 6 is unchanged.
  Reason: The Gysin sequence 0 → H¹(X̄′) → H¹(X̄) → ker(Q_p(−1)^{D(F̄)} → Q_p(−1)) → 0 adds s − 1 dimensions of weight 2. For X = P¹ ∖ {0, 1, ∞} (g = 0, s = 3), H¹(X̄) = Q_p(−1)² is pure of weight 2, so Gr_2 has dimension 2 &gt; g and W_0 = 0 is not Gr_2(−1).
  Affects: nothing.
  Known: new; no erratum found.
  Verification: Found by the independent review at the locator.

## Notes for existing Tau Ceti roadmaps

- **ProfiniteArithmetic.** Current main supplies generic ContinuousOut and continuous extension outer actions, absent from the atlas snapshot. The actual anchor is #layer-2-continuous-automorphisms-and-outer-automorphisms. Section 2.3 constructs the outer action but does not identify centre-free extensions with its pullback. Request that generic reconstruction/restriction theorem as ProfiniteArithmetic, Part II and index both contracts before assembly. No upstream file is changed in this job.
- **AlgebraicCurves.** Its current Layer 9 covers arbitrary residue fields and Layer 12 covers scheme/function-field dictionaries; the mixed-characteristic residue-function-field proof must cite these enlarged interfaces.
- **TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge.** Read current main at 070dc2becd74419e76303ede84b465ed4a69461f. B plans coherent cohomology/genus, E abelian varieties/tangent spaces, F the Abel–Jacobi universal property. The NC.2 cohomological bridges are not already their targets; route them to SF.3 and the cohomological suppliers, leaving the proper de Rham bridge explicit. No upstream file was edited.
- **TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicVectorBundles.** Current main uses L0A for module-sheaf monoidal structure and L0B for finite locally free sheaves, tensor/dual and pullback. Updated the snapshot reconciliation; these are imports, never NC.2 targets.
- **tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ReductiveGroups.** NC.3 consumes the existing smooth-unipotent and functor-of-points direction. Needed refinements are explicitly requested: vector central quotients and torsor triviality over affine characteristic-zero coefficient algebras. These are not replanned as a new group-scheme theory.
- **Preserve existing ownership and dependency direction.** NS, its symmetric Hom injection and rank are existing A2/A6 targets, resolving RT-AREA-algebraicgeometry/8. The maintainer should retarget BDMTV/9 to those exact nodes. Generic mixed extensions/heights remain the pending shared Part II; no fabricated stage, second owner or NC.5 foundation is added. Existing ED.6 nodes already own the worked model, arithmetic/rank assembly, precision bounds and rational completeness. NC.5 exports generic height contracts to ED.6; its worked illustration does not import ED.6 as a prerequisite and create a cycle. Source E507 requires an ED.6 corrected exceptional-disc replay.

## Restructuring proposals

These proposals affect the shape of this roadmap or its neighbours; they await the maintainer's decision, and the plan above is written so that it is correct whichever way they are decided. The first proposal recorded with the lemma-level targets (removing NC.6) is superseded by NC.6's own proposal to narrow the layer to its frontier statements.

- **rescope** (AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty; proposed with layer NC.0 and NC.3 lemma-level targets).
  Why: NC.6 is a process handoff, not a mathematical layer, in the reviewed audit.
  Proposal: Remove NC.6 after maintainer acceptance; retain reconstruction in NC.1 and rational-point exports in NC.5, supplying EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.6 directly. Keep section and eventual Chabauty–Kim completeness conjectural. Current NC.6 coverage remains pending acceptance.

- **rescope** (AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty, EtaleHomotopyTypes; proposed with layer NC.0 and NC.3 lemma-level targets).
  Why: The Schmidt–Stix extraction already retains an unaccepted EtaleHomotopyTypes candidate. Its generic foundational targets overlap the raw inputs needed here; its NC.1 centre-free input would create a cycle if used by the NC.0 foundation.
  Proposal: Reconcile and narrow the existing unaccepted Étale homotopy types and pro-spaces candidate into a generic foundational core: import existing pro-category/ordinary homotopy/site/IG.0/IG.1 owners, resolve its G1/G3/G7 closure obligations and supply raw étale pro-spaces, classifying pro-spaces, coefficient detection and elementary-fibration homotopy inputs without any dependency on NC.0 or NC.1. Leave source-qualified anabelian monodromy/orbit results to the downstream anabelian component. This packet alone owns the reserved K(π,1) predicate. Do not create a duplicate IG Part II owner or treat this candidate as a registered supplier stage.

- **extend** (ProfiniteProPGroups; proposed with layer NC.1).
  Why: Current upstream ProfiniteProPGroups has presentations and Demushkin theory but no explicit centre API; this is a generic supplier extension, not a second group-theory construction in NC.1.
  Proposal: ProfiniteProPGroups, Part II: centre-freeness of nonabelian free pro-p groups and of negative-Euler-characteristic pro-p surface groups, plus the open-subgroup criterion transferring this to profinite groups. Reuse all existing Frattini, presentations and cohomological-dimension carriers.

- **extend** (InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups; proposed with layer NC.1).
  Why: M95 §§3.5–3.13 is the source contract. NC.1 uses this generic notion as a supplier and owns only the potentially pre-admissible arithmetic cover system.
  Proposal: InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups, Part II: extend the existing balanced admissible-cover interface to invertible local node/marking indices without assuming invertible total degree; include its log lift and finite normalized fibre products.

- **split** (AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty; proposed with layer NC.1).
  Why: NC.2 has no planned nodes in the parent packet. The request here is for this foundation only, with no NC.1 reconstruction input. The current ProfiniteArithmetic lower-central Lie ring is reused; it does not itself assert a rational Malcev equivalence. Assembly must enforce this split so the stage-level NC.1→NC.2 application ordering cannot create a cycle.
  Proposal: Extract the foundational two-step Malcev/cup-relation interface requested from NC.2 into an earlier independent portion of the same roadmap; NC.1 and the remaining NC.2 then both import it.

- **extend** (ProfiniteCohomology; proposed with layer NC.1).
  Why: The current main explicitly excludes non-discrete coefficients and the spectral sequence. NC.1 requests these general tools from that owner, rather than planning another continuous cohomology theory.
  Proposal: ProfiniteCohomology, Part II: continuous integral and completed coefficient comparison, derived p-power inverse limits and arithmetic Hochschild–Serre, preserving the existing canonical carrier and cup/Kummer maps.

- **extend** (ProfiniteArithmetic; proposed with layer NC.1).
  Why: Reuse current §§2.1–2.3 for Aut, Inn, Out, characteristic-quotient topology and continuous outer actions. Prove the pullback map and its continuous inverse; centre-freeness gives uniqueness. Source: T97 §7A, Lemma 7.1, p. 188; M96 Theorems 7.4 and 10.2, pp. 607 and 626. Proper hyperbolic geometric kernels meet the finiteness/topology hypotheses. The atlas snapshot must index this existing owner and the extension; no new generic group theory is assigned to NC.1.
  Proposal: ProfiniteArithmetic, Part II: for a profinite extension with centre-free topologically finitely generated kernel, identify the extension continuously with Aut(kernel) ×\_{Out(kernel)} base. Restriction identifies continuous isomorphisms over the fixed base with geometric isomorphisms intertwining the outer actions, and descends modulo target-kernel inner automorphisms.

- **rescope** (ReductiveGroupsPartII, AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty; proposed with layer NC.4).
  Why: NC.4 needs the explicit characteristic-zero split-unipotent nonnormal homogeneous quotient and affine unipotent torsor-vanishing refinements requested from current ReductiveGroups layers 3 and 5. They are not distinct Albanese constructions; the existing ReductiveGroupsPartII packet does not supply these exact statements.
  Proposal: Extend Reductive groups, Part II by a foundational split-unipotent homogeneous-space refinement building on current ReductiveGroups layers 3 and 5 and SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.1. It supplies affine representability of U/H and H-torsor vanishing over every affine coefficient algebra, including nonreduced ones. Keep existing reductive-group and Weil-restriction targets unchanged. NC.4 imports that refinement; it owns only admissible periods, Albanese maps, loci and their conditional finiteness. Until the maintainer assigns the refinement, use the current upstream owner stages and the exact requests in this packet.

- **rescope** (AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty; proposed with layer NC.6).
  Why: The stage text of NC.6 combines a process instruction (export the outputs of NC.1–NC.5 to EffectiveDiophantineMethods ED.6) with a mathematical acceptance condition (preserve the section-conjecture and eventual-stabilisation frontiers, keeping motivic hypotheses explicit). The reviewed audit AUDIT-08 classifies the export as process; the earlier checkpoints of this job proposed dropping the stage. The frontier statements, however, are mathematics that no layer of the atlas states: the section map and its injectivity, Grothendieck's section conjecture, Kim's Conjectures 1 and 2 with their conditional bridges and known cases, and Kim's eventual-equality conjecture. This packet plans them and proposes narrowing the stage instead of dropping it.

Add NC.0 → NC.6, NC.2 → NC.6, NC.3 → NC.6 and NC.4 → NC.6, which the prerequisites use.

Two further proposals arise from joining the layers.

- **The cohomological core of NC.3 as an earlier part of the roadmap.** The abstract nonabelian cohomology of NC.3 (the lemma groups from "Continuous cocycles, H¹ and connecting maps" through "Stabilizers, invariant actions and kernel orbit fibres", with the assembled theorems built from them) uses no geometric input, while NC.0 and NC.2 use it. Moving these targets to a first layer, before NC.0, would make the layer order a construction order. Until then they are cited across layers as flagged above.
- **Atlas edges.** The atlas records NC.0 → NC.1, NC.0 → NC.2 → NC.3 → NC.4 → NC.5 and NC.1, NC.5 → NC.6. The targets use NC.3 → NC.0 and NC.3 → NC.2 (the cohomological core), NC.2 → NC.1 (the requested Malcev quotient) and NC.0, NC.2, NC.3, NC.4 → NC.6, and do not use NC.1 → NC.6 or NC.5 → NC.6. The layer graph should follow the targets; with the core moved as proposed above, it has no cycle.

- `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.1/arithmetic-exact-sequence`: Exact full arithmetic sequence for geometrically connected curves, with outer G_K action.
- `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.1/decomposition-inertia`: Ordinary decomposition/inertia quotient and geometric-lift conventions.
- `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.1/tame-and-prime-to-p`: Tame and prime-to-p quotients retain their stated residue/ramification hypotheses.
- `CrystallineCohomology:CR.5:log-algebra/log-structure`: Sheaf log structure on X_et; no finite chart assumptions without a separate fineness hypothesis.
- `CrystallineCohomology:CR.5:log-algebra/log-chart`: Actual monoid chart and associated log structure; chart is not necessarily characteristic stalk.
- `CrystallineCohomology:CR.5:log-algebra/kummer-morphism`: Kummer maps are injective with power-surjectivity; invertible torsion orders are required for Kummer étale.
- `NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties:R11.3/raynaud-extension-comparison`: Formal identity Raynaud extension for semistable abelian varieties over complete DVRs.
- `NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties:R11.3/rigid-uniformisation`: Semiabelian Raynaud extension modulo a lattice, with integral polarized valuation pairing.
- `NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties:R11.4/integral-monodromy-pairing`: Integral monodromy pairing without integral unimodularity.
- `NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties:R11.2/component-group`: Finite étale geometric component group; rational points are Galois invariants.
- `FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.1/tate-generic-fibre-theorem`: Over complete perfect-residue DVRs, homomorphisms of p-divisible groups equal G_K-equivariant Tate-module homomorphisms.
- `JacobianChallengePartII:JC0/picard-torsors`: Pic^d is an fppf Pic^0 torsor and may have no field point.
- `JacobianChallengePartII:JC4/actual-to-relative-obstruction`: Actual-to-relative Picard boundary in cohomological Brauer groups; no automatic actual line bundle.
- `AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A4/etale-tate-module`: Integral Tate sheaf with twist-valued Weil pairing, not a Z_ℓ-valued pairing.
- `AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A6/hom-to-tate-module-homs-is-injective`: Hom of abelian varieties injects into integral Tate-module Hom; this does not give Hom surjectivity.
- `FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.4/profinite-reciprocity`: Function-field idele class profinite completion is the abelian Galois group, with arithmetic Frobenius degree normalization.
- `FunctionFieldArithmetic:FA.4/local-abelian-existence`: Equal-characteristic local abelian existence; finite Artin maps use the class-field supplier.

- `InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.3/general-riemann-existence`: Finite étale schemes on a complex finite-type scheme correspond to finite topological covers; curves extend their covers by normalization at punctures.

Tate/H^1 is supplied by SF.3, good-reduction linear comparison by R06.5, and the proper de Rham Abel–Jacobi bridge is recorded separately. The current JacobianChallenge B–F layers do not state the cohomological or Kummer comparison.
- **Accepted AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty parent, NC.3** (`equivariant-topological-torsors`): The parent supplies abstract equivariant torsors for rational point realizations. Its abstract carriers do not establish scheme representability, fpqc descent or nonlinear crystalline comparison.

## Paper routing

The paper of Balakrishnan, Dogra, Müller, Tuitman and Vonk on the split Cartan curve of level 13 was routed item by item to this roadmap. Every item routed to NC.2 or NC.5 is accounted for by a target or an import; the worked computation itself belongs to EffectiveDiophantineMethods ED.6.

## Pinned library declarations

The 222 declarations below are cited by the targets above. Each was read at Mathlib `082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174` or Tau Ceti `f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369`, and provides what is stated, with its own hypotheses.

- `AddGroup.FG` (Mathlib, class, `Mathlib/GroupTheory/Finiteness.lean`): Finitely generated additive groups; the hypothesis under which an abelian group has no nonzero divisible element.
- `AlgHom.comp` (Mathlib, def, `Mathlib/Algebra/Algebra/Hom.lean`): Composition of actual algebra homomorphisms, including maps from coordinate algebras to coefficient rings.
- `AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyNoetherian` (Mathlib, class, `Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Noetherian.lean`): Local noetherianity via noetherian affine coordinate rings.

## The suggested Lean file

The [suggested file](../suggested/AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty.lean) has one import block, one standard note and one section per layer, with the cohomological core of NC.3 first because NC.0, NC.2 and the geometric part of NC.3 use it. Each layer keeps the namespace its plan gives to its declarations: `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology` for the cohomological core and `TauCeti.EtaleKPiOne` for the K(π,1) regressions; `TauCetiRoadmap.AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty.NC0`, `.NC2` and `.NC5` for the native carriers of NC.0, NC.2 and NC.5; `TauCeti.Anabelian` for NC.1 and NC.6; `TauCeti.NonabelianCohomology.NC3` for the geometric part of NC.3; and `TauCeti.ChabautyKim` for NC.4. The geometric part of NC.3 uses the cocycles, classes, coefficient maps and abelian comparison of the core directly; there is one carrier of nonabelian H¹ in the file.

The file elaborates against Mathlib `082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174` and Tau Ceti `f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369` with no errors and `sorry` as its only warning. It states what the pinned libraries can express: the definitions with their API and unit tests as `example`s, and the theorems whose carriers exist. Statements whose carriers are not at the pins (étale fundamental groups of schemes, unipotent completions, period rings, Selmer varieties, Galois cohomology of number fields) are targets of this document only; the closing comment of the file lists the 261 proposed names of the 100 targets concerned. Sixty-four definitions and instances of the file still have admitted bodies (most in the cohomological core, for example the coefficient map on H¹, the abelian comparison and the twisting equivalence); a roadmap package that keeps any of them gives it a real body.
